jobs.title: SUDAN - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - KHARTOUM
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date : 15/01/2027**
**Duration of the mission : 12 months**
**Location : KHARTOUM**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SI has been present in Sudan for a long time, untill expulsion in 2009 and subsequent reopening in the early 2010s.

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.

Geneina base scaled up in 2024 and 2025 to deliver life-safing and recovery humanitarian assistance through WASH, FSL and Shelter interventions.

SI opened an office in Zalingei, Central Darfur in November 2024, North Darfur in 2024/5 and in Ed Daein and West Kordofan in 2026.

Today, thanks to the support of SIDA, SHF, CDCS, ECHO and UNDP, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, East Darfur, North Darfur, West Kordofan, Khartoum and Jazeera States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors. SI is also in the process of opening up activities in Blue Nile State.

Across the Darfurs and in West Kordofan, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH -from 1st line to 2nd line & beyond- with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, networks, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.

In West Darfur, SI remains one of the main WASH actors and has developped a strong technical and access capacity through the rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.

In Central Darfur, the activities mostly focus on WASH and FSL. SI also has an Emergency Response Team based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA).

In the Eastern part of the country, SI is present with Wash and FSL activities in Khartoum and Jazeera, under ECHO, CDCS, SHF and US funds. Activities in Blue Nile are being launched by the end of 2026.

Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, including 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.

Mission size around 45 international staff and 190 National staff across different bases

Base Size (5 International staff and 22 National across Khartoum and Jazira Base)

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Field Coordinator oversees the development of Solidarites International's (SI) presence and response in their area of intervention, in line with the Country Strategy and the organisation's mandate.

Delegated by the Country Director, they are SI's representative in the area to aid workers, local administrative, military and political authorities, civil society and the media.

They are responsible for ensuring the security of SI teams and assets in their area, as well as compliance with the organisation's ethical framework and values.

**The main challenges:**

\- Bureaucratic impediments in East Sudan are significant and have the potential to delay interventions and activities. A good communication style and patience are necessary for maintaining relationships and solving problems is high.

\- Coordination is moving to Khartoum in January 2027, the integration of Project and Coordination remains to be implemented.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\- Consolidating 2027 strategy based on needs and funding and ensuring an appropriate structure

\- Consolidation of opening of Blue Nile activities and base

**Security constraints:**

Both states are at level 2-3 and are safe. Social life is more active in Khartoum, but staff can move freely in both states.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3-4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Security and access management
2. Rapid need Assesement
3. Strong negociations skills
4. Conflict sensitivy skills

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Work under pressure
2. Adaptability
3. Strong initiative capacities and solution-finding attitude

**LANGUAGES**

1. Fluent English
2. Arabic would be an advantage
3. French would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Khartoum is recovering and life is returning to normal, with a lot of restaurants and shops. There are also a lot of internationals, both humanitarians and others, and there is opporunity to socialize. The international hotels are reopening allowing for increase in variety of activities that can be done.

jobs.title: Director, People Development- CRRD
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

**The Director, People Development is responsible for planning and implementing a variety of people development initiatives for the IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department. Partnering closely with the Global Learning & Development Team and P&C Partners across CRRD, the Director, People Development, will plan and facilitate workshops, peer learning groups, facilitate talent review processes, and support other talent management and learning efforts across CRRD. CRRD people development activities must build capability and competency to achieve CRRD's strategic action plans, leadership diversity targets, and the overall development, retention, and improved internal promotion rates of top talent across CRRD.**

**Duties/Responsibilities:**

- Serve as a member of CRRD People & Culture leadership team and contribute to its strategy development and establishment of L&D priorities connected to IRCs Strategy 100 and Delivery Letter goals.
- Build and maintain trusted partnerships with senior CRRD leaders, regional directors, and country directors to ensure sustained engagement and measurable adoption of people development programs across CRRD.
- Serve as the primary voice of CRRD within the Global Learning & Development team by participating in strategy and planning sessions to ensure globally implemented programming reflects the needs, contexts, and constraints of field-based staff and leaders.
- Translate CRRD's strategic priorities — including Strategy 100, leadership diversity targets, and retention goals — into scalable learning and talent development plans, providing guidance on how programs should be adapted to varying operational contexts across a complex, globally distributed humanitarian operation.
- Partner with CRRD P&C Partners to design and deliver new leader integration and country director onboarding experiences that accelerate effectiveness and cultural alignment.
- Contextualize, communicate and drive org-wide learning and development initiatives across CRRD.
- Design and implement people development programs — including, but not limited to, talent review, succession planning, manager capability building, and P&C capacity strengthening — that equip, engage, and retain CRRD staff, managers and leaders.
- Build CRRD's talent movement and capability-building infrastructure — including workforce planning and succession readiness pipelines.
- Maintain and deliver a strategic roadmap of people development initiatives in CRRD while also remaining agile and able to deliver against last-minute and unexpected needs that may arise.
- Identify and champion the responsible use of AI tools and technologies to enhance talent development and learning and development work — improving the personalization, efficiency, and scalability of programs across CRRD's globally distributed teams — in alignment with IRC's approved AI tools and governance standards.
- Establish and track key metrics to evaluate program effectiveness and report progress to CRRD and P&C leadership.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to**: Dual reporting to Senior Director, CRRD People & Culture and Director, Global Learning and Development
**Position directly supervises**: N/A

**Key Internal Relationships**:

- Collaborate with colleagues across the People & Culture function including all CRRD Regional P&C Directors, Gender Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (GEDI), HR Operations, Compensation & Benefits, Global Learning and Development and others to achieve meaningful impact.
- CRRD Leadership and Country People and Culture teams.

**Qualifications:**

- Minimum 8–10 years of progressive experience in learning & development, talent management, or organizational development.
- Demonstrated experience designing and implementing people development programs across a complex, matrixed organization.
- Proven ability to design and facilitate leadership and manager development programs, talent reviews, and succession planning processes.
- Experience conducting learning needs assessments and translating findings into targeted, scalable development solutions.
- Proficiency in tracking and reporting on L&D metrics and using data to evaluate and iterate program effectiveness.
- Familiarity with instructional design methodologies and adult learning principles.
- Exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills, with demonstrated ability to partner effectively with senior leaders and stakeholders across functions and geographies.
- Strong in-person and virtual facilitation skills, with experience leading workshops, peer learning groups, and leadership programs across diverse, multicultural audiences.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and competing priorities, balancing a strategic roadmap with agile responsiveness to emerging needs.
- Deep understanding of the operational realities of field-based and humanitarian contexts, with the ability to design programs that are relevant and accessible across limited resource environments.
- Ability to work across multiple time zones and with globally distributed teams; willingness to travel internationally as needed.
- Some experience applying AI tools and technologies to talent development work — such as learning content design, program personalization, or talent/workforce analytics — preferred.
- English fluency. Proficiency in an additional core IRC language (French, Arabic, Spanish) strongly preferred.

**Compensation:** (GBP 65,785 - GBP 73,095). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Coordinador/a de Proyecto Tránsito de Esperanza
jobs.description:
La organización Plan International es una organización humanitaria y de desarrollo independiente que promueve los derechos de los niños y la igualdad de las niñas.

Creemos en el poder y el potencial de cada niño. Pero esto a menudo se ve reprimido por la pobreza, la violencia, la exclusión y la discriminación. Y son las niñas las más afectadas.

Trabajando junto con los niños, los jóvenes, nuestros partidarios y socios, luchamos por un mundo justo, abordando las causas profundas de los desafíos que enfrentan las niñas y todos los niños vulnerables.

Apoyamos los derechos de los niños desde su nacimiento hasta que llegan a la edad adulta. Y permitimos que los niños se preparen para las crisis y la adversidad y respondan a ellas. Impulsamos cambios en la práctica y las políticas a nivel local, nacional y global utilizando nuestro alcance, experiencia y conocimiento.

Hemos estado construyendo alianzas poderosas para los niños durante más de 85 años y ahora estamos activos en más de 80 países.

Plan International es una organización de desarrollo y respuesta humanitaria cuya misión se fundamenta en la defensa de los derechos de la niñez y el alcance de una igualdad sustantiva para las niñas. En México, nuestra labor es vital para abordar los retos de protección en contextos de movilidad humana y vulnerabilidad social. Operamos n la Ciudad de México, Tapachula, Chiapas y Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, donde nuestros equipos trabajan para atender las necesidades directas de personas en contexto de movilidad humana y sobrevivientes de violencia (retornadas, refugiadas, solicitantes de asilo y comunidades desplazadas).

Nuestro modelo se distingue por un enfoque transformador de género. No solo buscamos satisfacer necesidades inmediatas, sino garantizar el ejercicio pleno de los derechos de niñas y adolescentes, fomentando su liderazgo y participación activa en la toma de decisiones. Trabajamos para erradicar todas las formas de violencia basada en género —incluyendo la violencia sexual y el acoso—, desafiando las normas sociales y estructuras de poder que perpetúan la desigualdad. El objetivo es crear entornos seguros y equitativos para ellas, sus familias y sus personas cuidadoras, quienes son pilares esenciales en el sistema de protección integral.

Bajo una estricta Política de Salvaguarda, Plan International México garantiza que cada intervención y cada miembro de nuestro personal actúe bajo los más altos estándares de protección a la infancia. Promovemos el respeto absoluto a la dignidad humana, asegurando la no discriminación por identidad de género, edad, discapacidad, origen o cualquier otra condición. Nos enfocamos en eliminar las barreras estructurales que impiden que niñas, niños y adolescentes ejerzan sus derechos en condiciones de equidad e inclusión.

En Plan International México, transformamos la asistencia humanitaria en una oportunidad para construir un futuro donde la dignidad y los derechos de la niñez sean la prioridad en cada rincón del país.

## PROPÓSITO DEL PUESTO

Liderar la coordinación técnica, programática, financiera y operativa del proyecto, asegurando el cumplimiento de los objetivos, resultados, presupuesto, cronograma, estándares de calidad y compromisos establecidos con donantes, socios y participantes. La persona titular será responsable de coordinar la implementación del proyecto a lo largo de todo el ciclo de gestión de proyectos, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales de Plan International, las condiciones contractuales de los donantes, los principios de igualdad de género, inclusión, protección infantil, salvaguarda y rendición de cuentas. Asimismo, liderará al equipo del proyecto, coordinará con socios, comunidades e instituciones clave, supervisará la ejecución presupuestaria y promoverá la generación de resultados sostenibles e impactos positivos para niñas, niños, adolescentes, jóvenes y comunidades participantes.

## RESPONSABILIDADES PRINCIPALES

Esta persona será responsable de:

1. Planificar, coordinar y supervisar la ejecución integral del proyecto para asegurar el cumplimiento de los objetivos, resultados, cronograma, presupuesto y estándares de calidad establecidos.
2. Dirigir la implementación técnica del proyecto, asegurando la calidad programática, la aplicación de metodologías institucionales y la articulación efectiva entre los diferentes actores involucrados.
3. Adaptar metodologías, herramientas, materiales y estrategias de implementación a las características, necesidades, riesgos y contextos específicos de las poblaciones participantes y territorios de intervención.
4. Supervisar la ejecución financiera y administrativa del proyecto para garantizar el uso eficiente de los recursos y el cumplimiento de las políticas y procedimientos institucionales.
5. Fortalecer y gestionar las relaciones con donantes, instituciones, organizaciones socias y actores estratégicos para facilitar el logro de los resultados del proyecto.
6. Asegurar el seguimiento sistemático del desempeño del proyecto mediante procesos de monitoreo, evaluación, aprendizaje y rendición de cuentas basados en evidencia.
7. Liderar, acompañar y fortalecer al equipo del proyecto promoviendo una cultura de desempeño, colaboración, bienestar y mejora continua.
8. Asegurar la disponibilidad de los recursos, materiales y condiciones operativas necesarias para la implementación de las actividades del proyecto.
9. Promover entornos seguros para ejecutar las actividades programáticas, mediante la aplicación de protocolos de seguridad, la identificación de riesgos y la implementación de medidas de mitigación.
10. Promover la integración efectiva de las políticas de Salvaguarda, Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PSEAH) e Igualdad e Inclusión de Género en todas las actividades bajo su responsabilidad.

## EXPERIENCIA TÉCNICA, CONOCIMIENTOS Y HABILIDADES

**Calificaciones y experiencia**

- Licenciatura en ciencias sociales, gestión de proyectos, desarrollo o disciplinas afines.
- Experiencia mínima de cinco años en gestión o coordinación de proyectos.
- Experiencia en administración de presupuestos y cumplimiento de donantes.
- Experiencia en la articulación interinstitucional con instancias de gobierno relacionadas con la protección de la niñez.
- Experiencia en coordinación de equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Experiencia en proyectos humanitarios, protección infantil, género, educación o desarrollo comunitario en México.

**Competencias digitales y tecnológicas**

- Dominio de Word, Excel, PowerPoint y plataformas colaborativas como Teams y SharePoint.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas y sistemas de gestión de proyectos.
- Capacidad para registrar, sistematizar y analizar información sensible en plataformas digitales, garantizando seguridad y confidencialidad de datos.
- Familiaridad con protocolos de protección de datos y ciberseguridad en contextos humanitarios.

**Habilidades específicas al puesto**

- Liderazgo de equipos.
- Planificación estratégica y operativa.
- Comunicación y negociación.
- Coordinación interinstitucional.
- Gestión de riesgos y resolución de problemas.
- Análisis y toma de decisiones.
- Facilitación y representación institucional.
- Elaboración de informes técnicos y financieros.

**Otros requisitos**

- Compromiso con la igualdad de género y respeto a la diversidad sexual.
- Sensibilidad y empatía activa hacia personas migrantes y retornadas.
- Vocación de servicio humanitario y comprensión de desigualdades estructurales.
- Compromiso ético para el trabajo directo con niñas, niños, jóvenes y mujeres.
- Disposición de residir en la ciudad de implementación del proyecto.

**Comportamientos de liderazgo**

- Promueve los derechos de la niñez, juventud y mujeres y su participación en espacios de incidencia.
- Asume el compromiso de cero tolerancia al abuso infantil y cumple el Código de Conducta.
- Promueve la política de salvaguardia de la niñez y de igualdad de género.
- Se comunica de forma clara y eficaz.
- Actúa como agente de cambio.

**Ubicación: CDMX**

**Tipo de rol: Personal Tecnico de Coordinación**

**Informes a: Representante de Pais**

**Fecha de cierre: 10 de noviembre 2026**

La igualdad, la diversidad y la inclusión están en el centro de todo lo que Plan International representa.

Queremos que Plan International refleje la diversidad de las comunidades con las que trabajamos, ofreciendo igualdad de oportunidades a todos sin importar edad, discapacidad, reasignación de género, matrimonio y unión civil, embarazo y maternidad, raza, religión o creencia, sexo u orientación sexual.

Plan International se basa en una cultura de inclusión y nos esforzamos por crear un ambiente de trabajo que garantice que cada equipo, en cada oficina, en cada país, sea rico en personas, pensamientos e ideas diversas.

Fomentamos una cultura organizacional que abraza nuestro compromiso con la justicia racial, la igualdad de género, los derechos de las niñas y la inclusión.

Plan International cree que en un mundo donde los niños enfrentan tantas amenazas de daño, es nuestro deber garantizar que nosotros, como organización, hagamos todo lo posible para mantener a los niños seguros. Esto significa que tenemos responsabilidades particulares hacia los niños con los que entramos en contacto y no debemos contribuir de ninguna manera a dañar o poner a los niños en riesgo.

Se llevarán a cabo una serie de controles previos al empleo de conformidad con la política de Protección de niños y jóvenes de Plan International. Plan International también participa en el Programa de divulgación de mala conducta entre agencias. De acuerdo con este esquema, solicitaremos información a los empleadores anteriores de los solicitantes sobre cualquier hallazgo de explotación sexual, abuso sexual y/o acoso sexual durante el empleo, o incidentes bajo investigación cuando el solicitante dejó el empleo.

Al enviar una solicitud, el solicitante de empleo confirma que comprende estos procedimientos de contratación.

Tenga en cuenta que Plan International nunca enviará correos electrónicos no solicitados solicitando pagos a los candidatos.

jobs.title: Event Management Services for Financing Decent Work in Fragile Economies Event
jobs.description:
**Event Management Services for Financing Decent Work in Fragile Economies Event**

**In Baghdad, Iraq 30 November 20261**

## Background and rationale:

The International Labour Organization project named “The Promotion of the Development of SMEs” (IRQ/23/05/DEU), funded by KfW on behalf of the German Federal Government, has established Iraq’s first dedicated SME credit-guarantee architecture — the Empowerment Guarantee Fund (EGF), operated by the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees (ICBG) under the regulatory oversight of the Central Bank of Iraq. Working through participating financial institutions, the initiative was designed to shift the banking sector’s risk calculus toward small and medium enterprises and to expand access to formal finance under fragile-market conditions. The initiative also works in complementarity with other German (BMZ)-supported efforts in Iraq: the International Organization for Migration (IOM) refers eligible enterprises — including among returnee and displacement-affected communities — to the guarantee facility, connecting vulnerable entrepreneurs to the formal finance the fund unlocks.

Following an initial pilot phase, the project is now moving to full operational launch across all governorates of Iraq. This transition — from pilot to national scale — is a significant institutional milestone. It is also an opportunity to position the initiative where it belongs: not as a stand-alone SME-finance project, but as a practical, working demonstration of the Global Coalition for Social Justice, contributing directly to its thematic area on expanding decent work and sustainable enterprises.

**Conditions that must be met in the hall:**

1. The halls should have enough space for sitting including registration table at the entrance, per each day
2. The hall should have easy access to a minimum of 2 toilets
3. The hotel should have full considerations for disability access
4. The Hall should be sufficiently bright with good light and air conditions.

1. The hotel shall arrange for fully functional electronic and audio-visual equipment and workshop materials (such as banners and/ or flags banners, data shows, wireless microphones, audio systems, teleconference equipment, etc.)
2. Flipcharts with stands, whiteboard with paper, and markers
3. Meeting signage includes company logo to guide your guests.
4. 5 stars hotel and they must be approved by UNDSS.
5. Room on ground floor or higher (not basement floor) **Meeting room picture required to be attached**
6. Free Wi-Fi internet connection in the training room.
7. Pens and notepads per participants.

### Coordination

The service provider will liaise and report Gashaw Shareef at shareef@ilo.org copying Miran Bakragha at bakragha@ilo.org and Marina Rai at marina@ilo.org

### Application

- Interested applicants are requested to submit a complete quotation including price form and priced BOQ as per instructions in the tender
- All applications should be done through the dedicated platform-JAGGAER linked to the UNGM
- Quotation should remain valid for 90 days after the application deadline

### Payment

- If the contract to be issued in the local currency, then the ILO will only consider the UN operations exchange rate from USD to the meant currency
- According to the ILO policy, the payments of services are performed 30 days after receipt of service to the satisfaction of the ILO.
- The payment schedule will consist of a single payment, issued after the completion of the service and upon receipt of the invoice and required documents from the supplier, in line with ILO's satisfaction with the service.
- Means of payment: the payment will be paid via wire transfer to the designated bank account of the supplier.

### Evaluation Criteria

- The ILO will consider the Technically compliant/Cost effective quotation, with preference given to experience with UN agencies (preferably the ILO), companies which are registered in Iraq and the KRI, physical exitance on the ground in Iraq and preferably in Baghdad, and experience in managing events and logistics inside Iraq

### Important Notes:

The supplier will be billed to ILO based on the actual number of participants and service ONLY. And up to the acceptance of the ILO team.

### Participants list:

To be provided by the ILO upon awarding the contract.

jobs.title: ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR, HUB ACCOUNTING
jobs.description:
## ***JOB SUMMARY***

Manages across a regional Hub the development, implementation, and maintenance of one or more accounting systems and core accounting processes (e.g., journal entries, general ledger, accounts receivable, accounts payable, revenue reconciliation, and cash flows) in accordance with GAAP policies and procedures. Designs and improves operational procedures and processes to meet financial accounting standards and improve efficiency. Ensures integration of accounting data into systems and supports the objectives of financial analysts through accurate compilation, analysis, and reporting of accounting and revenue data. Participates in annual audits and special projects and may work with external consultants or auditors to provide required information and ensure proper recordkeeping. Selects, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the function. Reports to the Senior Director, Financial and Operational Support.

***RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES***
**Complexity & Problem Solving:**

- Provides operational leadership to Hub accounting staff and supports coordination with country teams across a geographic Hub.
- Assigns and reviews the work of country office accounting teams, providing guidance and support as needed.
- Monitors and improves the monthly close process by analyzing performance and implementing more efficient procedures and use of available resources.
- Serves as Hub point of contact for audit requests and supports timely provision of required documentation.
- Ensures country office accounting business practices are adequate, documented, and compliant with internal and external requirements.
- Conducts live and virtual trainings on accounting systems and processes and provides mentoring to staff as needed.
- Meets with country office staff to understand how business processes are performed and identifies problems, challenges, and improvement opportunities.
- Coordinates with Corporate Accounting to ensure trial balances are updated for local statutory audits.
- Facilitates timely month-end close and resolution of issues prior to general ledger uploads.
- Ensures financial documentation is filed and readily available per country and organizational requirements.
- Ensures internal system guidelines (e.g., GFAS, DPA, Costpoint, banking portal processes) are followed and aligned; provides training and supports uptake of the TM1 budgeting system as applicable.
- Coordinates closeout reconciliation of projects and clearing of outstanding issues before system close.

**Discretion & Impact:**

- Exercises judgment within established accounting policies, procedures, and management guidance to resolve moderately complex discrepancies involving data, analyses, and processes within assigned portfolios.
- Makes decisions that impact the team’s performance and the successful completion of operational initiatives (e.g., monthly close timelines, audit request responsiveness, and documentation readiness).
- Identifies issues that require escalation and coordinates resolution with appropriate stakeholders to protect accuracy and compliance.
- Protects confidential information and ensures appropriate handling and recordkeeping to support auditability and internal control expectations.

**Collaboration & Interaction:**

- Collaborates with Corporate Accounting and other finance stakeholders to ensure alignment on close, statutory audit support, and accounting data requirements.
- Works with internal and external auditors and/or consultants to provide required information and support audit processes as needed.
- Builds cooperation across country office teams by explaining accounting requirements, providing practical guidance, and supporting consistent adoption of processes.
- Uses strong communication, diplomacy, and negotiation skills to coordinate resolution of issues and drive timely completion of deliverables.

**Management & Supervision:**

- Provides direct supervision to Hub accounting staff (skilled individual contributors) and oversees team activities to ensure schedules are met and objectives align with broader departmental goals.
- Motivates, mentors, and manages individuals and groups from diverse backgrounds and expertise to support high-quality, timely work delivery.
- Selects, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the function.
- Works under direction with latitude for independent action on routine work; receives general guidance with periodic review for new work or special assignments.
- Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team’s multifaceted and evolving responsibilities.

## ***QUALIFICATIONS***

**Knowledge & Skills:**

- Strong knowledge of GAAP practices and reporting guidelines.
- Experience with automated financial reporting and government accounting practices, including CAS and FAR systems.
- Knowledge of laws and regulations impacting internal accounting and management controls.
- Strong organizational, supervisory, leadership, and managerial skills.
- Ability to provide guidance to teams, exchange information, and collaborate with colleagues and peers within and outside the organization.
- Excellent communication, diplomatic, and negotiation skills.
- Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s Degree or international equivalent.
- Minimum of 8+ years related work experience, including 3 years in line management and 3 years working at the corporate or organizational level.
- Past experience managing a financial accounting department is required.
- Fluent English (read/write/speak).

**Certifications:**

- Professional accounting certification (e.g., CPA/ACCA or international equivalent) preferred, based on hub/country operating needs.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Experience working in a Non-governmental organization (NGO) preferred.
- Experience working with an international organization preferred.

## ***TRAVEL***

- Less than 10%

***TYPICAL PHYSICAL DEMANDS***

- Typical office environment. Constantly uses a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.

***TECHNOLOGY***

- Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

This job posting summarizes the main duties of the job. It neither prescribes nor restricts the exact tasks that may be assigned to carry out these duties. This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time.

jobs.title: Country Director, Yemen
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than twenty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

The IRC launched an emergency health response in Yemen in 2012. Since then, and despite continued instability and conflict, the IRC has extended its presence throughout the country, implementing a diverse, integrated program of health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and cash programs. These programs prioritize local partnerships with both public institutions and civil society, and span emergency response, humanitarian, and recovery modalities, while serving vulnerable Yemenis including IDPs and returnees, migrants and refugees, women, children, and youth.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director (CD) sets the strategic direction, leads all programs, emergency response, financial and operational matters, and oversees humanitarian access and the adherence to and application of security measures, as well as external relationships and partnerships in Yemen. As lead of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the CD ensures accountability of the SMT for the overall leadership and supervisory management of approximately 120 IRC staff and more than 400 incentive workers, programming, and operations, including program quality and accountability, stewardship of resources, staff safety and security, performance management, and external representation, for which the CD remains accountable.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary, demonstrated leadership abilities who deploys strong communication and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong contextual analytical skills and an ability to translate the impact of geopolitical developments and rapidly changing humanitarian conditions into operational priorities and effective responses. They will build a network of partnerships, diversify program resources, and ensure organizational readiness to respond to emerging and escalating emergencies while maintaining continuity of critical humanitarian services. They will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design, and deliver responsive, high-quality humanitarian, emergency response, early recovery, and development programs; ensuring the efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance, and focused, timely reporting; and overseeing financial management and compliance systems.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Lead the country program by maintaining open and professional relations with colleagues, promoting a strong team spirit, and providing guidance, oversight, and resources to enable staff to perform successfully.
- Lead strategic representation and positioning with national and local authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private), European Union; UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups. Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Play a leadership role in efforts to improve humanitarian response coordination in Yemen
- Provide leadership for strong, mutually beneficial, and effective partnerships with Yemeni organizations.
- Seek out and pursue respectful and safe opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Yemen, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.
- Lead country program collaboration with colleagues in the IRC’s MENAU region to deliver regional programming and advocacy.
- Ensure leadership and management processes enable the IRC to effectively adapt to contextual changes and fully leverage opportunities to expand humanitarian access and assistance.
- Collaborate closely with regional leadership and neighboring country programs to address cross-border and regional issues coherently and effectively.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Growth***

- Set the strategic vision and direction of the country program is aligned with IRC’s strategy to serve more people with the most responsive and highest quality programming possible and secure the resources necessary to do so.
- Ensure the strategy action plan is of quality, implemented and guides decision making, to achieve IRC’s ambitions in Yemen and contribute to IRC’s strategic objectives globally.
- Ensure program quality through consistent use throughout the country program of rigorous assessment, design, and proposal development and review processes; comprehensive monitoring & evaluation, accountability and learning systems; staff development investments; and partner organization capacity strengthening.
- Actively seek out and pursue opportunities to expand, in line with the IRC’s mission, humanitarian, resilience and development programming in Yemen, in terms of populations and areas served.
- Develop a deep understanding of the geopolitical landscape and remain current on context analysis and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure timely submission of competitive, responsive, and high-quality proposals, and support colleagues in negotiations with donors.
- Lead implementation of IRC’s objective of expanding partnerships with Yemeni civil society organizations, and ensuring strong collaborative, principled partnerships that deliver effective and efficient program outcomes.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to changing contexts.
- Ensure the SMT delivers the leadership, management structures, staffing skills and approaches, and operational systems required to ensure a coherent “one IRC” approach to achieve Yemen and regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities for appropriate expansion and growth of programs, supported by the acquisition and investment of human resources.

***Emergency Response Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall strategic and operational emergency response readiness and action for the country program.
- Lead Country Context Analysis, Emergency Response Planning and Strategy Development as well as In-Country Emergency Response Teams
- Ensure the country program maintains robust emergency preparedness and response capacity, including crisis management structures, clear decision-making protocols, and surge readiness to enable rapid operational scale-up or adaptation in volatile contexts.
- Lead and oversee the management timely, well-coordinated, and principled responses to emergencies, including conflict escalation, displacements, critical incidents, and program disruptions.
- Engage with Regional and Global Emergency Response Teams prior to, during and post emergency response, in line with organizational Emergency Guidelines.
- Represent IRC with peer organizations, and other emergency response agencies operating in Yemen.
- Ensure coordinated emergency response in the event of cross-border/regional emergencies.

***Safety and Security Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Lead and oversee the management of all security risks and incidents, ensure timely, well-coordinated, and ensure primacy of the wellbeing and security of our clients, staff and partners. Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including training and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation, and contingency plans current and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety and Security Director on safety and security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.
- Liaise with the regional office, with peer agencies and use the tools and information portals available to keep abreast of all security-related matters; In case of necessity, ensure adequate roll-out of emergency procedures.

***Staff Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives and providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide direct oversight and guidance to multi-disciplinary teams across cross-cultural settings, ensuring performance excellence and alignment with strategic objectives.
- Effectively manage staff across various functions and locations, including setting clear expectations, performance monitoring, and accountability frameworks.
- Lead sensitive and complex staff-related conversations (e.g., performance issues, conflict resolution) with professionalism, empathy, and respect.
- Mentor and coach high-potential staff to support career progression and leadership development within the organization.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing across teams and departments.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to deliver compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, especially in the areas of People and Culture, finance, and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Yemen country program’s financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for grant funds and discretionary funds.
- Ensure a country-wide culture of safeguarding, grounded in accountability, transparency, and survivor-centered response. Provide strategic leadership to mainstream safeguarding across all country program operations and partnerships, in line with IRC’s Safeguarding Policy.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Regional Vice President - MENAU

**Position directly Supervises:** A senior management team responsible for Programs, Operations, Finance, People and Culture, Field Management, and Safety & Security and Compliance and Risk Management.

**Key Internal Contacts:** Country Program: All staff, Region: MENAU Regional Team, Head Office: Crisis Response and Recovery Department (CRRD), Ethics & Compliance, Operations and Strategy, Finance, Global Philanthropy & Partnerships, Technical Excellence and General Counsel.

**Key External Contacts:** Partner organizations, host country government officials, public and private donor agencies, international and national NGOs, UN agencies

**PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:**

- Strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and ability to deploy strong communications effectively, both internally and externally, and in emergency operational contexts. Ability to build networks, partnerships and diversify program resources.
- Experience in a leadership role in conflict settings and situations of constrained humanitarian access required.
- Graduate degree in a relevant field.
- At least 12 years of dynamically responsible international work experience, including leadership at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment, with demonstrated responsibility for emergency preparedness, crisis management, and operational response. Preference for experience in the MENAU Region.
- Fluency in English is required. Arabic is a preferred asset.

**Demonstrated Technical Skills:**

- Superior communication skills, verbal and written.
- Experience in managing security in a complex and rapidly changing security context.
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with both institutional and private donors.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Prior work experience and a keen understanding of political complexities in Yemen and the Middle East and North Africa region is preferred.

**Demonstrated Managerial/Leadership Competencies:**

- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in cross-cultural settings, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Analytical, strategic, and able to proactively develop solutions to complex challenges.
- Comfortable with ambiguity and decision making in a fast-paced environment.
- Effective in developing high-potential staff to achieve career growth and maximum contribution.
- Proven experience in managing high-quality programming that meets the needs of clients.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels of oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Experience building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization.
- Opportunity-awareness. A successful innovative approach to unpredictable programming, operational, and funding contexts.
- Ability to dispassionately represent program context, constraints, and successes to media, government, and other senior audiences.
- Highly resilient and comfortable working in an insecure environment with restricted personal freedoms.

**Ability to Travel: Position is primarily based in Aden, Yemen.** Approximately 5-10 % outside the region for workshops, representation, and conferences.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and giving them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENAU, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: National Protection Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** National Protection Coordinator

**Function:** Programmes

**Job Group** Programme Support

**Duty Station:** South Sudan

**Line Manager:** Programme Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** No

**Position Type:** Short-Term Casual (1 month)

**Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP)** is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**NP SOUTH SUDAN OVERVIEW**

NP has been implementing protection and peacebuilding projects in South Sudan since 2010. The programme currently encompasses four field locations across four states, providing emergency protection, social cohesion, and violence prevention among communities affected by conflict.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The National Protection Coordinator is a member of the programme team responsible for general community protection in Western Equatoria State for a month-long field deployment in December 2026. This includes implementing protection and prevention strategies for vulnerable beneficiaries and relationship-building with local communities, community leaders, and government authorities, as well as with all other relevant protection actors such as NGOs and INGOs, and UN agencies. The Protection Coordinator will assist with training and support of the NP team.

Current or previous NP employees are encouraged to apply.

**COMMITMENT TO NP PRINCIPLES**

All staff are expected to embody and actively work towards NP’s [core principles](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/NP_Global_Strategy_2021-2025_Final_November_2021.pdf) in all aspects of their work:

1. **Nonviolence** in our approach, language, and actions.
2. **Direct Action** when engaging meaningfully with mandate goals.
3. **Radical Connection** through fostering safe, respectful, and inclusive relationships with communities, partners, and colleagues.
4. **Process-oriented** by abiding by NP's values, policies, and the Global Employee Handbook.
5. **Independence** by maintaining integrity in judgment and conduct.
6. **Nonpartisanship** by acting without bias or partisan influence.
7. **Redemption and Healing** by contributing to environments where accountability and growth are possible.
8. **Pluriversality** by embracing and protecting the diversity of all people NP works with and for.

**KEY OBJECTIVES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Project Implementation/Programming**

1. **Information gathering and contextual analysis**
1. Assist with information gathering and verification, and context analysis.
2. Proactively engage with all stakeholders in conflict (local community leaders, government authorities, police, army, non-state armed groups, and NGOs) to identify ongoing and potential issues in the community that may trigger violence.
2. **Community Engagement**
1. Lead participatory meetings so as to support communities to apply NP principles and UCP mechanisms to improve their own security.
2. Conduct check-in calls and follow-up visits with community protection actors to assess their security situation and offer support in case of challenges with the implementation of protection mechanisms and security concerns.
3. **Translation**
1. Assist with written translation of training materials.
2. Provide oral translation during workshops and meetings.
3. Protective presence, accompaniment and other interventions
4. Provide protective presence in situations where and when an incident may occur or has happened and which is a direct threat to peace and stability of the community while upholding the principle of nonpartisanship.
5. Provide protective accompaniment to civilians at risk.
6. Assist in designing strategic interventions meant to mitigate conflict and protect civilians.

**2. Administration & Operations**

1. **Reporting**
1. Report on all work activities according to the set procedures and standards of the Team Leader.
2. Participate in team meetings, debriefs and strategy sessions, implementing recommendations arising from lessons learnt.
2. **Security**
1. Contribute to security assessments and contribute to the maintenance of security of the NP office and equipment.
2. Ensure all project work is consistent with agreed safety and security policies and procedures.
3. **Compound Maintenance and procurement**
1. Assist with procurement of supplies or other logistical matters when delegated by the Team Leader.
4. **Other**
1. Perform any work-related duties that may be assigned by the Team Leader.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Experience**
- 3-5 years of work experience in human security, child or civilian protection.
- **Field Readiness**
- Demonstrated ability to live, work and solve problems independently and effectively in remote, highly challenging locations.
- **Language**
- English
- Preference to anyone who speaks any of the local languages or Arabic
- **Skills & Competencies**
- **Crisis Management:** Decisive problem-solving skills under pressure with minimal immediate supervision.

**TRAVEL & WORKING CONDITIONS**

- **Deployment:** 100% international travel to a field-based setting for the full duration of the 1-month contract.
- **Environment:** Ability to operate effectively in high-pressure, fast-paced, and potentially resource-constrained environments with minimal infrastructure.
- **Schedule:** Expectation to work extended hours, including weekends, to maximize impact during the compressed 1-month timeline.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer committed to a fair, transparent and accessible recruitment process. All qualified applicants are considered solely on merit, regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

Nonviolent Peaceforce is committed to safeguarding the welfare of our employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, partner communities, and all stakeholders. All staff and volunteers are expected to uphold this commitment through our Code of Conduct, complete the appropriate safeguarding training, and work in accordance with our safeguarding policies.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
ICVA is looking for an Executive Director to harness the power of its large global membership and lead its secretariat to see the 2030 Strategy through to its close and shape what comes next.

## **About ICVA**

Founded in 1962, the International Council of Voluntary Agencies (ICVA) is a global network of NGOs. Our mission is to make humanitarian action more principled and effective by working collectively and independently to influence policy and practice.

Our members range from local and national organisations to large international NGOs. Working together, the Secretariat leads the network across three areas: Forced Displacement, Humanitarian Coordination and Humanitarian Financing, with the promotion of humanitarian principles running through all areas of work.

The secretariat is based in Geneva, with regional representation across Middle East, Asia Pacific, West, Central and East Africa and Latin America.

### **Managing the Secretariat**

The Executive Director heads a dispersed secretariat team, headquartered in Geneva, with staff currently in Amman, Bangkok, Bogota, Dublin, Nairobi, and Yaoundé. Yet leading ICVA is more than running an organisation. The secretariat exists to convene, support and amplify its members, so much of the Executive Director's leadership is exercised through influence, trust, and consensus.

Success depends on multiple factors: ensuring a well managed effective and funded secretariat, building a strong team, working under pressure in a constrained resource environment; listening to members across regions, bringing differing views to common ground and making sure the network as a whole is present in the decisions that affect humanitarian action and representing the vision of the members at Principal level in senior policy fora.

## **Why the network matters**

ICVA's value lies in both its members services, providing the members with tools, information, collective platforms and partnership, networking opportunities to facilitate their work and doing what members could not do alone, representing the collective NGO vision to forge an effective humanitarian system. The network brings the experience of NGOs working alongside people affected by crisis into the places where humanitarian policy is decided and carries those decisions back to the organisations that put them into practice.

It is also a space where NGOs of very different sizes, origins and mandates can test ideas, agree common positions and speak with one voice. That collective voice carries more weight with UN agencies, member states and donors than any single organisation could achieve on its own.

## **Influential Representation**

ICVA holds a number of representative roles on behalf of the NGO community. The Executive Director represents the network among the Principals of the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC), the most senior forum for international humanitarian coordination with the UN system, where ICVA is one of three NGO consortia invited on a permanent basis.

The Secretariat hosts key initiatives in the humanitarian sector - including the CBPF Resource Facility, the newly launched NRG Facility under the Grand Bargain, the Interagency PSEA Community Outreach and Communication Fund and is currently serving as PSEA Champion.

These roles carry real responsibility. In them, the Executive Director speaks for a diverse membership, and must earn and keep the trust of members, member states, UN and other international agencies and donors alike.

### **Shaping the next strategic period**

ICVA is nearing the close of its 2030 Strategy. With three years of the current strategy still to run, the incoming Executive Director will see it through to completion while leading the development of the new strategic plan that will underpin the next phase for ICVA.

That means taking stock with members of what has been achieved, reading a changing humanitarian landscape, and working with the Board to set a direction that keeps ICVA relevant and useful to the organisations it exists to serve.

## **Purpose of the role**

Working closely with Board members and reporting the Board Chair, the ED will lead the development and implementation of ICVA's strategy, oversee its financial and operational performance, and strengthen fundraising and partnerships. The ED will provide strong an effective leadership for the Secretariat Team.

The ED will represent an influential global network of civil society members, working with the members, partners and governmental bodies.

The ED will be responsible for the further development of the ICVA network by building on its strengths, maintaining the confidence of its Members, donors and stakeholders, and ensuring that ICVA delivers measurable, sustainable, and demonstrable impact for people affected by crisis.

For full details of the role please refer to: [https://icvanetwork.org/opportunities/7575](https://icvanetwork.org/opportunities/7575)

jobs.title: SOUTH SUDAN - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIPS HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - JUBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/01/2027**
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**
**Location : Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The Grants department currently has 1 Grants & Partnership Head of Department Expat, 1 Grants Manager Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer National. With the mission scale up, the idea is to add Compliance Manager National. A Compliance coordinator supports the mission only part time and is therefore not in charge of audits.

## About the job

**General objective:**

\- The objectives of the position rely on donor engagement, financing and partnership strategy, preparation of project documents, contract management, partnership management, compliance and external audits, external communication, internal control.
\- Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Grants & Partnership Head of Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. He/She supervises, adapts and optimises working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.
The Grants Department validates contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.
It plays a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). The Grants & Partnership Head of Department ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- SI has increased the number of consortium we lead/are part of and we need the Grants department to support better engagement with these partners.
\- SI also needs to have more capacities to engage on the localization agenda.
\- In the meantime, SI needs to build a strong Grants department supported by national staffs.
\- The Grants & Partnership Department scale up should facilitate and lighten the work of the program teams on the ground who have to face an increasing number of reporting & proposal requests.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\- Support localization effort and engage with a couple of selected local partners.
\- Support follow up of proposals submitted in the Dec-Jan period (notably ECHO)

**Security constraints :**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.
The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves
There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master Degree in financial / accountancy studies

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experience on a similar position : 0-2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Excellent writing skills & mastering of MS Office suite

2\. Donors rule understanding & knowledge: ECHO, CDCS, FIFSAN, Norway MoFA, FCDO, DoS, SSHF

3\. Donor platform technicities: APPEL, GMS, UNPP

4\. Contractual management

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Capacity building experience

2\. Department structuring knowledge

3\. Information management structuration is a +

4\. Networking capacities

5\. Very hands-on: not top senior management only: capacity to be a doer as well

6\. Attraction for the field

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Very good in English, written and spoken.

2\. French & Arabic are a +

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grants & Parternships Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.
Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.
Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

jobs.description:
**Role:** International Faculty Lead (French Speaking)

**Remuneration:** £4,500 gross per month, plus a 10% adverse conditions allowance for periods spent in-country.

**Hours:** Full-time, with some evening and weekend working required to support humanitarian programme delivery. Staff will have one full rest day per week during deployment.

**Duration:** From mid-November 2026 to 31 March 2027, with the possibility of an extension subject to funding availability.

**Location:** Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). International travel and deployment arrangements will be coordinated by UK-Med, subject to operational requirements and security clearances.

*Candidates must be able to travel quickly through Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), securing visas on arrival with eligible documentation. If you do not meet this requirement, you can join our register of humanitarian and health professionals for other opportunities.*

**Can you strengthen frontline healthcare worker preparedness during one of the world’s largest Ebola outbreaks?**

UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity. Born of the NHS, we’ve been working for over 30 years towards a world where everyone has the healthcare they need when crises or disasters hit.
We are seeking an experienced health professional to establish and lead the training function of UK-Med’s Ebola training and simulation programmes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (BDBV) outbreak continues to place significant pressure on national health systems and response capacities. Fluency in French (written and spoken) is essential for this role. Candidates must be able to facilitate training, manage teams and engage with stakeholders confidently in French.

Since cases were first reported in May 2026, the outbreak has spread across multiple provinces, with community transmission ongoing and linked cases confirmed in neighbouring countries. As of 26 October 2026, DRC has reported over 10,000 confirmed cases and nearly 4,900 deaths, with the highest burden concentrated in Ituri, North Kivu and Haut-Uélé provinces.

Working closely with WHO, the Ministry of Health and international partners, UK-Med is supporting efforts to strengthen outbreak preparedness and response through high-quality training, simulation exercises and workforce development. This includes plans to replicate WHO’s established Ebola Training Hub model, initially in Beni, North Kivu, with potential expansion to other priority locations.

You will oversee and coordinate the delivery of consistent, high-quality training programmes for healthcare workers, helping to build clinical confidence, improve infection prevention and control practices, and support safe patient care in a complex humanitarian setting. You will work closely with national stakeholders, international partners and programme leadership to ensure training activities are high-quality, well-coordinated, practical and responsive to operational needs.

The role requires strong technical expertise, adaptability and the ability to work effectively in resource-constrained environments. We are looking for an individual who can combine specialist knowledge with collaboration, flexibility and a commitment to strengthening local capacity during a critical public health emergency.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the Ebola response in DRC, supporting healthcare workers and health systems at a time when their expertise is needed most.
