jobs.description:
**Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Independent Red Teaming and AI Safety Evaluation

Procurement Method Open competitive tender

Assignment Type Independent organisation or specialist consultancy

Primary Market Kenya

Contract Period Approximately 10 weeks

Reporting To Head of Technology and Product

Clarification Deadline 10 November 2026

Proposal Deadline 18 November 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

Independence is a mandatory condition. The selected evaluator must not be involved in building, operating, or commercially benefiting from the systems evaluated under this assignment.

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that adolescent girls want, trust and need. We create digital-first brands and products that reach girls at scale across Africa and Asia, supporting them to make informed choices about their health, education and futures — with a particular focus on sexual and reproductive health (SRH).

Girl Effect has worked in responsible AI for several years and has published its own Ethical AI Guidelines and a Generative AI Whitepaper, co-authored sector guidance on the safe use of chatbots for social and behaviour change, and operates named accountability for AI safety — including a Failure Mode Register with safeguarding sign-off, and defined escalation protocols with service-level commitments for human follow-up. We believe that AI serving young people in the Global South must be held to the highest evidential standard, and that the organisations building such systems should not be the only ones marking their own homework. This engagement exists to put that principle into practice.

## **Background**

WAZZII is Girl Effect’s WhatsApp-based chatbot in Kenya. It provides adolescent girls and young women with confidential and non-judgemental information about their bodies, relationships and health. It also connects users to relevant products, referrals and health services, supported by a human help desk responsible for moderation and escalation.

WAZZII’s next phase will expand the use of generative AI in the girl-facing experience. This includes:

- Retrieval-grounded responses using clinically approved content;
- AI-assisted tools for human help-desk operators;
- Safeguarding and clinical escalation pathways;
- Internal evaluation of model outputs; and
- Defined policies covering content and actions that the system must never produce.

Girl Effect seeks an independent partner to test whether these safeguards perform as intended and identify risks that may not have been detected through internal evaluation.

The selected partner must be separate from the organisations developing or operating the systems being tested.

## **Objective**

The objective is to conduct a focused and independent red-team evaluation of WAZZII’s girl-facing generative AI capability.

The assignment will:

- Identify safety, safeguarding, clinical and technical vulnerabilities;
- Test whether the system recognises and safely escalates relevant risks;
- Assess whether existing evaluations and controls adequately reflect real-world use;
- Produce reproducible test cases that Girl Effect can rerun;
- Rank findings by severity, likelihood and potential impact; and
- Provide practical and prioritised recommendations for remediation and future evaluation.

The core assignment is a single time-bound evaluation. Remediation re-testing, review of agentic designs and periodic testing will be priced separately as optional extensions.

## **What You will do**

The core engagement runs over an indicative ten weeks. All work follows Girl Effect’s Ethical AI Guidelines, data policy and safeguarding policy: testing is conducted against staging environments using synthetic personas, no real user data is accessed or collected, data collection is minimised throughout, and no safeguarding case content is handled at any point. Girl Effect will provide staging access, including programmatic (API) access to the conversational endpoint, supporting automated test harnesses; testing may be conducted fully remotely, with no in-country presence required. Key activities include:

Phase 1 — Orientation and test design (indicatively weeks 1–3)

- Focused desk review of Girl Effect’s evaluation framework, red-line policies and escalation protocol — sufficient to design a well-targeted test plan, not a standalone audit
- Co-scoping of the scenario taxonomy and severity rubric with Girl Effect’s AI Ethics Officer and safeguarding leads, and agreement of the responsible-disclosure protocol for critical findings

Phase 2 — Red-teaming sprint (indicatively weeks 3–8)

- A structured, tool-supported testing exercise against the girl-facing GenAI experience in staging, combining adversarial and realistic non-adversarial scenarios and producing logged, machine-readable, re-runnable test cases, prioritising: clinically incorrect or harmful health advice; failure to recognise and escalate safeguarding disclosures; jailbreaks, prompt injection and policy circumvention; and age-inappropriate content
- Testing across the languages and code-switching patterns of real users (including Kiswahili and Sheng); local-language competence may be provided by the partner or in pairing with Girl Effect's own team
- Stress-testing of the human-escalation pathway, primarily with realistic non-adversarial scenarios (genuine distress, disclosure and clinical-concern personas where the system should hand over without being attacked): does it hand over to the help desk when it should

Phase 3 — Findings and briefing (indicatively weeks 8–10)

- A severity-ranked findings report with reproducible test cases, handed over so Girl Effect’s team can re-run them continuously after the engagement ends
- A findings briefing for Girl Effect leadership, with prioritised recommendations — including what a fuller evaluation should cover next and at what cadence

Optional priced extensions (quoted separately, commissioned at Girl Effect’s discretion)

- Re-test of remediated critical findings
- Architecture-level adversarial review of agentic system designs (threat-modelling autonomy, tool use and failure modes before deployment)
- Periodic re-testing and pre-launch adversarial gates for major releases

## **Deliverables**

Deliverable Description Indicative timing

Inception note & test plan Confirmed methodology, scenario taxonomy and

severity rubric, staging/access arrangements,

ethics and data-handling approach,

responsible-disclosure protocol Week 3

Red-team findings report Severity-ranked, reproducible findings

from the adversarial sprint, including

escalation-pathway results; test cases handed over

for continuous internal re-use Week 8

Leadership briefing & recommendations Findings briefing with prioritised recommendations

and proposed scope/cadence for future

independent evaluation Week 10

## **Duration and Working Arrangements**

The core engagement is expected to run for approximately 10 weeks.

Testing may be completed remotely. No in-country presence is required unless separately agreed.

Girl Effect will provide:

- Approved access to the staging environment;
- Programmatic access to the conversational endpoint where available;
- Relevant documentation and evaluation materials;
- Named technical, safeguarding and programme focal points; and
- Consolidated feedback on deliverables.

The partner will:

- Participate in a weekly progress meeting;
- Maintain a shared delivery tracker and risk register;
- Use secure communication and evidence-sharing channels;
- Escalate critical issues immediately;
- Protect access credentials and evaluation materials; and
- Manage its personnel and delivery approach independently.

## **Independence and Conflicts of Interest**

Independence is a mandatory condition of award.

The bidder must:

- Have no current contract to build or operate the system being evaluated;
- Have no commercial interest in the evaluation achieving a particular outcome;
- Disclose any current or previous relationship with Girl Effect’s AI, platform or technology suppliers;
- Disclose any relevant relationship held during the previous 24 months;
- Identify any tools or models being evaluated in which it has a financial interest; and
- Explain how any potential conflict will be managed.

Girl Effect will determine whether a disclosed relationship affects the bidder’s eligibility or independence.

## **Who You Are**

The successful bidder should demonstrate:

- Experience independently red-teaming deployed AI systems rather than only evaluating standalone models.
- Experience with conversational AI, retrieval-augmented generation and multi-turn systems.
- Experience in health, safeguarding-sensitive or other high-risk contexts.
- Experience working with adolescent or youth-facing digital services.
- Strong knowledge of AI safety, responsible AI and model evaluation.
- Ability to build automated, machine-readable and rerunnable testing harnesses.
- Understanding of human escalation and moderation workflows.
- Ability to test English, Kiswahili and Sheng directly or through a credible quality-controlled approach.
- Experience working in Kenya, Africa or comparable Global South contexts.
- Strong security, confidentiality and responsible-disclosure practices.
- Excellent analytical, technical-reporting and leadership-presentation capability.

The proposed team should include named individuals with appropriate AI evaluation, technical, safeguarding and language expertise.

## **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Bidders must submit separate technical and financial proposals (Max 10 pages).

### **Technical Proposal**

It should include:

- Understanding of the assignment;
- Proposed methodology and testing tools;
- Proposed scenario taxonomy and coverage;
- Approach to automated and manual testing;
- Approach to safeguarding and escalation testing;
- Language and cultural-context capability;
- Data-handling and information-security approach;
- Responsible-disclosure process;
- Workplan and team structure;
- Relevant experience and comparable assignments;
- Key assumptions, dependencies, limitations and exclusions;
- Independence and conflict-of-interest declaration;
- Three client references; and
- One redacted example of a relevant findings report.

### **Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in USD and include:

- A fixed price for the core 10-week engagement;
- A cost breakdown by phase and deliverable;
- Personnel roles, daily rates and level of effort;
- Applicable taxes shown separately;
- Tools, licences and third-party costs;
- Reimbursable expenses shown separately;
- Day rates for each optional extension; and
- Clear assumptions, exclusions and conditions.

## **Evaluation**

Proposals will be assessed in the following order:

1. Pre-screening;
2. Technical evaluation;
3. Pitch, demonstration or clarification stage, where required; and
4. Financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion**

- Relevant AI red-teaming and system-evaluation experience: 25%
- Quality, coverage and practicality of the proposed methodology: 25%
- Proposed team and safeguarding or AI-safety capability: 10%
- Language, local-context and affected-community perspective: 10%

Technical Total 70%

- Financial proposal and overall value for money 30%

Total 100%

Girl Effect may request written clarifications, invite shortlisted bidders to a pitch or technical demonstration, conduct reference checks and due diligence, or request a best-and-final offer.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: **4 November 2026**
- Questions/Clarification Deadline: **10th November 2026**
- Consolidated FAQ shared with all prospective bidders: **13th November 2026**
- Deadline for proposal submission: **18th November 2026**

### **Clarification Process**

Bidders may submit clarification questions to suppliers@girleffect.org by 10th November 2026

The email subject should state:

Clarification Question –**Independent AI Red-Team Evaluation**

To ensure a fair and transparent open-tender process:

- Girl Effect will not provide substantive answers to all bidders.
- All relevant questions and responses will be compiled into a consolidated FAQ.
- The FAQ will not identify the organisation that submitted each question.
- The consolidated FAQ will be shared with all prospective bidders through the same publication or communication channels used for the RFP.
- Bidders are responsible for reviewing the FAQ and any formal tender updates before submitting their proposals.
- Verbal information or guidance will not amend the RFP unless confirmed by Girl Effect in writing.

Girl Effect may decline to answer questions received after the clarification deadline.

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting:** The successful bidder will sign Girl Effect’s standard services agreement, statement of work and applicable data-processing and information-security documentation.
- **Payment:** Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of agreed deliverables. Girl Effect may withhold payment for incomplete, defective or unapproved work.
- **Pricing:** The agreed implementation pricing will remain fixed unless a change is approved through the formal written change-control process.
- **Expenses:** Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable. Reimbursable expenses must be supported by appropriate documentation.
- **Intellectual Property:** Girl Effect will own all foreground intellectual property, deliverables, source code, configurations, designs and documentation created specifically under the engagement, subject to agreed treatment of pre-existing tools and third-party materials.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The partner must protect Girl Effect’s confidential information and personal data and comply with applicable data-protection requirements.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference, safeguarding, information-security and compliance checks. The successful bidder must comply with Girl Effect’s code of conduct, safeguarding and anti-fraud requirements.
- **Subcontracting:** No material part of the assignment may be subcontracted without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The lead bidder remains responsible for all subcontracted work.
- **Warranties and Defects:** Bidders should propose a warranty period during which defects in accepted deliverables will be corrected at no additional cost.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal or participating in clarification, pitch or negotiation stages.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the procurement; reject any or all proposals; award the full or partial scope; award in phases; or make no award.
- **No Commitment:** Publication of this RFP does not constitute a commitment to enter into a contract.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Operation Officer - Kenya
jobs.description:
## Work Context

CESVI is an Italian humanitarian and development organisation with a regional coordination office in Nairobi. In Kenya, CESVI combines emergency response and long-term development through food security and livelihoods, protection, WASH, circular economy and disaster risk reduction, working with communities, local authorities and partner organisations.

CESVI works across emergency response and development, focusing on food security and agricultural livelihoods, protection, WASH, circular economy and disaster risk reduction. Its current interventions cover Garissa and Tana River counties through PROGRESA; Nakuru and Kilifi counties through AGRIPACT; and school and community WASH activities in Tharaka Nithi and Makueni counties through the ENI project. Activities are implemented in collaboration with county authorities, local organisations, cooperatives and communities.

## **Job Description**

**Job summary:**

Ensure effective financial administration, accounting, procurement and logistics support for CESVI’s activities. Work with the Project Manager, Country Administrator and logistics teams to maintain accurate records, compliant expenditure, timely procurement and reliable field operations in Kenya.

**1. PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLY CHAIN**

- Review and update project’s procurement plan and track requests, tenders, quotations, evaluation records, purchase orders and delivery schedules.
- Conduct supplier mapping and market surveys, collect comparable quotations and support transparent supplier assessments and procurement risk mitigation.
- Coordinate technical specifications and acceptance criteria with project staff.
- Prepare supplier and service contracts for authorized review and signature. Monitor performance, deliveries, warranties, and maintenance arrangements.
- Verify delivery of documentation with technical staff and maintain complete procurement and distribution records, including beneficiary handover and asset-ownership documentation.
- Respect delegated approval limits and segregation of duties.

**2. LOGISTICS AND FIELD OPERATIONS**

- Coordinate travel, accommodation, transport and training logistics for field activities, partner meetings and monitoring visits.
- Maintain stock and asset registers, movement records, and monthly stock reports. Organize physical checks and document discrepancies.
- Oversee assigned vehicles or transport services, maintaining records of rentals, fuel, servicing, repairs and use.
- Support shared-office arrangements in Garissa, Nakuru and Kilifi and Nairobi office requirements, coordinating leases, utilities, communications, supplies and maintenance within approved budgets.
- Provide day-to-day guidance to assigned support personnel or service providers, according to the approved staffing structure.
- Support implementation of CESVI security procedures, communication and contingency arrangements under the Head of Mission or designated security focal point. Report incidents and assist emergency movements when instructed.

**3. FINANCIAL ADMINISTRATION AND ACCOUNTING**

- Manage assigned cash and bank records and prepare monthly reconciliations, submitting them for independent review and approval.
- Maintain programme accounting and complete supporting files. Check expenditure eligibility, coding, documentation and approvals against CESVI, donor and partnership requirements.
- Prepare financial forecasts, cash requests, expenditure projections, and budget-monitoring updates with the Project Manager and Country Administrator.
- Prepare and upload accounting data weekly into the designated system. Track staff advances, petty cash and timely liquidation, resolving missing documents with responsible staff.
- Support interim and final financial reports, audit preparation and follow-up of financial queries. Maintain a clear audit trail and secure records.
- Prepare payroll inputs, timesheets, employment-cost documentation and supplier payment files, coordinating with administration on applicable Kenyan requirements, including submitting of local tax returns and statutory deductions.
- Close the cash account every month, physical counting, printing of reconciliation documents, checking of supporting documents as well as occasional surprise cash counts.
- File invoices according to accounting procedures
- Assist in documents preparation during audit

**4. HUMAN RESOURCE**

**Participate in managing the national staff and ensuring administrative follow-up of the files.**

- Check contract dates for Kenyan staff and inform the Country Admin and Head of mission of their expiry date;
- Keep the individual files up-to-date for Kenyan staff and selected Somalia staff
- Check that the procedures regarding recruitment and contract terminations are followed for Kenyan Staff
- Offer guidelines on the preparation of new employment contracts for Kenyan staff according to the HR manual and approved Salary Grid and final drafting of the final version of the contract
- Follow up the annual appraisals of Kenyan staff and ensure that all staff involved in the appraisal schedule it properly and respect the deadlines.
- Updating the database for Kenyan salary payroll and sharing with Regional Administrator for validation before payment
- Ensure that all the due taxes are regularly calculated and remitted.

**Contribute to exchanging information and respecting the HR procedures In Kenya.**

- Actively participate during meetings organised with national employees on the HR rules and procedures;
- Formal communication to staff on HR related updates (Holidays, closure of office)
- Inform new Nairobi’s employees of the internal rules; ensure that the base administrator provide the same information at base level

**Participate in evaluating and organizing the work.**

- Implement recruitment procedures; ensure that all the proper authorization has been requested, and that the proper format has been used, as well that the Job description are coherent with Cesvi standards and PMs needs for Staff recruited in Kenya
- Participate in the recruitment of junior national staff in Nairobi

**Participate in careers and staff mobility management.**

- Support the Line managers in the organization of annual appraisal meetings and analyse the grids;
- Train the managers in the use of HR tools;
- Facilitate the process of staff promotion;

**Work on the Kenyan Office human resources administratively:**

- Prepare identity cards for new employees;
- Sort all documents in the domestic employees’ individual files and check that all files are complete.

**5. COORDINATION AND REPORTING**

- Coordinate operational needs with the Project Manager, Country Administrator, Project technical staff, HQ support teams and projects’ partners.
- Prepare weekly operational updates and monthly finance, procurement, stock and fleet reports, flagging risks, delays, and proposed corrective actions.
- Train staff on administrative documentation, procurement requests, advance liquidation and stock or asset recording systems.
- Follow CESVI safeguarding, PSEA, anti-fraud, conflict-of-interest and confidentiality policies, and perform related duties assigned within the role’s competence.

## **Essential requirements**

- Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Procurement or a related discipline, obtained at least three years ago, in line with the source role requirements.
- At least two years of relevant experience in a similar combined administration and logistics role within a corporate environment, an NGO, UN agency or comparable international organisation.
- Practical experience in accounting, cash/ bank reconciliation, financial documentation, procurement, stock or asset management and budget monitoring.
- Knowledge of donor-funded procurement and financial compliance, with the ability to apply CESVI procedures and approved partnership arrangements.
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines under pressure.
- Strong communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with professional and diplomatic stakeholder engagement.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and experience using accounting or administrative systems.
- Fluent written and spoken English and Kiswahili. Willingness to travel regularly to projects implementation areas

### **Other requirements**

- Experience with AICS-funded projects or multi-partner programmes is an added advantage.
- CPA, ACCA, CIPS or another relevant professional certification.
- Experience with Kenyan employment-cost documentation, supplier administration and shared field offices.
- Experience supporting agricultural, cooperative or circular economy programmes.

## **Safeguarding**

CESVI has a zero-tolerance approach to any harm to, or exploitation of, a child or a vulnerable adult by any of our staff, related persons or partners.
CESVI commitment to being a safe organization begins with the staff recruitment process which includes meticulous checks, such as criminal records checks or check disclosure of previous convictions, to ensure children and vulnerable people are safeguarded and abuse is prevented. Safeguarding checks are part of the selection process performance.

For further information regarding CESVI policies: [https://www.cesvi.eu/who-we-are/transparency/our-policies/](https://www.cesvi.eu/who-we-are/transparency/our-policies/)

jobs.title: Program and Reporting coordinator – Geneva, Switzerland
jobs.description:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Geneva

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Direct report:** Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development

**Grade:** Coordinator

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this role?**

Under the direct supervision of Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development, the Program and Reporting Coordinator is responsible for the overall coordination of two global projects on protection of civilians and humanitarian engagement with armed groups and De facto and/or Provisional authorities. The overall activities are planning, coordination, and supporting the implementation of project activities; internal and external communications; managing partnerships with project stakeholders; and monitoring financial and compliance obligations for the project. The position holder is responsible for producing high-quality reporting on deliverables and further development and advancement of the projects.

## **Work Relations**

The Program and Reporting Coordinator will work under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development and will collaborate closely with Programme teams and country missions, as well as Policy, Research and Legal (PRL), MEAL and Donor Relations Units at HQ. The incumbent will also work closely with financial controllers and project focal points across HQ and country missions to ensure effective project planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting.

## **Duties and Responsabilities**

**Multi country Project coordination**

- Project planning of two global projects with all relevant missions and units to ensure efficient running of multi country porjects in alignment with defined timelines.
- Ensure coordination of projects with team members located in HQ and country missions to keep work and information flow on track.
- In coordination with focal points of the project, oversee HQ level administrative tasks associated with project.
- Organize and manage regular project meetings and enhance collaborations across various components of global projects.

**Project implementation**

- Support the Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development to monitor the progress of the project implementation, including from a financial perspective.
- In coordination with focal points, ensure implementation plans of the project are in place and all deliverables are monitored and reported on time.
- Coordinate with program, PRL and MEAL units and ensure programmatic methodolgies and guidelines are developed in alignment with Project Cycle Management (PCM) handbook.

**Project reporting, development and compliance**

- Ensure timely delivery of project outputs, monitor progress against indicators, and adjust plans as needed in coordination with the focal points.
- Compiling of information and impact stories required for drafting of the reports.
- Draft clear and impactful donor reports, ensuring quality and timeliness.
- Act as a focal point for internal and external communication regarding the projects, tailoring messaging to diverse audiences.
- In coordination with program team and Donor Relations unit, take lead in the development of proposals to ensure long term continuation of the projects.

**Financial Compliance and Management**

- Monitor and track projects budget in coordiantion with financial controllers and ensure financial resources are aligned with planned activities and donor requirements.
- Oversee compliance with Geneva Call policies, donor agreements, and legal obligations.
- In coordination with focal points, analyse potential risk and mitigation measures throughout project implementation.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in international relations, international development or a related field.

**Education (Desirable)**

- Recognised project management certification, such as PRINCE2, PMP, CAPM or IPMA.
- Additional training in Project Cycle Management, MEAL or donor compliance.

**Experience (Essential)**

- 10+ years of experience of experience in project management, including at least 2 years in an HQ setting.
- Proven experience in coordinating and managing global or multi-country projects.
- Strong understanding and practical experience of Project Cycle Management (PCM) processes and tools.
- Demonstrated experience in project administration, implementation, monitoring and coordination across different teams and locations.

**Experience (Desirable)**

- Previous experience in capacity building of partners on project deliverables.
- Experience working in an international humanitarian organisation or NGO.
- Previous experience in proposal development and resource mobilisation.
- Experience working with institutional donors and managing donor-funded projects.

**Job related competencies (Essential)**

- Strong financial literacy, including project budget planning, monitoring and management.
- Strong drafting and reporting skills, particularly in preparing high-quality donor reports.
- Strong IT skills and ability to use project management tools.
- Ability to integrate gender and intersectional perspectives into project design and implementation.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to represent the organisation externally and tailor communications to different audiences.

**Organisational Competencies**

- Strong leadership and people management skills.
- Ability to build and maintain trusting and collaborative relationships.
- Ability to promote teamwork and effective collaboration across departments.
- Commitment to fostering an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Ability to demonstrate accountability, sound judgement and alignment with Geneva Call’s organisational values.

**Language (Essential)**

- Fluency in English and French both spoken and written.

**Language (Desirable)**

- Knowledge of Spanish, Arabic, or any other language relevant to Geneva Call’s operations is an advantage.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call brings together people of diverse nationalities, cultures, languages and perspectives, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

As Program and Reporting Coordinator, you will play a key role in coordinating and advancing global projects, working across HQ and country missions to ensure effective implementation, meaningful results and strong partnerships. This is an opportunity to contribute to impactful humanitarian initiatives while collaborating with diverse teams and stakeholders in an international and multicultural environment.

jobs.title: Senior Research Manager
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

The Senior Research Manager will lead Farsight Africa Group’s research portfolio, taking responsibility for the design, delivery and quality of a wide range of research projects across our key areas. The role holder will work across Nairobi (Kenya), Somalia and Uganda, managing multi-country projects in East Africa, including fragile and conflict-affected settings.

The successful candidate will bring strong research, analytical, design and reporting expertise, drawing on a solid combination of qualitative and quantitative experience. They will manage client relationships, lead and develop the research team, and work with senior management to grow Farsight’s research business. The position reports to senior management and supervises Research Executives, Research Assistants, field teams and subcontractors.

**Scope of Work:**

**Research Leadership and Delivery:**

- Lead the management and delivery of research projects from scoping, design and methodology through fieldwork, analysis and report writing.
- Design and deliver a wide range of social research techniques, including in-person and in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, surveys, literature reviews and data analysis.
- Oversee qualitative and quantitative data collection, ensuring data quality, research ethics, safeguarding and data protection standards are upheld.
- Adapt research tools and approaches to the cultural, linguistic and security context of each country of operation.
- Produce insightful research reports, policy briefs and presentations with sophisticated, actionable advice that supports client decision-making.

**Multi-Country Project and Resource Management:**

- Plan and manage project resources, workplans, timelines and financial budgets across multiple countries.
- Recruit, manage and coordinate in-country field teams and subcontractors, including market research fieldwork partners, seeking best value at all times.
- Supervise, mentor and develop junior research staff to achieve project objectives and build team capacity.
- Anticipate operational risks such as access, security and logistics, and put proactive mitigation measures in place.
- Travel regularly to project countries to oversee fieldwork and engage clients and stakeholders.

**Business Development and Client Management:**

- Work with senior managers and directors to win new work from new and existing clients.
- Lead the preparation of written proposals and bids, including technical approaches, methodologies, workplans and budgets.
- Proactively identify new business opportunities in research services and policy markets, in line with the company’s strategic ambitions.
- Manage and develop relationships with clients, donors, government counterparts and partners.
- Raise the profile of Farsight’s research expertise with clients and key influencers through presentations, publications and events.

**Knowledge and Quality Management:**

- Ensure the company stays up to date with developments in specified policy areas and research markets.
- Set and maintain quality standards for research tools, data and deliverables across all projects.
- Contribute to internal research guidelines, tools and learning sessions.
- Perform any other duties assigned by management.

**Qualifications and Skills:**

- Master’s degree in Social Sciences or a related field, with a focus on research or project management.
- A minimum of 5–7 years of working experience in research and project management in the East Africa region, including multi-country projects.
- Demonstrated professional leadership and the ability to coordinate a team of professionals, including remote field teams.
- Experience designing qualitative fieldwork (such as in-depth interviews and focus groups) and quantitative fieldwork (such as survey questionnaires, data analysis and data visualisation).
- Proven track record of writing successful proposals and managing project budgets.
- Experience working in fragile or conflict-affected contexts; previous work in Somalia and Uganda will be an added advantage.
- Proficiency in analysis software such as SPSS, Stata, R or NVivo, and experience supporting presentation design and delivery.
- Excellent client-facing and internal verbal and written communication skills; familiarity with the Somali language will be an added advantage.
- Excellent analytical and reporting skills.
- Solid organisational skills, including attention to detail and multi-tasking.
- Ability to anticipate challenges and proactively head off obstacles.
- Excellent problem-solving skills; innovative and solutions-oriented.
- Willingness to work across and travel frequently between Nairobi, Somalia and Uganda.

**Equal Opportunity Statement**

Farsight Africa Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of gender, age, disability, religion, ethnicity, or any other protected characteristic. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

**Why Join Farsight**

- Work with a fast-growing, innovative African consulting firm.
- Lead meaningful multi-country research across governance, development and strategic communications.
- Be part of a dynamic, multicultural team operating across East Africa and the Horn of Africa.
- Access opportunities for professional growth, leadership and regional exposure.

jobs.title: Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services
jobs.company: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
jobs.description:
**Nature of Consultancy:** Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment (with mission travel to Port-au-Prince and designated departmental hubs). Any required mission travel, including its dates, arrangements, security requirements, and reimbursement of agreed expenses, shall be specified or separately agreed in writing.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days/hours, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, deliverables, and estimated levels of effort agreed between COAR and the Consultant.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 01 December 2026 to 31 December 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed; it does not create an obligation to provide or accept assignments, guarantee a minimum workload, or require continuous availability. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated Haiti Team Lead, acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope. This role is for assignment coordination and does not confer authority to direct the Consultant's day-to-day working methods or exercise line-management authority over the Consultant.

**Overview:** This Scope of Work (SoW) outlines the specific senior technical consultancy assignment with the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant may be commissioned to provide specialist analytical and advisory services for an in-depth study examining the systemic, historical, and multidimensional crisis in Haiti. Commissioned in the context of UNDP and UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) strategic planning, the study is intended to establish an evidence-based baseline to guide conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and sustainable recovery initiatives across Haiti. The assignment may include the preparation of a comprehensive, formally published biennial report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks, accompanied by a strategic intervention approach for the United Nations system. The Consultant's responsibility shall be limited to the agreed research, analytical, drafting, advisory, and facilitation outputs. Decisions concerning publication, institutional endorsement, strategic adoption, and implementation shall remain with COAR and the commissioning institutions.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**About COAR:** COAR is an independent social enterprise that directly supports practitioners, policymakers, and donors by facilitating humanitarian and development interventions in complex, fragile, and high-risk environments. COAR delivers neutral and objective research and analysis, which identifies - but does not influence - local stakeholders, relationships, interests, and analyzes broader political, economic, social, and security dynamics and trends. COAR research leverages social media, personal networks, field research teams, and local experts in order to map and translate the local human context; COAR analysis synthesizes and studies this data in order to inform both programmatic and strategic decision-making, reduce security and conflict sensitivity risks, and increase the impact of humanitarian, development, stabilization, peace-building, and peacekeeping initiatives.

**Objectives**

For the specific study assignment, the Consultant may be commissioned to:

- Conduct an analysis of historical trends and trajectories of Haiti’s systemic, social, community, political, and economic crisis to develop a comprehensive understanding of underlying structural dynamics;
- Analyze the multidimensional drivers of fragility and crisis across national, departmental, and cross-border domains;
- Map crises and trace underlying drivers of distinct forms of violence (criminal, gang-driven, political, and gender-based) to elucidate crisis systems;
- Evaluate crisis dynamics through intersectional gender, generational, and social inequality perspectives, highlighting the contributions and protection of women and youth in conflict prevention and mediation;
- Review and assess past and ongoing conflict prevention and peacebuilding interventions supported by the UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) and key multilateral/bilateral partners;
- Propose a tailored intervention approach for the United Nations system anchored in conflict prevention and peacebuilding principles; and
- Where included in the agreed assignment, provide substantive input into the preparation of an inclusive multi-stakeholder validation workshop, including contributing to validation discussions and moderating specified panel sessions.

**Activities and Key Responsibilities**

The following activities describe potential services under the study assignment. The specific activities to be performed, their estimated effort, and the associated outputs shall be confirmed in writing before commencement.

1\. Analytical Framing & Methodological Design

- Develop an analytical framework and research matrix tailored to the Haitian operational context, integrating OECD DAC peacebuilding criteria and UN Integrated Strategic Framework (ISF) objectives.
- Formulate and calibrate qualitative and quantitative research instruments, including semi-structured Key Informant Interview (KII) guides, Focus Group Discussion (FGD) protocols, and secondary assessment templates.
- Incorporate strict Conflict Sensitivity, Do No Harm, and data protection protocols, reflecting localized security constraints and protection considerations in gang-controlled and fragile environments.

2\. Multidimensional Fragility, Violence & Hotspot Mapping

- Trace historical fault lines, institutional degradation, and economic patterns driving instability across Port-au-Prince and outlying departments (e.g., Artibonite, Nord, Grand'Anse).
- Document geographic conflict hotspots, illicit trade flows, arms proliferation corridors, and cross-border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Assess formal and informal mechanisms, social cohesion structures, customary dispute-resolution mechanisms, and local resilience dynamics fostering community stability.

3\. Intersectional Analysis & PBF Portfolio Assessment

- Analyze structural socio-economic inequalities, youth recruitment vulnerabilities, and gender-based violence (GBV) as systemic drivers of fragility.
- Conduct a focused desk review and stakeholder assessment of UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects and partner peacebuilding programming in Haiti, evaluating impact, lessons learned, and systemic gaps.
- Identify practical entry points and age- and gender-sensitive recommendations to strengthen the leadership of women and youth in peacebuilding architectures.

4\. Report Authoring & UN Strategic Intervention Approach

- Prepare and coordinate the analytical synthesis and drafting of the formal, publication-ready baseline report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks in Haiti.
- Draft a pragmatic, forward-looking UN intervention approach that connects empirical research findings with strategic programming across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus.
- Integrate technical review comments from COAR leadership, UNDP, PBF, and institutional counterparts into final publishable outputs to the extent that such comments are provided within the agreed review process and schedule. The Consultant shall identify and discuss any material changes to the agreed scope or analytical conclusions that arise during review.

5\. Stakeholder Workshop Coordination & Panel Moderation

- Where specified in the assignment, provide substantive recommendations on the agenda and content of the national multi-stakeholder validation workshop.
- Deliver technical presentations on analytical findings, methodological approaches, and strategic recommendations to UN leadership, civil society, and international partners, at agreed events or sessions.
- Moderate thematic panel discussions during inclusive consultations to cultivate national ownership and partnership consensus where the relevant sessions, preparation requirements, and expected level of effort have been agreed in writing.

**Expected Results and Deliverables**

The primary result of this assignment will be a publicly available, formally published large-scale report examining fragilities and risks related to peacebuilding and development in Haiti. The report serves three primary purposes:

1. Understanding Haiti’s Crisis: Deepening multilateral and national understanding of the systems, drivers, and trajectories underlying the crisis.
2. Strategic & Programmatic Decision-Making: Informing conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and HDP nexus resource allocation.
3. Advocacy & Dialogue: Supporting continuous, multilevel dialogue among national authorities, civil society, and international partners.

**Required Experience and Expertise**

- Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in Peace and Conflict Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, or a related discipline required.
- UN System Experience: Required minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience advising or implementing peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and stabilization programming within or alongside the UN System (e.g., UNDP, BINUH, DPO/DPPA, IOM, or UN Country Teams).
- Country & Contextual Expertise: Desired analytical or operational track record in Haiti, with nuanced understanding of Haitian political history, gang territorial dynamics, departmental socio-economic disparities, and border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Analytical Capabilities: Proven track record conducting complex conflict analyses, fragility assessments, and intersectional studies focusing on gender, youth, and structural inequalities.
- Facilitation & Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue: Proven experience designing and moderating high-level validation workshops, roundtables, and policy panels involving government counterparts, UN leadership, and grassroots civil society organizations.
- Languages: Professional proficiency in both French and English (written and spoken) is required; fluency or working knowledge of Haitian Creole (Kreyòl) is a distinct asset.

**Safeguarding, Ethics, and Confidentiality**

In performing the Services, the Consultant shall comply with COAR’s Code of Conduct, any applicable Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), and safeguarding requirements that COAR identifies in writing as applicable to external consultants and relevant to the accepted assignment. In light of the delicate security and protection environment in Haiti, the Consultant shall conduct agreed research and stakeholder interactions in accordance with Do No Harm principles, informant anonymity, data protection protocols, and UN standards on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client. The Consultant shall promptly notify COAR of any material ethical, safeguarding, data-protection, or security concern arising in the course of the assignment, while retaining responsibility for the independent professional judgment required to perform the Services safely and ethically.

All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client, subject to the terms of the applicable consultancy agreement, including any agreed provisions concerning pre-existing materials, third-party materials, research data, intellectual property, and permitted retention of records.
