jobs.title: PIR Caseworker
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:( 20.97$/hourly**): Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Needs Assessment Consultant - Venezuela
jobs.description:
Relief International (RI) is seeking an experienced consultant or consulting firm to conduct a comprehensive needs assessment following the recent earthquake in Venezuela. The assessment will inform RI's decision on whether and how to establish a rehabilitation-focused programme and longer-term presence in the country.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities affected by conflict, climate change, and disasters to save lives, strengthen resilience, and support long-term health and wellbeing. RI works across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, delivering programmes in Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Livelihoods.

**The Opportunity**

Following an earthquake that has impacted communities and health services in Venezuela, RI is exploring potential humanitarian interventions focused on physical rehabilitation and assistive technology. We are seeking a consultant or firm to lead an evidence-based assessment that will identify priority needs, evaluate existing services and referral pathways, assess market and supply-chain feasibility for assistive technologies, and provide practical recommendations for future programming.

The consultancy will include desk review, service mapping, primary data collection, analysis, stakeholder engagement, and final reporting.

**Scope of the Assessment**

The assessment will focus on:

- Rehabilitation needs of earthquake-affected populations.
- People with pre-existing disabilities whose access to care has been disrupted.
- Individuals with newly acquired impairments resulting from earthquake-related injuries.
- Access to physical rehabilitation services, prosthetics and orthotics (P&O), assistive technology, and relevant mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.
- Existing service capacity, referral pathways, and partnership opportunities.
- Market availability and feasibility of assistive technologies, including spectacles, hearing aids, and other priority devices.

**Key Responsibilities**

The successful consultant or firm will:

- Design and implement the assessment methodology.
- Conduct secondary data review and stakeholder mapping.
- Lead qualitative primary data collection, including key informant interviews and focus group discussions.
- Assess rehabilitation service availability, accessibility, and continuity of care.
- Evaluate assistive technology markets, suppliers, and supply chains.
- Analyze findings and identify priority needs and service gaps.
- Develop feasible programme options and recommendations for RI.
- Facilitate a validation workshop with RI stakeholders.
- Produce high-quality reports and decision-making materials.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

Essential

- Significant experience conducting humanitarian needs assessments, health assessments, disability inclusion assessments, or similar assignments.
- Strong technical expertise in physical rehabilitation and continuity of care.
- Knowledge of prosthetics and orthotics (P&O) services and assistive technology provision.
- Experience assessing health systems, referral pathways, service gaps, and partnership opportunities.
- Proven qualitative research and analytical skills.
- Demonstrated ability to develop practical programme recommendations and indicative costings.
- Excellent report-writing skills.
- Ability to work independently and manage assessment activities within tight deadlines.

Desirable

- Experience in Venezuela or comparable contexts in Latin America.
- Professional proficiency in Spanish and English.
- Experience working with rehabilitation providers, Ministries of Health, OPDs, or humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Experience assessing assistive technology markets and procurement pathways.
- Familiarity with HD-NEST, Washington Group Questions, or other disability-inclusive assessment tools.
- Experience supporting organizations entering new geographic contexts.

**Consultancy Details**

**Location:** Venezuela (assessment locations to be proposed and agreed with RI)
**Duration:** Approximately 7-8 weeks from contract signature
**Expected Period:** November to December 2026

**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

MSI needs an experienced and ambitious strategic partnerships leader to establish our new Global Strategic Partnerships team. Building on significant success with our existing strategic funder partners, they will deepen those partnerships and add at least 1-2 additional strategic funding partnerships by 2030. They will play a key role in advancing MSI’s brand and reputation through the lens of our high impact relationships – positioning MSI as one of the lead go-to INGOs for partners looking for audacious, bold, sector - shaping innovators and acting as a public advocate on the reasons why MSI is highly valued in this way.

MSI’s high-performing team has successfully grown relationships and funding portfolios with 2-3 large, impact-focused foundation funders, who collectively contribute £50m+/year to MSI’s donor funding and view MSI as their SRHR partner of choice. We are looking for a dynamic leader with a deep understanding of impact-focused funding, extensive connections across the social impact landscape and a track record of growing strategic funding partnerships with large, complex and highly engaged funders at the £10m+/year level, who can take MSI’s strategic funding partnerships to the next level, positioning MSI for growth and mission impact in a rapidly evolving funding landscape. Aligned with MSI’s ownblended social business delivery model, new strategic partners may come from a range of sectors including foundations, corporates, donor advised funds or public-private initiatives.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Deep understanding of social impact funder priorities and ways of working, especially those focused on maximising impact at scale.
- Proven ability to network, engage and co-create new high impact global partnerships at the highest level.
- Ability to work confidently across teams to accelerate delivery of priority, cross-cutting initiatives that meet the needs of strategic funders/corporate partners.
- Excellent communication skills - excellent verbal and written English communication skills and ability to organize and present information in a compelling way for a social impact leadership audience
- Strategic thinker with evidenced ability to influence funder future direction and maximise the alignment of funder and MSI strategies
- Strong coaching and capacity building skills

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Experience of securing and leading durable strategic funder partnerships at the £10m+ level
- Extensive network amongst international social impact funders and implementers
- Experience of leading and motivating high-performing teams
- Experience of working for or in partnership with a service delivery social impact organisation (the successful candidate may have worked on the funder side or implementer side)
- Excellent communication skills, including significant flair in written communication and a strong understanding of visual modelling and graphical representation of ideas. You will demonstrate the ability to shape responses to technically complex problems and ideas, whilst also being able to simply summarize the core concept/s.

**Formal education/qualification**

- No formal educational requirement, qualification through experience is sufficient for the role

Please see the job description [here](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Director-of-Global-Strategic-Partnerships-2026.pdf)

jobs.title: GBV/VAW Specialist Trainer - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**1. Background**

MiCT is implementing “Words That Protect” project that supports gender-responsive journalism and more responsible media coverage of violence against women in Iraq.

to strengthen collaborative journalism and gender-responsive reporting on violence against women (VAW) in Iraq. Component 2 combines media monitoring and baseline research, capacity building for Iraqi journalists, supported story production, and reflection on reporting practices.

The research examines how Iraqi media cover gender-based violence (GBV) and VAW, including terminology, framing, source selection, contextualisation, and the representation of survivors. Its findings will inform capacity-building activities and provide a reference for assessing reporting produced through the project.

MiCT seeks a GBV/VAW Expert and trainer to support the interpretation of research findings, review terminology and thematic accuracy, and deliver one day within the capacity-building workshop.

**2. Objective of the Assignment**

To strengthen the conceptual accuracy and survivor-centred approach of the project’s research interpretation and training, and improve participating journalists’ understanding of gender, GBV/VAW, and the social dynamics that shape violence against women in Iraq.

**3. Scope of Work**

The expert will undertake the following tasks in coordination with the Project Lead, research team, and lead trainer.

**A. Research interpretation and technical review — two working days**

Review the research findings with the research team to verify gender and GBV/VAW terminology, strengthen conceptual accuracy and interpretation in the Iraqi context, and identify key messages for training. Provide consolidated written feedback with recommended revisions.

**B. Training delivery — one working day**

Deliver 1 day training within the Component 2 workshop covering gender and power relations, forms and root causes of VAW, harmful norms and misconceptions, and survivor-centred principles, including consent, confidentiality, and avoiding secondary harm.

**C. Preparation and reporting — two working days**

Coordinate with the research team and lead trainer, prepare the session plan and supporting materials, and submit a concise report summarising the contribution, key observations, and recommendations.

The allocation of these two days between preparation and reporting will be agreed in the consultancy workplan.

**4. Deliverables**

Deliverables will be submitted to MiCT for review and acceptance in coordination with the Project Lead. Exact submission dates will be agreed in the consultancy workplan.

- **Research review feedback:** Consolidated comments on terminology, conceptual accuracy, and interpretation, with recommended revisions and key messages for training.
- **Training plan and materials:** A session plan, presentation, and practical exercises for the agreed training day.
- **Delivery of one training day:** Facilitation of the agreed gender and GBV/VAW sessions within the capacity-building workshop.
- **Final assignment report:** A concise summary of support delivered, key observations, and recommendations.

**6. Coordination and Responsibilities**

The expert will work under the supervision of the Project Lead and coordinate closely with the research team and lead trainer. MiCT will provide relevant research materials, the workshop framework, participant information, and project templates.

**7. Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Relevant academic qualification in gender studies, social sciences, human rights, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender equality, GBV/VAW, and survivor-centred approaches.
- Strong understanding of the Iraqi context, including social norms and barriers faced by survivors.
- Experience reviewing research findings and translating complex concepts into accessible learning materials.
- Experience designing and delivering participatory training for adult audiences.
- Excellent spoken and written Arabic.
- Ability to coordinate with the project team and review relevant materials in English.

Previous work with journalists or media development programmes is an advantage. Journalism expertise is not required.

**8. Confidentiality and Ethical Standards**

The expert must maintain the confidentiality of unpublished research, project documents, and participant information. All contributions must uphold survivor dignity, privacy, informed consent, and the Do No Harm principle. Training examples must avoid disclosing identifying or sensitive information about survivors.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Logistics Officer provides operational and administrative support to the Country Office and all field offices, focusing on procurement, rental and lease agreements, logistics-related payments, cost tracking, and documentation. The role ensures accurate and timely processing of procurement and payment requests, compliance with organizational procedures and donor requirements, and effective communication with field teams, Finance, suppliers, and service providers.

This varied role, will require a high-level of organisational, communication and IT skills to provide a key central support function to various teams: HR, Finance and the Field teams, in particular the Field Programme Officers (FPO).

The role supports the Country Office and all field offices with administrative and operational duties. This includes performing a variety of administrative tasks, including management of office and accommodation contracts, management of the office administration.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

1\. **Commitment to NP Principles:**

- Demonstrate a commitment to NP’s mandate and principles.
- Maintain a positive image of the organisation full-time while communicating with external actors, staff or operating in the field.

2\. **Support to Logistics:**

- Process procurement of goods and services valued below USD 10,000 for the Country Office and all field offices, including simple procurement and procedures requiring BID analysis.
- Research the market, collect and compare supplier quotations, and update the vendor list to support purchasing decisions.
- Arrange procurement for office facilities and premises-related needs, compare options for value for money, and prepare the required contractual documentation.
- Check facility-related contracts and service providers, follow up on service quality and delivery issues, and report any non-compliance with agreed terms.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for utilities, facility services, consumables, and office supplies required by the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare vehicle lease agreements for the Country Office and all NP field offices, follow up on negotiations and signatures, and track renewals and contract implementation.
- Follow up on payments under fuel supply agreements for vehicle refuelling across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Arrange and track payments for vehicle servicing, maintenance, and repairs for the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for rented premises, including offices, hubs, and guesthouses, across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Check that payment processing and supporting documents comply with NP policies, procurement procedures, delegated approval limits, contractual terms, and donor requirements where applicable.
- Prepare monthly requests and supporting documents for office-related costs, including rent, utilities, telephone services, and other recurring charges, and check them for completeness and compliance with organizational procedures.
- Support monthly cost planning and forecasting by collecting and consolidating information on rent, utilities, facility services, fuel, vehicle maintenance, and other recurring logistics expenses across the Country Office and field offices.
- Track submitted, pending, overdue, and completed payments; follow up on delays with Finance and suppliers; and update the relevant trackers and stakeholders.
- Check invoices and payment requests against the relevant contract, purchase order, delivery or service confirmation, approved budget, and payment terms; clarify discrepancies before submission.
- File payment and procurement records in the relevant SharePoint folders and provide required hard copies to Finance, including BID analyses and payment tracking documents.
- Compile and verify procurement records and update the Purchase Request (PR) tracker with the latest status.
- File logistics documents in the relevant SharePoint folders and arrange for required hard copies to be retained by Finance, including BID analyses, payment documents, and payment trackers.
- Maintain a consolidated payment calendar for recurring and contractual costs, track due dates, and notify relevant colleagues of upcoming deadlines or missing documents.
- Carry out other logistics duties assigned by the Senior Logistics Officer or Logistics Coordinator\*\*.\*\*

3\. **Support to Administration:**

- Update tracking tools and databases for recurring monthly costs, procurement progress, lease agreements, and other operational records.
- Serve as the contact point for office and accommodation lease agreements and related technical services, and assist with drafting and reviewing rental contracts.
- Check contract balances, advance payments, deposits, and outstanding liabilities for assigned services and premises, and flag discrepancies and upcoming renewals or expiries in good time.
- Collect and consolidate monthly payment requests from field offices, check submissions for completeness and consistency, and return incomplete or unclear requests to the relevant focal points for correction.
- Keep in regular contact with Field Team Leaders and FPOs to identify upcoming operational needs, confirm expected costs, resolve documentation issues, and support the timely submission of payment requests.
- Inform Field Team Leaders, FPOs, and relevant budget holders about payment delays, contract or supplier issues, missing approvals, and actions required from them.
- Send documents to the relevant teams and follow up to ensure they reach the appropriate staff for review, approval, and filing.
- Prepare complete and accurate payment packages for Finance, checking that supporting documents are available, approvals are in place, and payment details are correct.
- Liaise with Finance and budget holders to check budget availability, budget codes and donor allocations, required approvals, and the status of submitted payments.
- Provide administrative assistance to the Logistics team as required.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- High school diploma.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft applications, in particular Word & Excel, other applications an asset. High level of computer literacy, knowledge of Salesforce a significant benefit.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- Experience working in NP or similar organisation.
- Familiarity with INGO logistics and administration structure and function with preferred experience within NP.

**KEY CHALLENGES:**

- Building and sustaining collaborative partnerships, negotiating, and resolving contentious issues and conflicts of interest while managing and balancing varied, diverse stakeholder priorities across a geographically dispersed region.

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

- Experience in I/NGO administration, office management, procurement and/or logistics.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in English and Ukrainian.
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a team and independently.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Independent Judgment/Analytical: Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

- This country office position includes travel to field locations (Kramatorsk, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Kherson) and may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable and changeable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic accommodation, which may include shared housing during travel and field site support tasks.
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols and maintain high level of discipline.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) [Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

jobs.title: DRC Accounting & Payments Coordinator (Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

The Accounting & Payments Coordinator supports One Acre Fund DRC’s operations by ensuring timely, accurate and properly authorized payments, complete expense documentation, and reliable financial records across all program sites.

## **Responsibilities**

Payment Processing

- Review payment requests submitted by departments to verify their completeness, accuracy, supporting documentation and required approvals, in accordance with internal policies.
- Determine the appropriate payment method—bank transfer, cheque, cash or an approved mobile money channel—based on internal procedures, transaction requirements, security considerations and available funds.
- Prepare bank transfers, cheques and other payment instructions for authorized approval and release;
- Monitor payments through to confirmation, investigate failed or delayed transactions, and retain proof of payment.
- Support Procurement in assessing supplier payment arrangements, including payment methods, advances and payment upon delivery
- Keep requesting departments informed of payment status, missing requirements and anticipated delays, including changes affecting agreed service timelines.

Expense Documentation and Advance Reconciliation

- Maintain a tracker of staff and supplier advances, including responsible parties, supporting documentation requirements, reconciliation deadlines and outstanding balances.
- Collect and review advance reconciliations and expense reports to confirm that expenditure is supported by a complete, valid and consistent documentation package.
- Follow up with suppliers on outstanding invoices, billing discrepancies and requests for clarification, coordinating with Procurement and requesting departments as needed.
- Escalate overdue reconciliations, unresolved discrepancies and recurring documentation gaps to the manager.
- Maintain an organized and accessible archive of payment and expense records, linking requests, approvals, invoices, receipts, reconciliation forms and proof of payment in accordance with document retention requirements.

Cash Management

- Coordinate approved cash allocations and transfers between sites to support operational needs while maintaining appropriate transaction records.
- Act as custodian of the Kinshasa office cashbox, ensuring secure custody of funds, disbursement against approved documentation, timely recording of transactions and daily cash balancing.
- Identify practical opportunities to reduce cash usage and promote approved electronic payment methods without disrupting field operations.

Account Reconciliation

- Prepare monthly reconciliations for all country bank and cash accounts, including across all sites, within the agreed closing calendar.
- Perform weekly reconciliations of sales collections received through mobile money, where applicable, against transaction records and related settlements.
- Maintain accurate accounting trackers, including the lease repository, fixed asset register, register of non-capitalized equipment, etc.
- Provide complete and timely supporting documentation and explanations to the Global Accounting team for transaction recording, monthly closing and financial reporting.
- Respond to accounting queries and coordinate corrections with the Global Accounting team, seeking the manager’s guidance on complex or judgment-based matters.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- SYCEBNL knowledge and application
- Excel / Google Sheets proficiency
- Process implementation and improvement
- Attention to detail and financial control judgment
- Stakeholder coordination

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

1 year

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

28 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Technical Partner for the Next-Gen Climate Cooperative in Jigawa State
jobs.description:
## Background

Pathfinder International, through its women-led innovation platform Women&Co, seeks a technical partner (“the Consultant”) to lead the climate methodology, community data system, technical facilitation and evidence synthesis for the Next-Gen Climate Cooperative (NCC) pilot in Jigawa State, from November 2026 to June 2027.

NCC is a women-led climate resilience initiative working at the intersection of climate, health and leadership. It positions women as climate data collectors, entrepreneurs and advisors to government rather than as beneficiaries. Jigawa faces annual flooding along the Hadejia River, drought and land degradation, and women make up most of its farm workforce but are rarely part of climate planning.

The pilot runs in 2 Local Government Areas (LGAs) with about 60 core participants (about 30 per LGA), drawn from existing women’s and youth groups, trained as community climate data collectors. The pilot tests a lean, locally anchored NCC model to establish what it is, what it costs, what works and what can be replicated. It is aligned with the draft Jigawa State Climate Change Policy and is implemented with the Ministries of Health, Environment and Climate Change and Women Affairs and Social Development.

The pilot’s first learning cycle is the NCC Jigawa Climate Information Sprint, which asks: is useful climate information reaching women in time to act? It follows women from receiving climate information, to understanding and trusting it, acting on it and seeing results, and identifies the barriers and support gaps that remain, across agriculture, heat and health, and water and flooding. The Consultant will build the data system behind the sprint and an interactive NCC Jigawa Climate Information Dashboard that presents its findings, alongside women’s own stories, for the pilot team, State partners and funders. The dashboard is a Climate Information Sprint prototype and is not intended to be the final Jigawa Climate Dashboard.

## Objectives of the assignment

The Consultant will provide the technical backbone of the pilot. Specifically, the assignment will:

1. Ground the pilot in a sound understanding of local climate risk and livelihoods in the 2 pilot LGAs.
2. Equip participants with practical climate leadership and community data skills.
3. Build a simple, women-operated community climate data system and an interactive dashboard that answer the Climate Information Sprint questions.
4. Turn community evidence into practical climate and livelihood solutions and into policy-relevant messages for the State.
5. Document what the NCC technical model involves, what worked, and what is needed to replicate it.

Download the full RFP document through the link below

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ynylVrMAUpXbQmRxT0GZFVqPRuA-xyAm/view?usp=drive_link

jobs.title: Regional Emergency Response Advisor (Asia)
jobs.description:
***Job Summary***

The STRIDES Regional Emergency Response Advisor supports outbreak response planning, coordination, and implementation across Asia, ideally bringing prior experience with high-consequence pathogens. The advisor aligns country programs with STRIDES leadership’s direction, tracking and reporting on response efforts while leading coordination with technical, finance, and operations teams to mobilize resources. They develop tools and guidance, and work within established incident management frameworks to strengthen emergency readiness and execution. In addition, this person will manage the creation of knowledge products—reports, technical materials, and conflict-sensitive solutions. Working with project teams and HQ, the advisor leads program evaluations on effectiveness, reviews technical/operational activities, and directs assessment reports across their portfolio. The role also contributes to business development, including pursuing opportunities, capture/proposal leadership, and building partnerships. This position will be based either in Manila, Bangkok, or Jakarta.

## ***Accountabilities:***

**Technical Requirements:**

- Leads outbreak response and preparedness activities in alignment with established STRIDES emergency response protocols and in-country incident management systems.
- Manages the coordination of day-to-day response activities across technical, operational, and administrative teams to ensure alignment with response objectives and timelines.
- Oversees the consolidation of response information and manages internal coordination during active outbreaks.
- Leads standardization of response processes across their portfolio of countries, including reporting templates, deployment trackers, and coordination tools.
- Spreadheads continuous improvement of emergency response systems by integrating lessons learned and best practices into tools and guidance.
- Provides project staff with overall technical direction and guidance in line with the project expected outcomes.
- Leads analysis of project implementation to identify areas for improvement and propose appropriate technical strategy and guidelines.
- Manages the collaboration with the research and evaluation team to report on data and assessments.
- Leads the development and dissemination of tools, materials, reports, papers, and intervention for research projects.
- Serves as the authoritative on emergency response and preparedness best practices to assist with implementation
- Reviews technical work plans and budgets for accuracy and aligned with the STRIDES program and donor goals.

**Project Design Implementation:**

- Mentors and provides technical guidance to junior emergency response staff and partners across the region; may supervise junior technical staff, sub-contractors, and others implementing technical project work.
- With technical oversight, provide technical leadership in design, development, planning, implementation; and capacity- building of specific technical components of projects
- Creates technical portion of the project plan, within the given resource and financial constraints
- Directs the day-to-day technical and operational activities of assigned projects, tracking delivery of project outputs and monitoring staff members' LOE (Level of Effort) needs to ensure adequate coverage of resources.
- Coordinates requests from CO (Country Office) for technical assistance
- Engages in the design, development, planning, and implementation of global-level innovative technical strategies.
- Develops or writes technical briefs, reports, or other necessary materials to facilitate research, best practices, policies, and procedures.
- Leads collaboration with the DTT (Digital Transformation & Technology) team to develop and maintain response tracking systems (e.g., dashboards, trackers, logs) to support situational awareness and decision-making.
- Oversees the adaption and maintenance of tools, templates, SOPs (standard operating procedures), guidance notes, and job aids to support outbreak preparedness and response activities, ensuring implementation is consistent with best practices in the industry/subject and meets client/funder contractual obligations.

**Business Development and Client/Funder Support:**

- Maintains collaborative relationships with donor/client organizations, relevant government agencies, bilateral and other NGOs (non governmental organizations) and consistently maintained and viewed as a knowledgeable resource in their technical area.
- Leads proposal research and development proposal strategies, which consists of directing proposal research, data collection, and strategies.
- Reviews proposal, budgets, and workplans.
- Participate in client / funder meetings and provide technical input, and drafts sponsor reports and presentations
- Represents the organization and / or Institute to external entities at professional meetings and conferences.

**Capacity Building, Training and Supervision:**

- Develops and implements technical training and capacity building interventions related to emergency response and preparedness.
- Supervises and/or provide technical guidance to staff members locally and in the region.

**Operations Management (Finance, HR, etc.):**

- Manages the processes, services, planning, organizing, coordinating, and controlling of all technical resources for a project.
- Directs efforts to work with the Finance Team to develop and track response budgets, spending forecasts, and cost monitoring in coordination with finance teams.
- Oversees the processing of emergency procurement requests, consultant deployments, and surge staffing needs.
- Ensures the overall project portfolio remains aligned with organizational timelines, technical standards, and donor/client expectations, holding junior technical officers accountable for work plan execution.
- Manages the timelines of multiple projects and budgets, leading the development of donor reports and presentations.
- Proposes and executes solutions to operational resource gaps and constraints
- Reviews SOPs (standard operating procedures), SOW (statement of work), and reports on technical and financial tracking data.
- Cultivates supplier relationships to ensure rapid procurements for outbreak response

**Project/Program Reporting:**

- Organizes processes with the MEL Team to track outbreak response activities, milestones, deliverables, and resource utilization across response pillars or workstreams.
- Reviews regular situation reports, activity summaries, and operational updates for leadership, partners, and donors as required.
- Manages the timely and accurate documentation of response actions, lessons learned, and after-action inputs.
- Oversees SOWs and budget tracking systems
- Drafts sponsor financial and technical reports.
- Collates and uploads output and deliverables data to sponsor data systems.
- Prepares and delivers presentations to sponsors on progress.
- Helps in the development and review of country work plans.

**Quality Assurance:**

- Ensures technical deliverables are consistent with best practices in the industry / subject and meet client / funder contractual obligations
- Identifies areas for improved efficiency or effectiveness within prescribed parameters, and institutes enhancements to procedures.

## ***Applied Knowledge & Skills:***

- Ensures appropriate and timely technical support for field projects.
- Ensures the quality of implemented technical activities and systems at all levels. Conducts routine coordination with employees and consultants, on-site and in the field.
- Strong knowledge and skills in a specific technical area/function and general understanding of concepts and principles of related technical areas/functions.
- Solid knowledge of standards for the technical area/field, operational processes and procedures, work, and task flow.
- Has the ability to manage projects, set realistic priorities, and plan for the successful implementation of activities.
- Proficient writing and verbal communication skills.
- Relevant computer software skills (including, at a minimum, the standard applications in MS Office).
- Ability to manage their own work to job and performance standards.
- Must be able to read, write and speak fluent English fluent in host country language. Other languages would be helpful, including: Georgian, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Nepali, Bengali, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, Filipino, or Indonesian.

## ***Competencies:***

There are 31 FHI 360 development competencies, of greatest focus for this particular job will be:

- Project Management (Planning and Time Management) - Accurately scopes out length and difficulty of tasks (sets objectives/goals/measures). Breaks down work into steps, schedules, task/people assignments. Marshals people, time, and resources efficiently. Arranges information in a useful manner and orchestrates multiple activities at once.
- People Management (Making Others Great) – Facilitate professional development of staff by providing challenging, learning assignments and opportunities. Shares and solicits feedback monthly at the very least. Helps establish compelling development plans. Assigns responsibility and accountability for tasks/decisions. Monitors process, progress, and results. Creates a climate in which people want to do their best.
- Creating and Managing Systems and Processes – Recognizes the need for standardization and balances client and organization need in systems design. Anticipates the effects of process change on people while optimizing task efficiency and simplicity.
- Employees are expected to possess or have high potential for the development of these three fundamental competencies.

## ***Problem Solving & Impact:***

- Demonstrates the ability to assess needs within agreed upon duties and considers course of action best to meet those needs.
- Effectively applies knowledge of technical area to solve a range of problems. Demonstrates the ability to develop solutions to problems that cannot be solved using existing methods or approaches.
- Faulty decisions/ recommendations /failures to complete assignments will normally result in serious delays to assigned projects resulting in considerable expenditure of additional time, resources, and funds.
- Decisions and actions impact primarily workflow, project processes and timeframes. Problems encountered are varied, requiring review of practices and precedents to resolve. Problem solving involves evaluating and resolving discrepancies with data, analyses, processes, etc. within prescribed guidelines.
- Policies or guidelines exist for most problems; others must be referred to by a supervisor or more senior professional.

## ***Supervision Given/Received:***

- May supervise junior staff members.
- Coordinates own workflow and sets individual priorities.
- Works under general guidelines for completion and accuracy as determined by the supervisor.
- Accomplishes results through lower-level staff managers or through experienced staff who exercise independence in their assignments.
- May manage a centralized functional area of activity.
- Serves as mentor to more inexperienced technical staff.

## ***Education:***

- Master’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Knowledge/Information Services, Communications, Education, Environment, Health, Behavioral, Life/Social Sciences International Development, Human Development or Related Field.
- Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.

## ***Experience:***

- Typically requires 8+ years of relevant experience in technical implementation of large projects and/or programs – may manage activities of lower-level staff, however, main function is individual contributor.
- Documented experience providing technical assistance, capacity building and business development in the specific technical domain.
- Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or private organization.
- International or Domestic (US) Program Development or Program management preferred.
- In-depth knowledge of concepts, practices and procedures associated with outbreak emergency response, with a focus on high consequence pathogens.
- Development of scope of work and deliverables for partners, consultants, etc.
- Broader knowledge of incident management (IM) structures, emergency response frameworks, and quality standards for outbreak response
- Has sensitivity to cultural differences and understanding of political, contextual, and ethical issues.
- Must be able to read, write and speak fluent English fluent in host country language. Other languages would be helpful, including: Georgian, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Nepali, Bengali, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, Filipino, or Indonesian.
- Excellent organizational and analytical skills.
- Ability to influence and collaborate with others.
- Ability to analyze and interpret data, identify errors, and prepare reports.
- Ability to solve problems and implement corrective action as needed.

## ***Typical Physical Demands***\*\*:\*\*

- Typical office environment.
- Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
- Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
- Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.

## ***Technology to be Used***\*\*:\*\*

- Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

## ***Travel Requirements:***

- Up to 35%

***The expected hiring salary range for this role is PHP 2,500,000 - 3,500,000 for annual basic salary. When determining an offer amount, FHI 360 factors in multiple considerations, including but not limited to: relevant years of experience and education possessed by the applicant, internal equity, market pay, and budget. For internal candidates, salary placement will also follow FHI 360’s current promotional increase guidelines.***
