L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

**Job Overview**

Airbel is IRC's innovation lab. We work alongside people affected by conflict and crisis to design services that are more useful, more dignified, and more likely to last. This role puts a designer in the middle of that work in West and Central Africa, close to the communities, the frontline workers, and the questions that decide whether a product or service actually helps someone.

You will be our eyes and hands in the field. You will run the design research, interact with clients and providers, notice what they do and why, and turn what you find into prototypes you test and refine on the ground. You will work closely with the Human Centered Design Lead, who will support synthesis and concept development as you shape your own work.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Run design research in the field: interviews, observation, and time spent with clients and frontline workers.
- Stay close to one geography or work stream long enough to notice the patterns that only show up over time.
- Make sense of what you see on the ground, and find the sparks of innovation already present in people's own workarounds and ideas.
- Turn research into prototypes, test them with real users, and iterate as you learn rather than following a fixed script.
- Bring what you learn back in a form the team can use: clear notes, visuals, journey maps, whatever makes the insight legible.
- Partner with country program teams, technical leads, and frontline staff with care and respect, earning the access that good research depends on.
- Work across francophone West and Central Africa, and other humanitarian settings as needed, adapting quickly to new contexts and teams.

**Job Requirements**

**Work Experience**

We would like to see how you think and work, including:

- Experience doing research with people, in any setting: design research, ethnography, UX or product research, participatory or action research, or any other kind of qualitative research. What matters is that you went past a script to understand why people do what they do.
- You have built or set up something (a service, a small pilot, a tool, an app, even a rough paper version of an idea), tested it with the people it was for, and changed it based on what you learned. We call this prototyping, but you do not need to have used the word.
- A way of noticing opportunities in the everyday: workarounds, small details, and the things people have already figured out for themselves.
- Something that shows how you think: a portfolio, a case study, a research write-up, photos of a prototype, or a project you helped shape. It does not need to be polished, but we would like to see your thinking in some form.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong research skills: you can plan and run fieldwork, talk with anyone, hold ethics with people in vulnerable situations, and read a situation for what it is telling you, with care in how you gather and record what you find.
- Strong prototype testing skills: You build rough, test early, and change things during testing rather than waiting for a finished version.
- Real curiosity about why people behave as they do, and the judgment to find the spark of an idea inside it.
- Comfort in the field: You can spend two weeks at a stretch in a field site and do good work there.
- Adaptability across cultures, languages, and changing plans, held together by humility and care for the people you work with.

**Language Skills**

Working French and English, enough of both to do research and to work with teams elsewhere on the continent. Proposals and presentations can be written in either language and translated.

**Preferred experience & skills**

- An eye for making insights legible through visuals, maps and simple decks.
- Experience in humanitarian, health, or community settings.

**Work Authorization**

Candidates must have the legal right to work in the country where the position is based

**Working Environment**

This role is based in an IRC country office in DRC, Nigeria, or Chad, with a standard office setup. The work involves regular travel, up to 40%, to sites across humanitarian settings, in the region and globally. A design research or prototyping visit can mean two weeks at a time in places that are remote, low-resource, and sometimes insecure, with basic accommodation, limited connectivity, and long days. If being close to where the work happens is the part that draws you in, this is a role built for that.

jobs.title: Oficial WASI - Santa Bárbara del Zulia
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial WASI** altamente calificado con sede en **Santa Barbara, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Base, y acompañamiento técnico del Especialista de SWI (Shelter, WASH & Infrastructure) el Oficial de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH) estará directamente involucrado y velará por la implementación diaria de las actividades WASH en las áreas de intervención conforme a los estándares humanitarios y regulaciones nacionales aplicables. Asegurará la ejecución oportuna y de calidad de las actividades de asistencia humanitaria, incluyendo evaluaciones de necesidades, distribuciones de insumos, promoción de higiene, fortalecimiento comunitario y mejoras de infraestructura WASH. Asimismo, apoyará la coordinación con autoridades, líderes comunitarios y otros actores humanitarios para garantizar una respuesta integrada, centrada en la protección y alineada con los estándares humanitarios aplicables.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

- Liderar las evaluaciones de necesidades relacionadas con el agua, el saneamiento y la higiene en las comunidades de acogida, instituciones y otros sitios de interés en las zonas de interés, según las instrucciones del Gerente de Base y bajo la gestión técnica del especialista de SWI y el equipo MEAL.
- Ayudar en la identificación y selección de las comunidades, beneficiarios o centros de intervención en coordinación con las autoridades locales y en conjunto con los equipos de Protección, Recuperación Económica y Preparación para Desastres.
- Planificar y coordinar la ejecución de actividades WASH en los sitios de intervención, asegurando la participación y apoyo de autoridades y entes locales relacionados, socios locales, comunidades, otros equipos dentro de DRC y demás interesados, asegurando estrategias de sostenibilidad de las acciones.
- Brindar orientación técnica y estratégica para el diseño, planificación e implementación de actividades WASH, así como para la gestión de recursos asociados a la respuesta ante fenómenos naturales, incluidos eventos relacionados con El Niño e inundaciones, en comunidades de acogida / instituciones.
- Planificar en conjunto con los socios locales de DRC la ejecución de las actividades de los programas WASH, garantizando el fortalecimiento de capacidades y la transferencia de capacidades a los socios, con las orientaciones del Gerente de Base y el Especialista SWI, siguiendo los lineamientos de cada proyecto.
- Garantizar que las comunidades y grupos vulnerables y/o con riesgos de protección, incluidas las mujeres, participen en cada una de las etapas del ciclo de los proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Servir de enlace con otros actores/ONG relevantes y representantes de las personas de interés y líderes comunitarios para los esfuerzos de colaboración, incluyendo la participación en las reuniones de coordinación local de grupos temáticos sobre agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Realizar las gestiones para la obtención de los permisos necesarios ante las autoridades y entes necesarios para la ejecución de obras y otras actividades en los lugares de intervención, en conjunto con el Gerente de Base y con el apoyo técnico del Especialista SWI.
- Participar en los espacios de coordinación dentro de DRC con los equipos de otros sectores programáticos como Recuperación Económica, Protección y Preparación para Desastres, para garantizar la implementación integrada con una planificación adecuada de las actividades.
- Garantizar que todas las partes interesadas relevantes tengan información sobre los antecedentes, el programa, los objetivos, las áreas de trabajo, la duración de los programas y las actividades en el campo de la organización.
- Realizar un seguimiento y preparar semanalmente, mensualmente, trimestralmente, todos los planes de compras de bienes y servicios necesarios para el programa de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Administrar de manera efectiva la ejecución física y financiera de los proyectos de WASH utilizando las herramientas adecuadas para garantizar que estos se entreguen a tiempo, dentro del presupuesto y cumpliendo con la calidad y otros requisitos técnicos esperados.
- Desarrollar materiales de información y comunicación asociados a la higiene/saneamiento y sensibilización para personas con necesidades específicas (PDE), los desplazados internos y las comunidades de acogida las zonas seleccionadas, de conformidad con la cultura y las prácticas de la población.
- Preparar el plan de trabajo de las actividades de promoción de higiene y fortalecimiento de capacidades en consulta con el Gerente de Base y del Especialista SWI.
- Facilitar todas las capacitaciones/campañas sobre agua, saneamiento e higiene en terreno mediante el uso de un enfoque participativo y orientado al cambio de comportamiento.
- Planificar, ejecutar y documentar la distribución de las entregas de kits e insumos WASH en los lugares de intervención, garantizando la calidad, trazabilidad y rendición de cuentas del proceso.
- Preparar oportunamente especificaciones técnicas y requerimientos para adquisiciones y contrataciones para su revisión y aprobación por el Especialista WASH y realizar las solicitudes de compra de bienes y servicios al equipo de Soporte. Esto incluye contenidos de kits, especificaciones técnicas, estimaciones de cantidades de obra, presupuestos base y otros documentos técnicos para intervenciones de infraestructura WASH.
- Supervisar obras de rehabilitación o construcción de infraestructuras de WASH, asegurando la calidad técnica de las obras ejecutadas y verificando el cumplimiento de estándares técnicos.
- Documentar adecuadamente la ejecución financiera de las obras de infraestructura y llevar la documentación de administración de contratos de las obras.
- Garantizar la recopilación de datos de los beneficiarios, documentar historias de éxito y otra información que sea requerida para el reporte de las actividades e indicadores de cada proyecto, y suministrar aportes para los informes de progreso o finales que son enviados a los donantes u otras partes interesadas.
- Documentar los resultados y las lecciones aprendidas de la implementación del programa de agua, saneamiento e higiene, considerando la retroalimentación de las comunidades y de otros equipos técnicos de DRC y partes interesadas.
- Contribuir a la planificación de contingencias para la preparación y una posible respuesta de emergencia en materia de agua, saneamiento e higiene, si es necesario.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el equipo de agua, saneamiento e higiene.

EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:

- 2 años de experiencia en el campo de WASH y en la implementación de proyectos humanitarios.
- Sólida comprensión de la capacitación básica en programación de agua, saneamiento e higiene, métodos de promoción participativa, movilizaciones comunitarias y creación de redes.
- Buen manejo de normas, estándares y prácticas sobre obras de construcción y/o rehabilitación de sistemas básicos esenciales de agua, saneamiento e higiene en instituciones o comunidades, incluyendo sistemas de agua, sistemas de disposición de excretas, manejo de residuos, entre otros.
- Conocimiento sobre las prácticas adecuadas de gestión de residuos y saneamiento, métodos de tratamiento de agua a nivel domiciliario y otras prácticas de higiene para evitar riesgos de salud pública.
- Experiencia en la implementación de actividades de formación, promoción de higiene y formación de comités en temas relacionados con agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Título en Ingeniería en Salud Pública/Ingeniería Civil/Ingeniería Mecánica/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente con experiencia en WASH.
- Conocimientos informáticos y gestión de datos estadísticos.
- Implementación efectiva y oportuna de todas las intervenciones descritas en el producto y cualquier otra actividad programática relacionada con el agua, el saneamiento y la higiene.
- Experiencia laboral y conocimiento del lugar de destino local.
- Capacidad de adaptarse a situaciones cambiantes según sea necesario.
- Capacidad de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.

Deseable

- Maestría o especialización en Ingeniería de Salud Pública, Ingeniería Hidráulica, Ingeniería Ambiental, Ingeniería Civil, Ingeniería Mecánica, Arquitectura o campo directamente relacionado;
- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de protección;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de crear buen ambiente de equipo y trabajo con socios locales implementadores;
- Manejo del inglés;
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**EDUCACIÓN:**

- Título en Ingeniería en Salud Pública/Ingeniería Civil/Ingeniería Mecánica/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente con experiencia en WASH.

**IDIOMAS:**

- Fluidez en español; manejo del inglés es una ventaja.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**

jobs.title: Senior Pricing Advisor, World Bank
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery & Development department (CRRD) leads and delivers the IRC’s work in crisis-affected contexts around the world. In the last year, we served approaching 20M crisis-affected people with high quality humanitarian programming. This was achieved by over 12,000 staff across 300 offices in 40+ countries, working to deliver more than 600 individual grants and contracts.

The Awards Management Unit (AMU) within CRRD is responsible for identifying, securing and managing funding from government donors for the IRC. AMU is a bridge between donors and the IRC’s work on the ground. The team leads donor engagement, provides expert technical advice to colleagues delivering our services around the world, ensures consistency and compliance with donor policies and procedures, and manages associated risk. They also support all IRC staff working on awards from government donors and partners.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, United Kingdom and Germany.

***Global Business Development***

Within the Awards Management Unit, the Global BD team leads IRC’s public BD strategy and donor engagement for IRC’s international programs. The team brings together capacity across the organization to drive donor engagement and BD services to secure the public funding needed to deliver our work to clients. The team includes technical, operational and donor specialists able to lead our most complex proposals and manage our most important donor relationships.

**Purpose of the Role**

The Senior Pricing Advisor will join a global BD team and will help drive IRC’s new business development efforts- particularly with, but not limited to the World Bank- by engaging with global, regional, country, and financial staff throughout the business development cycle. The role provides essential guidance, technical assistance, quality assurance and hands-on support throughout the business development lifecycle, ensuring a delicate balance between cost recovery, risk mitigation, price competitiveness, and compliance with internal policies and donor regulations.

The ideal candidate will have significant, high-level experience in pricing for complex or high-value opportunities, with extensive experience working with the World Bank. . Knowledge of other multilateral organizations and bilateral donors, such as FCDO, BMZ, AFD, is also highly desirable.

As a key member of proposal teams, this position collaborates closely with IRC Country Offices, Finance Department, and Technical Units to facilitate the development of cost proposals.

**Responsibilities**

**Capture & Program Design**

- Serve as the ‘Capture Pricing Lead’ to ensure IRC is well prepared to develop an effective budget proposal for important funding opportunities, particularly with, but not limited to proposals for the World Bank and other Multilateral Devt Banks
- Conduct research and evaluation of cost drivers specific to each country to understand cost proposal development challenges and opportunities to improve pricing strategies within the predefined clients’ needs and regulations.
- Aggregate all available budgetary details at the activity level, encompassing all anticipated interventions and necessary support provisions, into clear rough estimates.

**Pricing Strategy & Budget Development**

- Lead Budget Development and/or provide quality assurance or backstopping for budgeting for major proposals.
- Review released solicitations to assess whether cost-related considerations might hinder the development of a competitive, compliant, and viable bid
- Provide pricing expertise to the donor budget proposal process to ensure proposals are of high quality; reflect the needs of the solicitation and include the necessary shared costs.
- Ensure the proposal team understands the financial requirements and donor regulations of the bid, by clearly communicating what is required and providing guidance and support as needed.Identify all key financial and commercial risks and proactively propose a tailored mitigation plan and adjustments as necessary.
- Drive and/or ensure that pricing inputs from IRC Country Offices, technical or other contributors are integrated effectively. Lead all aspects of detailed cost, and technical queries in anticipation of submission timelines.
- Maintain, expand and apply technical knowledge in World Bank by attending educational workshops and trainings, reviewing the latest donors’ regulations and policies and market trends
- Offer guidance and strategies for creating intricate budgets, presenting cost-related aspects efficiently and effectively, developing payment by results structures and fee payment schedules
- Develop comprehensive donor budgets in line with internal and external requirements, ensuring that all cost drivers are adequately considered, drawing input from different collaborators.
- Engage with and provide technical guidance to partners, and integrate all partner pricing inputs into the consolidated budget, budget narrative, and overall cost application
- When required, develop or adapt budget development tools, guidance and materials for existing and new donors and contractual mechanisms
- When required, conduct cost reviews of selected proposals
- Ensure adherence to IRC's standard processes and policies, as well as compliance with solicitation requirements and client policies across a variety of opportunities and donors.

**Strategic Pricing and Capacity Building**

- As a donor budgeting expert, the Pricing Advisor will be invited to contribute to wider organizational initiatives to improve pricing approaches and capacity in the organzation. This may include, the development or review of pricing tools, templates or strategies.
- Support training and other capacity development initiatives to strengthen organizational donor pricing approaches
- Participate in learning initiatives, including After Action Reviews to ensure IRC continuously improves its pricing approaches.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

- Demonstrable experience developing cost proposals. Demonstrable experience developing cost proposals for grant and contract types including Payment by Results approaches and fee rate structures.\*
- Minimum of 5 years’ experience preparing proposals, with a background at an INGO or a commercial organization.\*
- Demonstrates in depth understanding of World Bank financial rules and regulations; is able to identify donor-specific risks and design cost proposals in a way that mitigates those risks. \*
- Flexible work attitude: the ability to work in an inclusive team environment, independently and ability to meet unexpected demands.
- Demonstrates ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues in ‘remote’ and complementary teams.
- Excellent inter-personal skills and able to communicate clearly and concisely complex financial information with diverse set of stakeholders.
- Strong organizational and work prioritization skills, and ability to focus and pay attention to details.
- Able to plan ahead and manage a complex and diverse workload with tight deadlines
- Ability to travel internationally; (up to 20% of time).
- Ability to work autonomously and under remote management.
- Proficient in written and spoken English is required; fluency in French is strongly preferred.

**Compensation (United Kingdom):** (GBP 52,210 - GBP 61,999 - annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal opportunity employer**

IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

jobs.title: UNE EXPERTE OU UN EXPERT ENQUÊTE NUTRITIONNELLE SMART- RCA
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable de Département Ssanté et Nutrition, votre mission sera de mettre en place fournir une expertise technique à la mission ACF RCA, pour la réalisation d'une enquête SMART nutritionnelle dans le District Sanitaire de Bouca.
L'objectif de cette enquête est d'évaluer la situation nutritionnelle des enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois dans le DS de Bouca, ainsi que le taux de mortalité rétrospective chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans, pour une meilleure planification des interventions dans l'avenir.
Dans ce cadre, vos responsabilités seront:
Assistance technique à la réalisation d'une enquête SMART nutritionnelle et coordination de l'activité avec les autorités locales et ONGs partenaire
Planification, préparation des outils et supervision de l'enquête
Elaboration du protocole d'enquête, préparation du matériel de formation et de tout autre outil de travail conformément aux normes d'enquête SMART
Elaboration d'outils de collecte des données et de questionnaires prédéfinis dans des tablettes utilisant le logiciel Kobo Collect, ACF disposera de tablettes contenant l'application Kobo Collect
Recrutement, formation (méthodologie d'enquête SMART), et sélection des staffs techniques et des agents communautaires devant conduire l'activité dans le District.
Coordonner toute la collecte des données sur le terrain pour garantir une collecte de données de qualité
Nettoyer les bases de données et analyser les résultats de l'enquête à l'aide du logiciel standard ENA et de tout logiciel supplémentaire (EPI-Info) requis pour les indicateurs
Présenter les résultats préliminaires à ACF et à toutes les parties prenantes concernées pour obtenir des commentaires (verbaux et écrits) et formuler des recommandations.
Sur la base des retours, finaliser le rapport avec des recommandations claires et pertinentes dans les délais impartis et présenter les résultats à un groupe plus large (coordination d'ACF, cluster nutrition et ministère de la Santé)

Profile :

Vous êtes diplômé·e en nutrition, santé publique, médecine, soins infirmiers, épidémiologie, biostatistique ou dans une discipline connexe, avec de bonnes connaissances en méthodologie d'enquête et en recherche.
Vous justifiez d'au moins 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la nutrition, de la santé publique ou de la santé maternelle, infantile et nutritionnelle.
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la coordination, la mise en oeuvre et le suivi-évaluation de projets de nutrition, ainsi que dans la réalisation d'évaluations nutritionnelles et le monitoring des activités de santé et nutrition.
Vous maîtrisez les statistiques, l'analyse de données, ainsi que les logiciels EPI Info, ENA for SMART, SMART+ et les outils informatiques associés.
Vous êtes reconnu·e pour vos qualités de communication, votre capacité à animer des ateliers et à rédiger des rapports d'évaluation de qualité.
La maîtrise du français oral et écrit est indispensable.
La connaissance des langues locales et du contexte humanitaire en RCA constituera un atout apprécié.

Conditions d'emploi

Contrat à durée déterminée d'usage de droit français : 1,5 mois jusqu'au 31/12/2026.
Salaire mensuel brut : de 2130 à euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois
Remboursement assurance retraite pour les citoyens non français : 16% du salaire mensuel brut
Augmentation du salaire de base : 6% tous les 12 mois de contrat continu
Per diem et frais de vie mensuels : 775euros nets, versés sur le terrain
Allocation contexte mensuelle : 300euros
Allocation enfant : 1500euros par an et par enfant présent dans le pays d'origine (plafond de 6000euros/an)
Transport et logement : Prise en charge des déplacements et logement collectif
Couverture Médicale : 100% de la prise en charge des cotisations santé et assurance rapatriement, de vos frais médicaux et ce jusqu'à 1 mois après la fin de votre contrat
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)
Congés et RnR : 25 jours par an de CP et 20 RnR par an ; prise en charge du billet avec plafond pour se rendre sur la zone de break choisie, et 215euros d'indemnité forfaitaire par RnRAccompagnement et formation
Suivi et accompagnement parcours professionnel
Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft
Déplacements terrains : Ouham-Fafa, Ouham
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Department**

The Global Funding, Innovation and Impact (GFII) Department brings together four strategic functions- Government Partnerships, Strategic Partnerships, Trusts & Foundations, and Global Philanthropy, working alongside two specialist thought-partnership and execution teams: Evidence and Impact, and Business Development and Innovation.

This role sits within the Global Trusts & Foundations team: a full-time, permanent position based in London, with occasional travel. The function has two related remits. The first is to develop and steward MSI's relationships with core private donors in the UK & Europe, ensuring effective oversight of their funds, excellent funder relationships, and programmatic excellence aligned to strategic priorities. The second is to support the Head of Philanthropy and wider Trusts & Foundations team to diversify MSI's funding base by opening new markets and donor audiences and growing private philanthropic investment, in line with the MSI 2030 strategy.

The role will be based in MSI’s Global Support Office (GSO) in London. MSI operates a hybrid working policy with all GSO staff expected to be in the office for a minimum of two days a week.

**About the Role**

The Advisor role is a new role within the UK & Europe Trusts and Foundation team which is part of the wider Global Trusts and Foundations team at MSI. Reporting to the Head of Philanthropy, UK & Europe, this is a pivotal, delivery-focused role at a heart of a fast-paced, high-performing fundraising team.

Working closely with the Head of Philanthropy UK & Europe, the Advisor will split their time approximately 60/40 between grants and portfolio management and supporting the Head of Philanthropy with new business development.

On the grants side, they will manage a diverse foundations portfolio across the region, supporting donor stewardship and ensuring gold-standard grant management - coordinating approvals and high-quality reporting in close partnership with country programmes, Regional Support Teams, and MSI's International Operations, Finance, and Evidence and Impact teams.

This role is ideal for a highly proactive self-starter who takes initiative without waiting to be asked, instinctively moves things forward, and is keen to learn and develop in the role.

**Now is an especially great time to join MSI Reproductive Choices, as this role plus two others will join the global funding and innovation team!**

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

jobs.description:
**I. INTRODUCTION**

**Purpose**

International Center for Transitional Justice (ICTJ), the Center for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation (CSVR) and the Africa Transitional Justice Legacy Fund (ATJLF) seek the services of a consultant to conduct the final external evaluation of the EU-funded project “European Support for Transitional Justice in Africa”/ “Initiative for Transitional Justice in Africa” (NDICI AFRICA/2023/442-639).

The overall objective is to assess the results and impact of the project. The evaluation will be part of the final report as foreseen in the grant agreement. The findings and conclusions of the external evaluation will inform follow-up planning to ensure that future actions build on the results achieved through the project. The evaluation report will also be used by representatives of the European Union to inform current and future interventions in Africa Union member states.

**II. THE PROJECT**

The Initiative for Transitional Justice in Africa (ITJA) is a three-year project jointly launched by the African Union (AU) and the European Union (EU) to support AU member states to domestically incorporate and implement the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP). The project is implemented by a consortium of three organizations led by the International Center for Transitional Justice (ICTJ) working in collaboration with the African Transitional Justice Legacy Fund (ATJLF) and the Center for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation (CSVR).

This initiative promotes and supports the domestic implementation of the AUTJP by providing technical assistance to the AU, its organs and member states; fostering transitional justice knowledge production and management; and strengthening the capacity of civil society and victims’ groups to popularize the AUTJP and advocate for inclusive and accountable transitional justice processes in Africa. Ultimately, the project aims to help societies across the African continent to become more peaceful, just, and accountable.

**Main Objectives:**

1. To strengthen relevant AU organs, Regional and Economic Communities (RECs) and AU Member States’ capacity to implement the AUTJP and to design and operate tailored gender-sensitive reconciliation and reparation mechanisms.
2. To make available rigorous and relevant knowledge on transitional justice experiences in Africa to inform the design of stabilization and reconciliation strategies consistent with the AUTJP.
3. To strengthen the accountability and popularization of African transitional justice mechanisms while ensuring wide consultations with the various strides of affected societies, in particular women and youths.

**Main Activities:**

- Provision of technical expertise to AU Member States, RECs and AU Organs on Transitional Justice
- Supporting African women’s engagement in transitional justice processes.
- Convening several cross-continental EU-AU Expert Seminars on Transitional Justice to discuss lessons learned and share best practices.
- Convening several continental forums on Transitional Justice to discuss, reflect on and assess the state of transitional justice in Africa.
- Increasing capacity and expertise on topical and emerging TJ issues through dedicated webinars.
- Production of new research pieces, case studies and policy briefs, including on the state of TJ in Africa, women and reparations and the use of technology in TJ.
- Supporting the establishment of a research network focused on developing African transitional justice knowledge.
- Supporting the establishment of an African Transitional Justice Expert Reference Group.
- Activating and strengthening the African civil society community of practice on TJ.
- Supporting civil society-led initiatives on transitional justice across the continent.

**III. EVALUATION OBJECTIVE**

To assess the results of the project “European Support for Transitional Justice in Africa” / “Initiative for Transitional Justice in Africa” (NDICI AFRICA/2023/442-639) and produce a final evaluation report.

**IV. SCOPE OF WORK**

The evaluation will cover the work done throughout the three-year implementation of the action across African Union Member States.

**Evaluation Criteria and Key Evaluation Questions**

The consultant is expected to address the key evaluation questions below and to provide recommendations for improving project effectiveness and sustainability going forward. The evaluation will be done in accordance with the EU evaluation guidelines and will follow the [OECD-DAC evaluation criteria](https://www.oecd.org/dac/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.htm).

- Effectiveness
- To what extent has the project achieved its intended results?
- What factors have contributed to and hindered the attainment of the project’s objectives?
- Have there been any unexpected outcomes of the intervention? Positive/negative.
- Relevance
- To what extent did the project address beneficiaries’ needs and priorities? How well was the project designed to address them?
- What are the beneficiaries´ perception of the relevance of the intervention?
- How suitable have adaptations made during the project (if any) been in continuing to meet the needs and priorities of beneficiaries?
- To what extent did the intervention take into consideration the context and was sensitive to the constraints, opportunities and challenges faced by its beneficiaries?
- Efficiency
- Were the human and financial resources used appropriately? Were they fully utilized?
- To what extent have results been achieved in a timely manner and within the intended timeframe?
- Was the timeframe reasonably adjusted during the intervention where unintended obstacles emerged? How were delays mitigated?
- Impact
- To what extent has the project generated significant positive or negative, intended, or unintended, higher-level effects?
- To what extent has the project achieved its overall objective?
- Coherence
- How did the project fit in Ethiopia’s wider political and transitional justice context?
- Have contradictions or synergies been observed with other programs operating in the targeted regions? If so, which ones?
- Sustainability
- To what extent are the positive effects of the project likely to continue over time?
- How has the project contributed to creating an enabling environment for its benefits to be sustained over time, or how has it not?
- What factors may inhibit or put the sustainability of the action at risk?

**V. APPROACH AND METHODOLOGY**

The Consultant is expected to propose an evaluation design and select the appropriate methodologies for collecting and analyzing results.

**VI. DELIVERABLES**

**Inception Phase**

- Develop an *Inception Report* that describes in detail the overall evaluation framework, and that defines the methodology and protocols for data collection and analysis. This deliverable needs to be approved by the ITJA Consortium.

**During desk/field work**

- Conduct thorough interviews and other agreed-upon data collection methods.
- Store and secure all collected project information from interviews and the like in accordance with GDPR rules and regulations.
- Conduct routine check-ins with the focal point of the evaluation in Ethiopia and, if required, ICTJ’s Senior DME lead.

**During data analysis and report writing**

- Keep ICTJ’s focal point updated on the progress of the evaluation assignment.
- Validate with a designated evaluation committee composed of representatives of the ITJA Consortium the preliminary evaluation findings and conclusions.

**By the deadline (agreed upon contract)**

- A final evaluation report. The final report shall include the following sections:
- **Executive summary**: a description of the project, a summary of the targets and intended outcomes, a summary of the methodological approaches used, a description of the main findings, and a conclusion outlining the project’s relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability, impact, and contribution towards the attainment of the final goal.
- **Methodology**: a description of the methodology used, and the target groups involved. Methodological constraints, challenges and limitations should also be discussed in this section.
- **Findings**: a section addressing the evaluation questions. The findings may be presented under evaluation criteria or by domain of impact. *Findings must be supported by evidence*\*\*.\*\* Relevant project indicators used to monitor implementation must be used in the analysis under this section. When evidence relies on perception or feedback of stakeholders interviewed during the evaluation, the consultant must illustrate key findings with selected quotes or careful summaries/translation of statements made by key informants.
- Recommendations and lessons learned.
- Annexes: final terms of reference, evaluation schedule, table of project indicators measured, list of people interviewed, list of documents reviewed, acronyms and abbreviations used, operational definition of terms, etc.

Evaluators are encouraged to include stories of change based on their findings to illustrate changes identified.

The final report should not exceed 40 pages (without annexes).

**VII. SCHEDULE AND BUDGET**

**Time frame:**

We estimate that preparatory work for this evaluation will commence no later than **20 November 2026** and end on **5 February 2027**.

*Proposals must include a timeline considering these deadlines.*

**Budget:**

Proposals should include a preliminary estimated budget and an appropriate number of workdays according to the methodology and approach of their choice.

Said budget should include all costs to be incurred by the evaluator (e.g. consultant fees and per diem, accommodation, international and local transportation, communication costs, insurance costs, etc.). Relevant staff at ICTJ, CSVR and ATJLF will make their best efforts to assist the consultant to schedule in person or virtual meetings and interviews.

All evaluation costs shall be paid by the consultant as part of the budgeted amount.

**VIII. REQUIREMENTS**

Key qualifications to successfully complete this consultancy include:

- Solid experience in conceptualizing and conducting evaluations of transitional justice, democracy building, peacebuilding, or human rights programs in post-conflict contexts.
- Extensive experience conducting evaluations of complex programs in diverse settings.
- Previous experience in evaluating EU funded programs/projects.
- Solid knowledge of the African Union and its Member States’ context is required, particularly of the countries covered by the action. Examples of such countries include Ethiopia, The Gambia, Lesotho and South Sudan among others.
- An advanced degree in a relevant field.
- Excellent written and communications skills.
- English proficiency required. Working level French is also required.

jobs.title: Proposal Lead - World Bank
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Global Business Development**

Within the Awards Management Unit, the Global BD team leads IRC’s public BD strategy and donor engagement for IRC’s international programs. The team brings together capacity across the organization to drive donor engagement and BD services to secure the public funding needed to deliver our work to clients. The team includes technical, operational and donor specialists able to lead our most complex proposals and manage our most important donor relationships.

***Please note that the candidates MUST INCLUDE a COVER LETTER and give a recent example or a World Bank Proposal they have led. Failure to include a cover letter will result in disqualification.***

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Germany and UK,

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Senior Program/Business Development Advisor (World Bank) will join a global BD team and will help drive IRC’s new business development efforts by engaging with global, regional, country, and technical staff throughout the business development cycle from opportunity tracking and positioning/capture planning to proposal development, and submission. The SPDA will primarily serve as capture and proposal manager, and s/he will also offer technical assistance and mentor staff working on proposals on relevant business development topics.

The ideal candidate will have significant high-level experience in managing capture and proposal development for opportunities that are complex or high-value nature. This should include a track record of successful multi-million dollar proposal development with the World Bank or other multilateral development bank. Experience of large funding proposals with other major government donors will be a distinct advantage.

**Key Accountabilities**

***Bid leadership and coordination (70%)***

- Lead proposal development for complex and strategic public opportunities, including capture strategy, management of proposal teams, calendars, and deadlines; strategy development with technical staff; consortium management and negotiations; recruiting; writing; production; and after-action reviews.
- Collaborate with regional, country, and technical teams to develop and implement opportunity-specific long-term capture and positioning strategies.
- Lead strategic capture efforts for frameworks, single opportunities and wider funding sources including donor mapping, SWOT analysis, support to win theme development, and relevant strategies for pre-positioning efforts.
- Contribute to strengthening IRC’s profile and relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, peer organizations, local partners, and government institutions to support opportunity-specific strategic planning and decision-making.
- Advises Technical Teams and Country Teams on strategic approaches for funding opportunities, guiding a robust and evidence driven Go/No Go process.
- Supports technical units and country teams to offer pitches to prospective partners to secure the most competitive consortia possible.
- Review and/or draft expressions of interest, concept notes, and proposals to ensure quality and compliance with donor standards.
- Collaborate with IRC’s pricing team and other budget leads, ensuring technical coherence and value for money with the cost proposal.
- Collaborate with Proposal Recruiters to identify and assess candidates for key personnel positions on proposals.
- Organize and manage internal processes to ensure IRC is always submitting the most competitive and compliant proposals.

***Business Development process improvement and knowledge management (10%)***

- Conducts After Action Reviews, Donor Feedback Reviews and capture wider learnings to disseminate to wider organization
- Contributes to and models the use of standard business development processes, tools, templates and information.
- May serve in short term mentor role to junior staff leading large bids for the first time.

***Partnerships and Strategy (20%)***

- Conducts landscape analyses as necessary to identify most strategic partnerships in public donor markets, with a particular focus on fostering local partnerships.
- Drafts high quality positioning materials as necessary, including capability statements and prior project reference sheets.
- Strengthening collaboration with internal stakeholders including country teams, technical units, and other team members.
- Contributes to country-specific BD strategies and BD action plans as necessary to support prioritization of new business development opportunities.
- Work with colleagues across IRC, in particular the BD Quality & Systems team to support change initiatives to continuously improve, evolve and innovate IRC approach to effective, mission aligned business development.

**Person Specification**

**Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:**

- At least six years of focused experience working with major institutional donors on large and often complex procurements, with extensive World Bank experience required. Additional experience with other multilateral and bilateral donors such as FCDO, French AFD, or German BMZ is an advantage. \*
- Strong knowledge of World Bank compliance, rules, and regulations, along with familiarity with the policies of other relevant donors. \*
- Familiarity with standard Business Development processes, and a willingness to learn and apply IRC's BD guidelines.
- Fluency in English and French required.\*

**Experience:**

- Successful track record of acting as proposal manager on complex subject, multi-year, multi-partner proposals with minimal supervision\*
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively manage a variety of relationships in a multicultural environment
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate equally effectively with colleagues in ‘remote’ and diverse teams, including as team leader for proposals
- The ability to work productively and accurately while under pressure in a fast-paced, demanding environment
- Experience managing large development or humanitarian programs- a strong understanding of program implementation and donor engagement throughout the project cycle will desirable.
- Lived and/ or working experience in Sub-Saharan Africa is an advantage.
- Ability to travel internationally (up to 20% of time)

**Compensation (UK):** (GBP 58,476- GBP 69,440 annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

As Manager of Philanthropy in the UK, you will support both the organization’s vision and the Philanthropy Department's strategy to grow private donor income from individuals residing in the UK, Canada and Europe. Reporting to Senior Director of Global Philanthropy and line managing the UK Philanthropy Officer, you will nurture relationships with individual donors giving £1K-£25K per annum.

You will take the lead in designing and launching innovative fundraising programmes online and in person. You will join the team responsible for doubling MSI’s individual giving revenue by 2030 and ensuring MSI’s nascent legacy society gains solid footing and membership over the next 5-10 years. You will also act as the Philanthropy liaison with the Global Communications team, and you will oversee cultivation and stewardship events across the UK.

**Now is an especially great time to join MSI Reproductive Choices, as this role plus two others will join the global funding and innovation team!**

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Ability to develop long-term, productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Accountability to metrics and an ability to work effectively with donor data and analytics.
- Experience in securing four-to-five-figure gifts from individuals through segmented and targeted email campaigns and one-to-one engagement.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

jobs.title: Country Manager - Haiti
jobs.description:
The scale of humanitarian need in Haiti continues to grow. An estimated 6.4 million people require assistance, and nearly 1.5 million were internally displaced by mid-2026. Armed groups control up to 90% of the capital and are expanding into the Centre and Artibonite departments, while access to food, water, health care, shelter, and education remains critically limited.

By January 2026, only 10% of national inpatient health facilities were fully operational. In Port-au-Prince, just 41% of bed-equipped facilities remained functional due to insecurity, damaged infrastructure, medicine shortages, and the departure of an estimated 40% of medical personnel. NoRC supports the Croix-Rouge Haïtienne in delivering lifesaving prehospital and primary health care to vulnerable populations, particularly those affected by violence and displacement.
The Country Manager (CM) is responsible for achieving NoRC’s humanitarian objectives through strategic leadership, project and risk management, and oversight of NoRC-supported health programmes implemented with the Haitian Red Cross (CRH).
The CM ensures technical quality, compliance with NoRC standards and policies, and effective programme delivery. The role also includes managing the NoRC country team and serving as the primary liaison with Movement and external partners, contributing to stronger health programmes and improved humanitarian outcomes.

**Strategic responsibilities**

- Develop further, with effectiveness and efficiency, the cooperation with the CRH in accordance with established incountry agreements.
- Develop and strengthen the Movement partnership between CRH, NoRC, the International Committee of the Red
Cross (ICRC) and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) through programme
development and management in line with existing and future agreements and plans.
- Represent Norwegian Red Cross in-country within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement (RCM), within the wider
community of humanitarian organizations, and vis à vis the Norwegian stakeholders and contribute to
complementary RCM roles and responsibilities.
- Draft yearly plans of action and corresponding budgets for NoRC country portfolio in consultation and collaboration
with the CRH and follow up on progress through regular meetings and reporting.
- Oversee that NoRC supported interventions comply with established technical and operational standards, and
relevant thematic frameworks.
- Lead in the technical area of emergency preparedness and response, contributing to emergency preparedness and
response initiatives at country level and in close collaboration with the CRH.

**Operational responsibilities**
The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following tasks:

- Ensure that CRH health projects (including protection components) are designed, implemented and monitored in
line with established technical standards and overall project management (planning, monitoring, evaluation and
reporting) standards.
- Assist with the technical capacity strengthening of the national society on health-related matters to ensure
coherence and technical alignment with other community-based initiatives supported by Movement partners in
Haiti.
- Provide technical support to the quality design, including monitoring structures, of health programmes, in line with
NoRC strategic documents and technical standards. Liase with technical staff in RO, NO, ICRC, IFRC an
others to guarantee technical inputs when required.
- Ensure timely implementation and quality monitoring of NoRC supported health projects through structured and
regular monitoring, field visits, follow up and reporting on them.
- Support in providing trainings and coaching Host National Society project staff on the operationalization of
established technical standards and when challenges arise.
- Ensure operationalisation of NoRC and Movement health technical standards to ensure an evidence-based
approach.
- Responsible for quarterly, tertiaty or annual narrative reporting to NoRC regional office as stablished.
- Ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality reporting to donors, in compliance with grant agreements and
organizational standards.
- Ensure sound financial and administrative management of NoRC projects in line with NoRC rules, regulations, and
operational guidelines, and in accordance with established rules and guidelines within the RCM.
- Oversee the planning and implementation of project- and delegation-related procurement plans and ensure
application and respect of established procurement guidelines and norms.
- Develop, with support from the security focal point and ICRC, the security policy and procedures for the NoRC Haiti office and fully ensure respect for security rules.

**Collaboration**

\- Collaborate with ICRC, IFRC, other PNS and the CRH to ensure coordination and complementarity for
maximized humanitarian outcomes.
\- Collaborate and ensure complementarity with health programmes of other Movement and non-Movement partners
which are carried out in the same areas.
\- Collaborate with NoRC regional team and national office to ensure alignment with NoRC established work processes,
technical standards, and efficient use of NoRC technical resources for the purpose of the country portfolio.
\- Coordinate regularly with all other PNSs, IFRC and ICRC in country and in project location (as applicable).
\- Collaborate with Movement partners to ensure an inclusive approach putting the NS closer to the center of the
operation and with a stronger focus on the reinforcement of local capacities.
\- Collaborate with CRH sub delegations and NS branches, when relevant and in coordination with the CRH NO, in
target zones in matters related to health project and field security management
\- Engages with the wider humanitarian community in Haiti through relevant networks events and workshops to
ensure closer coordination and collaboration with non-Movement partners
