jobs.title: Consultancy - PowerBi Dashboard
jobs.description:
## BACKGROUND

In April 2026, the IMPACT HR Department initiated the development of an HR Power BI Dashboard to strengthen data-driven decision-making and improve workforce planning across the organization. The project responds to the current fragmentation of HR data across multiple systems, including the software where our base of employees is (CORE), JIRA, and country-level trackers, which requires significant manual consolidation and limits timely access to strategic workforce information.

The purpose of this assignment is to finalize, validate, and fully operationalize the HR Power BI Dashboard by developing automated data integrations, ensuring data quality, and delivering user-friendly reporting tools. The dashboard will serve as a centralized source of HR information, providing real-time visibility on key workforce indicators and reducing administrative reporting efforts.

The dashboard is expected to provide automated reporting on key HR metrics, including workforce composition, recruitment performance, vacancy management, turnover, expatriation processes, contract management, diversity indicators, and workforce planning trends, enabling HR and senior leadership to make informed and timely decisions.

## THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment consists of finalizing, validating, and operationalizing IMPACT’s HR Power BI Dashboard to establish a centralized, automated, and reliable HR analytics platform. The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen data-driven decision-making, improve workforce planning capabilities, and enhance the efficiency, quality, and accessibility of HR reporting across the organization.

The consultant will begin by conducting a review of existing HR data sources, reporting processes, and dashboard requirements to assess current functionality, identify data gaps, and validate business needs. Based on this assessment, the consultant will design and implement the required technical solutions to integrate data from CORE, JIRA, and other relevant HR data sources in excel files into a single reporting environment.

Building on these integrations, the consultant will finalize and refine interactive Power BI dashboards that provide real-time visibility on key HR indicators, including workforce composition, recruitment performance, retention and turnover trends, diversity metrics, expatriation processes, contract management, and workforce planning. Particular attention should be given to ensuring data accuracy, consistency, user experience, and alignment with the reporting needs of HR Leadership and Senior Management.

The consultant will also establish appropriate data validation and quality assurance mechanisms to ensure the reliability and sustainability of the dashboard over time. Comprehensive technical documentation and user guidance materials will be developed to support future maintenance and administration of the platform.

Finally, the consultant will conduct testing, validation, and knowledge transfer sessions with relevant stakeholders, incorporate feedback into the final product, and support the deployment of a fully operational HR Power BI Dashboard. The assignment should ensure that IMPACT possesses a sustainable, user-friendly, and scalable HR reporting solution capable of supporting strategic workforce management and organizational decision-making.

The consultant will be expected to review and finalise the existing HR Power BI dashboard, building on the work already completed. The assignment should focus on correcting identified data and categorisation issues, integrating missing historical data sources, developing missing or enhanced indicators and visuals, and improving the usability of the dashboard.

The existing dashboard and the detailed HR Dashboard Gap Mapping will be provided as reference material for the consultancy work.

### Deliverable 1: Workforce dashboard finalisation

Finalise the“IMPACT’S Workforce: all staff” dashboard, including:

- Review and correct the workforce categorisation and mapping, in particular the treatment of National Staff, International Staff, Global non-HQ staff and HQ Staff.
- Establish the required connection to the relevant National Staff Excel data source, including the historical source required to report workforce evolution.
- Add HQ Staff to the gender split.
- Add workforce evolution including National Staff.
- Enhance geographic reporting with a graph showing staff distribution by country and staff type, with particular visibility of the National versus International split and percentage by country.

### Deliverable 2: Global and International staff profile and evolution

Finalise the current HQ/International staff profile and evolution pages around the revised population definition: eg Global (HQ-based staff, International Staff working for Geneva/Global teams and SYNI) and International (non-Global International Staff). Apply this categorisation consistently to the relevant metrics, visuals and filters.

Develop or adjust the following:

- Numerical staff distribution by country, complementing the existing map, with comparison against the equivalent point one year earlier.
- Average age evolution allowing analysis by Global versus International population, in addition to the existing analysis by grade.
- Review the categorisation used in relevant grade and contract-type visuals.
- Redesign the filters so that they are useful and consistent across the relevant dashboard pages.
- Where required because current 2025 data is not reliable, connect the relevant historical Excel data source (excel file) for historical comparisons.

### Deliverable 3: Diversity dashboard redesign and completion

Reorganise and complete the diversity reporting, including:

1\) Overall GN/GS ratio monitoring. Develop an overview allowing HR to monitor:

- overall Global South/Global North ratio for the combined relevant workforce at the selected reporting date; evolution of the GS/GN ratio;
- GS/GN ratio by grade; evolution of this ratio by grade.

2\) Diversity profile: Develop a complementary diversity profile in which the GN/GS filter operates on the relevant analytical visuals, including:

- contract type;
- gender;
- country of assignment;
- nationality list/ranking.

Ensure that the nationality ranking can be filtered by GN/GS so that Global South nationalities can be isolated without requiring a duplicated page.

In addition:

- Restore an expatriation evolution visual and create/connect the required historical Excel-based source.
- Include the National versus International share of surges within the diversity dashboard as an indicator of National Staff deployment, even if this information is also available within surge reporting.

### Deliverable 4: Staffing dashboard, vacancy reporting

Complete and enhance vacancy/recruitment reporting, including:

- Integrate the historical Excel source for vacancies, correcting/reconciling reporting for 2025 and earlier with the current data.
- Add a historical view of the number of vacancies remaining open at the end of each month.
- Develop vacancy-rate reporting, with clear numerator and denominator definitions.
- Develop a separate due-vacancy rate, covering vacancies already due versus the relevant total population of positions.
- Add the split of vacancy openings between New Position and Replacement.
- Add reporting on the initial planned duration of positions opened, including:
- overall average initial duration;
- breakdown by country where supported by the source.
- Add vacancy closure outcomes using the relevant historical/agreed categories, including National Recruitment, Internal Mobility, External Recruitment and Cancelled Position.
- Add reporting on positions closed by candidate type, including External Recruitment, ongoing staff and former staff.

### Deliverable 5: Recruitment duration analysis

Develop a coherent duration-to-close analysis for recruitment, including:

- overall average duration to close a position;
- duration by closure/recruitment type, including external versus internal;
- duration by country;
- duration by grade.

The dimensions should work as filters or drill-downs around the same core duration metric rather than as disconnected measures.

The consultant should also review the existing operational time\_to\_done\_hours measure against the recruitment duration-to-close definition and ensure that the appropriate metric is used for HR recruitment reporting.

### Deliverable 6: Surge reporting

Complete the surge reporting, including:

- Integrate the historical Excel source for surges, correcting/reconciling reporting for 2025 and earlier with the current data.
- Add a country breakdown/ranking of surge requests opened, allowing HR to identify the countries generating the highest surge demand.
- Add the number/share of surges filled by National Staff versus International Staff, including historical evolution where the data allows.

### Deliverable 7: Staff retention, exits and turnover

Introduce Staff Retention Rate as a headline KPI at the beginning of the “Staffing our Teams dashboard”.

In addition, develop the underlying exit/turnover reporting, supported by the current source and historical Excel data, including the required voluntary/non-voluntary exit analysis and associated historical reporting.

### Deliverable 8: Staff Performance and Development indicator

Introduce a new Staff Performance and Development indicator showing: % of eligible staff with an appraisal carried out during the past year. The metric definition and treatment of the reporting/reference period should be validated during implementation.

### Deliverable 9: Contractual visibility

Develop the contractual-visibility reporting using the already connected current data source, including:

- contract duration of current International Staff in Grades 3 and 4;
- contract duration granted to newly onboarded International Staff in Grades 3 and 4;
- number of International Staff whose contracts end within the following four months, by grade;
- International Staff whose contracts end within the following four months as a percentage of total International Staff;
- The existing source is connected, but the usability/readability of this reporting needs to be improved.

### Deliverable 10: Cross-cutting data validation and technical documentation

- For all developments and data-source integrations described in the deliverables above, the consultant will:
- reconcile newly integrated historical data with current reporting to ensure continuity of the relevant indicators;
- validate the calculations developed or modified as part of the assignment;
- test and resolve identified inconsistencies in workforce categorisation and other reporting logic;
- document the principal calculation rules and definitions used for the new or modified indicators;
- document the relevant data sources, source dependencies and connections introduced or modified through the assignment;
- document known data-quality limitations that cannot be resolved within the scope of the consultancy;
- provide sufficient technical documentation to allow the HR team or a future Power BI developer to understand and maintain the solution.

### Deliverable 11: Final dashboard testing and handover

Following completion of the developments above, the consultant should:

- conduct functional testing of the new and modified measures, visuals and filters;
- support HR validation against the agreed gap/needs mapping;
- correct issues identified during validation;
- ensure consistent filter behaviour across the dashboard;
- provide the final updated Power BI dashboard together with the information required for its continued maintenance.

The list above describes the substantive development requirements to be costed by the consultant. jobs.title: Junior National Lawyer (Ukrainian Nationals Only)

**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

Mobile Justice Teams (MJTs) are groups of local and international experts and practitioners collaborating with and in support of local justice actors, such as Ukraine’s Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG) and Regional Prosecutor Offices (RPOs), to advance Ukraine's capacity to investigate and build complex command-level cases into international crimes through tailored support and the institutionalisation of international standards and best practices. The MJTs are organised across thematic areas to address context-specific and cross-cutting legal issues. The teams work in the most affected regions of Ukraine to provide advisory and case-building support, focusing on supporting prosecutors and investigators in their investigations and prosecutions.

We are seeking a Junior National Lawyer to join our team in Ukraine. The Junior National Lawyer assists the team working on a specific category of international crimes (e.g. crimes against humanity, genocide, and aggression) or a designated thematic area within the team’s mandate (e.g. air strikes, detention-related crimes, pillage of essential resources, SGBV, crimes against and affecting children, occupation-related crimes).

- Support legal and factual research.
- Support in developing standard operating procedures, tools and methodologies, providing strategic advice on investigations and case-building, and delivering tailored capacity-building initiatives

- Assist in delivering other project objectives.
- Assist in maintaining regular dialogue with other actors, including international organisations and local CSOs, to foster meaningful collaboration, avoid duplication and promote complementarity and harmonisation of support.
- Facilitate meetings and other interactions with relevant stakeholders including interpretations where required.
- Assist in the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration.
- Perform other tasks as requested (or authorised) by the MJT Lead and reasonably foreseen under the scope of work.

**Your Background**

- Qualified in law (LLB mandatory).
- 2+ years professional legal experience practising law within a law firm, prosecution service, court, etc.
- Knowledge of the Ukrainian justice system, including criminal and criminal procedural legislation.

- Practical experience working with Ukrainian justice actors, preferably within a national or international prosecution team.
- Flexible, able to work in a changeable environment.
- Administratively competent.

- Practical experience of working with highly sensitive material and an ability to demonstrate the requisite skill in storing, sharing and working with such material.

jobs.title: Intersectional Procurement Manager - RDC
jobs.description:
**Rattachement hiérarchique:** Cette position est redevable devant le Intersectional Supply Emergency Steering Committee (ISSC), composé d’un représentant du département approvisionnement de chaque centre opérationnel participant aux activités d’achat mutualisées.

Rattachement fonctionnel Intersectional Procurement Advisor à la Global Procurement Unit

**Domaine:** Supply

**Lieu:** Intervention d’urgence Ebola, Bunia, République démocratique du Congo (RDC)

Contrat Contrat à durée déterminée à 100 %

**Nombre de postes:** Deux postes, l’un pour une prise de fonctions immédiate et l’autre pour une prise de fonctions dans un délai de 3 mois, en février 2027.

**Durée:** 3 mois plus période de suivi post affectation Ebola de 21 jours

**Date de début:** 01 Décembre 2026

**Fermeture publication**: 09 Novembre 2026

**I. CONTEXTE**

Une épidémie d’Ebola, causée par le virus Bundibugyo, a été déclarée le 18 mai 2026 dans la province de l’Ituri (RDC). Depuis, la situation évolue rapidement et se propage aux zones avoisinantes. MSF a mis en place une réponse d’urgence pour soutenir les autorités sanitaires et les communautés touchées.

Compte tenu de l’évolution de la situation, cette réponse s’inscrit probablement dans la durée. MSF se prépare donc à une intervention prolongée, articulée autour de plusieurs phases de déploiement. Afin de garantir la sécurité opérationnelle et le respect des normes de MSF, tout le personnel est tenu de se conformer au code de conduite de l’organisation, ainsi qu’aux procédures spécifiques liées aux interventions contre Ebola.

OCBA, OCB et OCG s'approvisionnent localement à Bunia, un marché instable, limité et partagé avec de nombreuses autres ONG qui se disputent les mêmes fournisseurs. Bunia est également la principale plaque tournante d'approvisionnement pour les projets menés par d'autres organisations de la communauté.

**II. OBJECTIF DU POSTE**

L’Intersectional Procurement Manager (IPM) définit et met en œuvre la stratégie d’achat pour les catégories d’achat identifiés comme prioritaires, afin de répondre aux besoins communs des activités d'urgence des centres opérationnels (OC) présents à Bunia,.

L’objectif de ce poste est de renforcer la disponibilité et la qualité des biens et services, d’améliorer la maîtrise des risques, et de mutualiser les efforts d’approvisionnement afin de générer des économies sans compromettre la qualité. Il vise également à simplifier la gestion des catégories d’achats gérés en intersection et éviter la mise en concurrence entre les centres opérationnels.

Le poste a par ailleurs pour finalité d’assurer une approche cohérente et harmonisée des approvisionnements au sein du mouvement MSF, à travers l’alignement des méthodologies, pratiques, outils et processus d’achat, dans le respect des protocoles, standards et procédures de MSF ainsi que de la réglementation locale, afin de renforcer la capacité des centres opérationnels à répondre efficacement aux besoins opérationnels.

Pour ce poste spécifiquement le titulaire sera chargé de coordonner les activités « source to contrat » pour les achats locaux pour les trois OCs, en mettant l'accent sur l'évaluation du marché et la négociation des contrats avec les fournisseurs afin de garantir les prix et la disponibilité des produits.

**III. RESPONSABILITÉS CLÉS**

Domaines d’intervention requis et objectifs spécifiques :

1. **Piloter les achats stratégiques inter-OC en contexte d’urgence**

• Identifier et hiérarchiser les principales catégories d’achats effectués de manière récurrente par OCBA, OCB et OCG à Bunia.

• Réaliser une évaluation rapide du marché : identification des fournisseurs, qualification, vérification juridique et administrative, validation des prix – en s’appuyant dès à présent sur les informations disponibles dans le cadre du programme national,

• Négocier et signer des accords-cadres intersectoriels / contrats locaux pour ces catégories, validés par les coordinateurs opérationnels/techniques de OCBA, de OCB et de OCG.

• Consolider les besoins confirmés et les projections basées sur des scénarios (et non sur des prévisions historiques) des trois OC.

• Tenir à jour une liste de fournisseurs indiquant leur statut de conformité et les prix validés, partagée entre les trois OC.

**2. Gérer un réseau fonctionnel pour les achats intersection**

• Organiser des réunions régulières des parties prenantes et rendre compte régulièrement au Comité de pilotage des urgences d’approvisionnement et au GPU.

• Briefer les nouveaux points focaux achat / Supply et répondre à d’autres demandes de briefing ad hoc.

• S'assurer que les départements financiers reçoivent leurs copies des contrats et soient informés pour vérifier si les prix facturés sont conformes aux prix convenus.

• Veiller à ce que les produits soumis à la TVA soient répertoriés en collaboration avec le BIP (bureau des protocoles) et que l'application de l'exonération de la TVA soit accrue.

• Garantir la cohérence entre les termes contractuels des fournisseurs et les documents nécessaires pour l'application de l'exonération de TVA.

• Faire du réseautage avec d'autres organisations – Ex. Log Cluster et autres plateformes.

• Coordonner le travail avec les Responsable achats des OCs (PMs) afin d'éviter les chevauchements et la concurrence sur les mêmes activités. Le IPM se concentrera sur les catégories mutualisées convenues tandis que les PMs se concentreront sur les priorités propres à chaque OC, tout en collaborant étroitement sur les besoins opérationnels.

• Assurer l'implication adéquate des parties prenantes clés, y compris les référents techniques pour la validation des sources et des articles, afin de garantir une mise en œuvre réussie de la stratégie d’achat.

• Communiquer en temps opportun sur les problèmes, opportunités ou toute mise à jour importante liée à l'activité achat intersection.

• Fournir un soutien technique et accompagner le personnel des OCs pour contribuer au développement des meilleures pratiques et des capacités en matière d’achats.

**Hors périmètre :**

• Validation technique des sources pour les articles logistiques et médicaux nécessitant une telle validation.

• Passer les commandes aux centrales d’achat.

• Les activités transactionnelles comme le placement des commandes, la réception des marchandises et la facturation restent du ressort de chaque OC.

• Évaluation du marché en dehors de Bunia.

**IV. RESULTATS ATTENDUS**

• Signature de contrats intersectoriels pour ces catégories, et pas seulement une liste de fournisseurs.

• Liste de fournisseurs avec vérification de conformité et prix validés, partagée entre OCBA, OCB et OCG.

• Vue d’ensemble consolidée des besoins confirmés par rapport aux projections basées sur des scénarios.

**V. CRITERES DE SELECTION**

**Connaissances pratiques / techniques**

jobs.title: ASSISTANTE OU ASSISTANT GESTION DE PROJET JEUNESSE - FRANCE
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Nous recherchons un·e stagiaire capable d'apporter un appui par les missions suivantes :

Participer à la logistique des projets Jeunesse en lien avec des prestataires
Participer au traitement de la collecte liée des projets Jeunesse en lien avec les établissements, les CPJ-R, les APJ-IDF

Participer aux activités du pôle IDF
Participer à la vie du service

Tu es une personne organisée et rigoureuse.
Tu es à l'aise lorsqu'il s'agit de t'exprimer devant un public.

Durée du Stage : 6 mois (basé à Montreuil, 102 rue de paris)

Conditions Salariales :
Stage indemnisé à hauteur de 4,57euros net par heure (sur une base de 35h par semaine).

Temps de travail hebdomadaire (38,75h).

Titres restaurant à 8 EUR (pris en charge à 60% par ACF).

Prise en charge à hauteur de 50 % des frais de transport en commun.

jobs.title: CM Worker CP
jobs.description:
**Location**: Al-Lataminah – Kafr Zita

**Job summary**

Provide case management services to children in accordance with established guidelines, prepare reports, and develop plans that address their needs. The role includes providing support and counseling, referring children to appropriate services, ensuring confidentiality, following up on cases, and documenting success stories, while maintaining the protection and safety of beneficiaries.

**Qualifications and education requirements**:

Technical diploma or bachelor's degree in Social Work, Social Sciences, Psychology, Counseling, or another relevant field.

Completion of CP Case Management training.

Familiarity with and commitment to humanitarian and protection standards.

**Required Skills and Experience**:

- Effective communication skills.
- Priority and time management.
- Data analysis
- Ability to work remotely.
- Report preparation skills.
- Technical computer skills
- Outlook
- Teams
- Word
- Excel
- PowerPoint
- OneDrive

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

- Provide case management services to children and adhere to the relevant case management guidelines.
- Prepare case reports and provide recommendations.
- Develop case management plans that address identified needs based on risk assessments and comprehensive assessments, seeking support from the supervisor when necessary.
- Provide support and counseling services to children and their parents or caregivers.
- Refer children and families to other services when necessary.
- Maintain the confidentiality and privacy of case management files.
- Ensure that the best interests of the child guide every service provided and every decision made concerning the child.
- Close cases in accordance with the minimum standards outlined in the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Safeguard the psychological and physical well-being and safety of beneficiaries.
- Maintain the case management tracking sheet, ensuring that all relevant information is recorded and updated monthly according to case developments.
- Document success stories of children who have received case management services and whose cases have been successfully closed.
- Regularly update the service mapping to ensure its availability and relevance to the case management process.
- Perform any other case management-related tasks as requested by the Programs Manager or Program Officer.
- Perform core administrative responsibilities in coordination with the Human Resources Department, including developing and updating job descriptions, supporting performance management, capacity-building plans, attendance follow-up, recruitment processes within the department, and coordinating employee-related HR matters while promoting compliance with HR procedures.

**Protection Policy:**

Ataa Association considers any type of child abuse unacceptable, as it recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. Ataa Association confirms that it is committed to ensuring a safe environment for children and takes a strict stance against any type of child abuse and exploitation.

**Discrimination, Abuse, and Harassment Policy:**

Ataa Association provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, or harassment (sexual or otherwise) based on race, religion, origin, age, marital status, nationality, or disability. , or the military situation.

jobs.title: Guard-Incentive Worker-Hazima
jobs.description:
**لمحة عن لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية:**

غالبًا ما توصف الأزمة السورية بأنها أسوأ كارثة إنسانية منذ نهاية الحرب الباردة. اليوم ، يحتاج 13.4 مليون شخص في سوريا - أكثر من نصف سكان البلاد - إلى المساعدة الإنسانية مع تفاقم الاحتياجات بشكل متزايد بسبب التدهور الاقتصادي. ومن بين هؤلاء ، هناك 6.8 مليون لاجئ وطالب لجوء فروا من البلاد. هذه ليست حلقة إنسانية قصيرة المدى. ستستمر العواقب البشرية المدمرة على أعداد هائلة من الناس لعقود. سيستغرق إصلاح تدمير العلاقات والمجتمعات وسبل العيش والمنازل والبنية التحتية سنوات.

تقدم لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية استجابة إنسانية قوية للأزمة السورية من خلال برامج سريعة التوسع ، بدعم من أكثر من 1000 موظف في البرنامج القطري السوري. تقوم لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية بتنفيذ برامج في سوريا والدول المجاورة لتركيا , العراق ولبنان والأردن في مجالات الصحة وحماية الطفل وتنمية الطفولة المبكرة والتعليم وحماية المرأة وتمكينها والمواد غير الغذائية وتوزيع المواد الغذائية والمساعدة النقدية والمياه والصرف الصحي والحماية وسيادة القانون وبرامج سبل العيش. يثير عملنا في هذه الأوضاع الصعبة بعضًا من أكثر القضايا إلحاحًا التي تواجه العمل الإنساني المعاصر ، بما في ذلك مسائل الوصول والأمن والتمويل والتنسيق.

**معلومات عن الوظيفة:**

بالتنسيق مع مسوؤل الوصول الأنساني سيكون الحارس الأمني مسوؤلاً عن تقديم الدعم لموقع لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية . حيث سيكون مسوؤلاً عن أمن وسلامة موقع لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية والتاكد من أن موقع المنظمة يتوافق مع جميع سياسيات واجراءات الأمن والسلامة لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية في الرقة.

**المسؤوليات الرئيسية**:

- إجراء جولات منتظمة بالتوافق مع التوجيهات الأمنية
- ملاحظة المشاكل والإبلاغ عنها ، بما في ذلك الأنشطة المشبوهة والسلوكيات والمخاوف ذات الصلة بالصيانة.
- الحفاظ على سجلات الأمان بالتوافق مع سياسات وإجراءات لجنة الأنقاذ الدولية .
- الاستجابة لحالات الطوارئ وغيرها من المشاكل ، وفقا للمبادئ التوجيهية وسياسات وإجراءات لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية
- المشاركة في أنشطة التدريب والتطوير المهني ، حسب الحاجة أو الطلب.
- مراقبة وسائل تزويد الكهرباء الرئيسية ومواعيد تشغيل المولد وإيقافه وفقا لما هو مبين في توجيهات المنظمة بالإضافة إلى ذلك ، مراقبة ساعات استخدام المولد بعناية وإخطار المسؤول اللوجستي عندما يحتاج المولد إلى خدمة.
- أداء واجبات أخرى ، ذات صلة ، أو عند الطلب

**الخبرة / المؤهل / المهارات المطلوبة:**

- يجيد القراءة والكتابة وشهادة التعليم الثنوي ميزة اضافية
- 1-2 سنوات كحد أدنى من الخبرة المهنية في وظيفة مماثلة سابقة .
- القدرة على العمل بشكل مستقل في بيئة مهنية سريعة التغيير بهدف التوصل إلى وضع الإجراءات التي تضمن الأداء
- مهارات جيدة في التعامل مع الآخرين ومهارات تنظيمية ومهارات إدارة الوقت.
- التمتع بقدرة عالية في المحافظة على السرية في العمل .
- القدرة والاستعداد للعمل والقدوم إلى العيادة/الموقع في ظل ظروف مختلفة ويفضل من ابناء المنطقة .

**المهارات والكفاءات:**

- الالتزام برسالة لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية ورؤيتها وقيمها ونهجها - مدونة السلوك المهنية.
- مهارات الاتصال الكتابية والعرضية واللفظية. القدرة على نقل المعلومات بشكل فعال والخبرة القوية في توفير التدريب وتطوير الموظفين.
- إحساس ظاهر بالتمسك المهني والنزاهة والقدرة على التعامل مع المواقف المعقدة دبلوماسياً وإيجاد حلول فعالة.
- إدارة ممتازة ومهارات التعامل مع الآخرين وقدرة قوية على تعزيز العمل الجماعي المتناغم / المتماسك ، في سياق متعدد الثقافات.
- التحقق من القدرة على التخطيط على المدى الطويل وتنظيم الأولويات والعمل تحت ضغوط إدارية وبرامجية مع توجيه تفصيلي وصبر مهني.
- متعاون للغاية وواسع الحيلة. القدرة على إقامة علاقات عمل إيجابية مع الإدارة العليا وجميع الشركاء الآخرين لتعظيم التعاون والإنتاجية.
- الفضول ، والرغبة في التعلم والتطور باستمرار وروح معنوية جيدة أمر لا بد منه.
- القدرة التحليلية في إيجاد حلول فعالة للمسائل المعقدة مع الالتزام بقوانين العمل والسياسات الداخلية.

**اللغة / السفر:**

- يجيد القراءة والكتابة اللغة العربية
- القدرة والرغبة في المجيء الى موقع العمل -مخيم واشو كاني في مختلف الظروف

**علاقات العمل الرئيسية*****:***

- المدير المباشر*:* مساعد الوصول الانساني
- المدير غير المباشر (إن وجد)*:* مشرف الوصول الانساني

**المعايير المهنية**: يجب على موظفي لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية الالتزام بالقيم والمبادئ الموضحة في نهجلجنة الإنقاذ الدولية المعايير العالمية للسلوك المهني و هي النزاهة والخدمة والمساءلة والمساواة. وفقًا لهذه القيم ، تعمل لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية وتنفذ سياسات حماية المستفيد من الاستغلال والإيذاء ، وحماية الطفل ، ومكافحة التحرش في مكان العمل ، واحترام النزاهة المالية في العمل ، ومكافحة الانتقام.

**المرشحون الوطنيون العائدون**: نحن نشجع بشدة المرشحين الوطنيين أو العائدين على التقدم لهذا المنصب. إذا كنت مواطنًا في البلد الذي يقع فيه هذا المنصب وتوجد حاليًا خارج بلدك الأم ولديك أكثر من عامين من الخبرة في العمل الدولي ، فقد قدم إقليم الشرق الأوسط حزمة مكافآت منافسة. تتضمن الحزمة التعويض التنافسي ورحلة العودة إلى البلد وبدل الشحن والإسكان المؤقت وبدل الانتقال. قد يتم تطبيق قيود معينة. تسعى لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية جاهدة لجذب وتحفيز والاحتفاظ بالموظفين الوطنيين المؤهلين في برامجنا.

**المسائلة أمام العملاء**: يجب على موظفي لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية الالتزام بالمساهمة في استدامة وتطوير آليات استجابة العملاء ، والحفاظ على ثقافة تحديد أولويات احتياجات عملائنا والمجتمعات المتضررة من خلال الاستماع بشكل منهجي إلى وجهات نظرهم واستخدام ملاحظاتهم. لاتخاذ قرارات برنامجية ومنحهم تأثيرًا أكبر على تصميم البرنامج وإنجازه.

**المساواة بين الجنسين:** لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية ملتزمة بإتاحة المجال للجنسين في المناصب القيادية. نحن نقدم مزايا توفر بيئة مواتية للمرأة للمشاركة في القوى العاملة لدينا بما في ذلك الإجازة الوالدية ، والبروتوكولات الأمنية التي تراعي الفوارق بين الجنسين وغيرها من المزايا والبدلات الداعمة.

**التنوع والشمول**: في إقليم الشرق الأوسط ، نحن متحمسون لإنشاء مكان عمل شامل يعزز التنوع ويقدره. يتم التحقق من صحة المنظمات المتنوعة في العمر ، و الجنسية ، والعرق ، والقدرة البدنية أو العقلية ، والعرق ، والمنظور لتكون مؤسسات أفضل. والأهم من ذلك ، أن إنشاء بيئة عمل آمنة حيث يمكن للجميع ، من أي خلفية ، بذل قصارى جهدهم هو الشيء الصحيح الذي ينبغي فعله. لذا ، أحضر نفسك بالكامل إلى العمل.

تلتزم لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية بخلق بيئة عمل متنوعة وشاملة ومحترمة وآمنة حيث يتم التعامل مع جميع الأشخاص بإنصاف وكرامة واحترام. تمشيا مع قيمنا الأساسية للنزاهة والخدمة والمساءلة والمساواة ، تسعى لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية جاهدة للحفاظ على بيئة عمل مبنية على الاحترام المتبادل حيث يعامل جميع الأفراد بعضهم البعض بشكل مهني ، وخالية من التحيز والتمييز والمضايقات. . لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية لن تتسامح مع التمييز أو المضايقة أو الانتقام أو التنمر من الأشخاص في أي مكان عمل ل لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية. جميع موظفي لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية ، أينما كانوا ، مسؤولون عن خلق بيئة خالية من التمييز والمضايقة و التنمر والانتقام.

jobs.title: Agricultural Value Chain and Market Development Specialist
jobs.description:
Global Path Research and Analytics LLC is seeking an experienced **Agricultural Value Chain and Market Development Specialist** to support the assessment of agricultural market systems, smallholder sourcing models, agribusiness performance, and value chain development interventions. The specialist will contribute to the evaluation of market linkages, commercialization pathways, sourcing arrangements, private sector engagement, and sector-level outcomes affecting farmers, cooperatives, aggregators, processors, and financial institutions.

The position will provide technical expertise in analyzing agricultural value chains, identifying market opportunities and constraints, assessing buyer-supplier relationships, and evaluating how investments contribute to strengthening domestic sourcing, improving market access, increasing competitiveness, and expanding smallholder participation in commercial agricultural markets.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead value chain and market systems analyses across targeted agricultural commodities.
- Assess the effectiveness, efficiency, and sustainability of smallholder sourcing and aggregation models.
- Evaluate market linkages between farmers, cooperatives, aggregators, processors, financial institutions, and buyers.
- Analyze supply chain performance, including volumes, quality, productivity, aggregation, and commercialization outcomes.
- Assess how project interventions have contributed to improved access to markets and increased participation of smallholder farmers in commercial value chains.
- Examine factors influencing domestic sourcing, import substitution, market competitiveness, and private sector investment.
- Analyze relationships between producers, off-takers, processors, and market actors to identify opportunities and constraints affecting value chain performance.
- Support assessments of agribusiness engagement, business model sustainability, and market expansion strategies.
- Conduct stakeholder consultations with farmers, cooperatives, agribusinesses, traders, processors, exporters, and financial service providers.
- Contribute to the development of analytical reports, presentations, learning products, and dissemination materials.

**Required Qualifications**

- Master's degree in Agricultural Economics, Agribusiness, Rural Development, Agricultural Marketing, Value Chain Development, Economics, or a related field.
- Minimum of 7 years of experience in agricultural value chain development, market systems development, agribusiness, or agricultural commercialization.
- Demonstrated experience conducting value chain analyses and market assessments.
- Strong understanding of agricultural markets, commodity systems, market linkages, supply chains, and private sector development.
- Experience working with farmers' organizations, cooperatives, agribusinesses, agricultural processors, traders, and financial institutions.
- Knowledge of inclusive business models, market systems approaches, and agricultural commercialization strategies.
- Experience supporting donor-funded agricultural development, market systems, or private sector development programs.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

jobs.title: Stagiaire - Juriste généraliste/droit du travail F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission du/ de la stagiaire Juriste généraliste/droit du travail est d'apporter un soutien aux opérations humanitaires à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre les activités de MSF, spécifiquement associées à l’Unité RH / Duty of Care et Incidents

**Mission**

Le Département Juridique de MSF apporte conseil et support juridique généraliste / privatiste aux équipes de Médecins Sans Frontières aussi bien sur le terrain qu’au siège.

Le/la stagiaire intégrera le Département juridique Intersection, au sein de l’Unité RH / Duty of Care et Incidents, qui intervient sur les problématiques relatives aux salariés déployés sur le terrain ainsi que sur les incidents susceptibles de les affecter.

Ces sujets recouvrent des situations individuelles ou collectives, principalement en droit du travail et en droit de la responsabilité, mais pouvant également relever du droit pénal. En lien étroit avec les équipes opérationnelles, l’Unité analyse les risques juridiques associés aux situations rencontrées et accompagne la gestion d’incidents variés : procédures disciplinaires, accidents, abus, incidents de sécurité ou encore incidents médicaux.

**Activités principales**

**Les activités principales du/de la stagiaire sont, en support des opérations humanitaires de MSF, et à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre nos activités :**

- Analyse et préparation de dossiers en réponse aux demandes des terrains d’opération ;
- Rédaction de mails, notes, outils et guidelines destinés aux opérationnels sur le terrain ;
- Participation active aux projets de l’Unité ;
- Support à la gestion de différends liés aux ressources humaines dans nos pays d’opération (analyses de risques, négociations, précontentieux) ;
- Support à la gestion des dossiers contentieux sur le terrain (social, pénal, responsabilité civile et délictuelle) ;
- Recherches juridiques variées sous différentes législations.

Les missions du/de la stagiaire impliquent de travailler sur des législations issues de nombreuses juridictions, en tenant compte des spécificités locales, des enjeux humains et des principes humanitaires qui guident l’action de MSF.

Ce stage offre une expérience formatrice du métier de juriste, à travers des problématiques concrètes et diversifiées, au croisement du droit, des ressources humaines et des opérations humanitaires. Il permettra au/à la stagiaire de développer ses compétences en analyse juridique, en gestion des risques et en accompagnement des équipes opérationnelles, dans des contextes exigeants et particulièrement enrichissants.

**Profil recherché**
**Formation/Expérience :** Stage PPI EFB / Titulaire d’un Master 2 en Droit / Ecole de droit de Science Po / Autre profil équivalent. Expérience en cabinet d’avocat ou entreprise de minimum 6 mois.

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Rigueur rédactionnelle
- Capacité de recherche, de problématisation de créativité et de synthèse
- Intérêt pour les activités humanitaires et associatives de MSF
- Ouverture d’esprit
- Réactivité
- Capacité d’adaptation et travail en équipe.

**Langues :** Français C1, Anglais B2, oral et écrit (50% du travail en anglais).

**Statut et conditions**

- Stage de 6 mois, avec convention de stage obligatoire.
- Basé à Paris 19ème.
- Le montant de la gratification est compris entre 4,50€ et 7,97€ brut par heure en fonction du niveau d’études.
- 1 ticket restaurant est attribué par jour travaillé, d’une valeur faciale de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF).
- 2 jours de repos indemnisés par mois.
- Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir** :4 janvier 2027.

jobs.title: Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
arche nova - initiative for people in need (AN) is an independent, non-religious, non-profit and non-governmental organisation (NGO) from Germany working in the fields of humanitarian aid, rehabilitation and development. The primary focus of our activities lies in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH).

Since 2013, AN has been working in Mali, implementing humanitarian and transitional aid projects in the sectors of WaSH, Food Security & Livelihoods (FSL) and DRR. The activities in Mali are managed through the AN Bamako office in close collaboration with the arche nova’s headquarters in Germany.

We are currently looking for a

**Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)**

**Position to be filled:** 15thof December 2026

**Duty station:** Bamako, Mali with travels to the project locations in Gao (Mali) and Niamey (Niger)

**Duration:** initial 12 months contract (extension desired) with 6 months’ probation period

**Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.**

**Overall Purpose of the Position**

The responsibilities of the **Head of Mission (HoM) Mali** include the overall operational, human resources and financial management of the mission Mali, ensuring programme quality, compliance, staff wellbeing, and the implementation of the country strategy. The responsibility also includes fundraising as well as communication and representation of arche nova e.V. towards relevant authorities and stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. General**

- Coordinate the general management of the AN Mali office and, in close coordination with headquarters (HQ), the further adjustment of the organisational structure.
- Ensure the strict application of arche nova's policies and procedures.
- Ensure all relevant and required reporting for authorities in Mali.
- Ensure that all operations are in line with laws of Mali.
- Implementation of AN Mali mission strategy in collaboration with the HQ in Germany and Senior Management Team.
- Ensure AN is represented in technical working groups in relevant sector clusters, ensure meaningful participation in advisory boards, steering committees, NGO consortia and other relevant meetings for Mali.
- Maintain strong relationships with authorities, donors, UN agencies, INGOs, and local partners.
- Ensure quality and timely communication and reporting with all relevant stakeholders.
- Close collaboration with and regular reporting to the different relevant departments at HQ level.
- Identify new funding opportunities and develop donor engagement plans.
- Ensure the promotion and visibility of AN through presentations, reports, and external communication.
- Fostering a positive and accountable work environment, as well as empowering and encouraging staff to take initiative
- Ensure safeguarding of AN’s assets and interests and protect from loss arising from fraud, waste, weak administration and poor value for money.
- Guarantee the correct, efficient, and effective use of logistical, financial and human resources.

**2. Programme & Grants Management**

- Oversee the management and quality assurance of all programmes and grants, ensuring compliance with AN policies and donor regulations in close cooperation with the Head of Programmes.
- Ensure that programme design reflects innovation, community participation, sustainability, and humanitarian principles.
- Supervise project implementation and provide regular support to programme staff and partners.
- Ensure MEAL systems, accountability mechanisms, learning processes, and safeguarding standards are implemented in close collaboration with the MEAL Officer.
- Lead and coordinate proposal development, ensuring strong technical input and alignment with donor priorities.
- Lead and strengthen existing consortia relations in close cooperation with the Desk Manager and the Head of Programmes.
- Approve and oversee external research, evaluations, audits, and rapid assessments of emerging crises.

**3. Human Resources, Administration & Capacity Building**

- Overseeing the HR management: development of programme staff structures, recruitment, performance monitoring, capacity building (including being the lead for any disciplinary procedures of AN staff, e.g. issuing warnings, terminations, suspensions, etc.)
- Promote staff wellbeing and duty of care, ensuring safe and enabling working conditions.
- Identify and support capacity-building needs for staff and partners.
- Ensure compliance with national labour laws, AN HR policies, safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and anti-fraud measures.
- Ensure harmonised and compliant administrative, procurement, and financial procedures.
- Ensure that internal review and exchange meetings are regularly conducted and documented

**4. Finance Management & Compliance**

- Oversee financial planning, budget management, expenditure monitoring, and forecasting.
- Ensure compliance with AN’s authority matrix, procurement rules, and donor financial regulations.
- Signatory of all contracts (i.e. employment, consultancies, contractors, PAs, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with AN, donor and governmental rules and regulations
- Support internal and external audits and ensure follow-up on audit recommendations.
- Monitor financial risks and advise HQ on sustainability and growth.

**5. Security Management**

- In collaboration with the HQ Global Security Advisor and the Security Focal Point, monitor the programme implementation environment, including security, political, development and personnel issues that may affect implementation of the projects, and provide updates to the Desk Manager (DM) and Team Lead Africa in a timely manner
- Ensure all security protocols, SOPs, contingency plans, and risk mitigation measures are up to date.
- Provide regular security briefings to HQ and ensure staff receive security training.
- Ensure appropriate response to political, operational, or natural crisis developments affecting programming.

**6. Operations, Logistics**

- Oversee logistics, procurement, fleet, warehousing, and asset management.
- Ensure transparent and efficient procurement in line with AN and donor standards.
- Oversee office registrations, legal compliance, and adherence to national regulations.
- Manage risk, prevent fraud, and safeguard AN’s assets and reputation.

**7. Partnership Management & Localisation**

- Strengthen partnerships with national NGOs, community-based organisations, and technical institutions.
- Lead due diligence processes, capacity-strengthening plans, and partnership compliance.
- Promote equitable partnerships and localisation principles.
- Where appropriate and feasible visit to project sites for monitoring purposes.

**8. Safeguarding (PSEA & Child Protection)**

- Ensure that safeguarding and PSEA policies are implemented across all offices and programmes.
- Deliver and monitor mandatory staff training on PSEA and child protection.
- Ensure there are confidential, safe, and efficient reporting mechanisms for safeguarding concerns.
- Promote a culture of protection, equality, and accountability among the staff and affected populations.

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree (or BA with substantial experience): in development and cooperation, humanitarian and international affairs, management of non-profits or other relevant fields.
- Minimum **5 years’ experience** in senior management roles in humanitarian or development settings.
- Strong experience in programme management, strategic leadership, HR oversight, and financial management.
- Firm understanding of donor compliance, reporting and proposal development (especially BMZ, German Federal Foreign Office, Europe Aid, ECHO)
- A broad understanding of the roles and responsibilities of international cooperation and humanitarian architecture including key actors, standards, clusters, donors
- Strong understanding of and experience in security management in complex environments.
- Excellent team leader skills, guidance and support to the team
- Fluency in written and spoken French; Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Bambara, is a strong asset.
- Sensitivity to cultural differences and the ability to work in a culturally diverse team
- High degree of intercultural competences and conflict-sensitivity, strong sense of integrity and sensitivity towards the needs of vulnerable groups
- Having the ability to work under pressure and changing project environment.
- Experience in West Africa, particularly Mali.
- Commitment to gender equality, safeguarding, and localisation.

Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.

We would like to encourage people with similar CVs, and especially women to apply.

**We offer:**

- Competitive salary
- 30 days of annual leave + public holidays
- Professional development and training
- An inclusive, respectful, and diversity-positive organisational culture

**Attention:** this is not a family duty station

However, arche nova is a family-friendly employer and allows for flexibility regarding children or care work.

AN is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment without attention to race, age, ability, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other factor. At AN we celebrate diversity and appreciate our employees for the people they are and their unique skills, backgrounds, and perspectives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply!

**Deadline for application:** 15.11.2026

jobs.title: Head of Programme
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Head of Programme.

Danish Refugee Council is a leading protection agency pursuing our mandate to protect and promote durable solutions to displacement-affected populations based on humanitarian principles. In East Africa and the Great Lakes, DRC has operational presence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

In the DR Congo, DRC has been involved in humanitarian aid since 2009. Initially working in Province Orientale, DRC gradually extended its reach to North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The sectors of intervention for DRC in the country are provision of Emergency Response, Protection (including GBV and child protection), Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH. DRC is currently responding to the Ebola outbreak as this is unfolding in Ituri province where DRC has a longstanding presence.

**About the job**

Provide strategic direction, leadership and oversight of DRC’s country programme, ensuring coherent strategy, high programme quality, effective departmental management and sustainable funding. Lead country-level programme development and support accountable implementation through Area Managers and Project Managers. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the HoP oversees a multi-sector portfolio spanning emergency response, early recovery and resilience in eastern DR Congo, including consortia led by DRC, and works closely with the Head of Support Services and the Head of Safety to balance programme excellence, cost efficiency and safety.

**Main Responsibilities**

*Programme Strategy & Development*

- Lead and periodically review the Country Programme Plan, Theory of Change and sector/geographic priorities; translate strategy into clear departmental workplans.
- Coordinate an integrated, multi-sector approach across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; ensure the centrality of protection, safe programming, access and adherence to humanitarian principles; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Promote cash and market-based programming (including multi-purpose and emergency cash) and link emergency response with early recovery and durable solutions.
- Drive innovative programme design with the SMT, in line with DRC global and regional strategies.

*Programme Coordination*

- Lead the Programme Department; clarify reporting lines, roles, delegation, staffing and cost structure with the Head of Support Services.
- In collaboration with the Area Manager, maintain consolidated priorities, deliverables and follow-up
- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Oversee portfolio quality and delivery; work with Area Managers on operational feasibility, project start-up/closure and timely escalation of implementation risks.
- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Coordinate programme approaches across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Maintain programme risks and mitigation actions in the Country Office Risk Register; analyze options and take timely decisions within delegatedauthority.
- Provide concise, decision-oriented updates to SMT and coordinate priorities with Area Offices, Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Safety, Regional Hub and HQ.
- Ensure effective and transparent planning and use of financial resources (budget follow-up, burn rates) in compliance with DRC and donor rules; keep programme staff updated on donor regulations.

*Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)*

- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Ensure monitoring systems produce quality evidence that is used for programme adjustment and accountability to affect populations; document and share lessons learned and good practices internally and externally.

*Fundraising, Proposal Development & Reporting*

- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Oversee timely, quality concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports with Grants, Finance and field teams, in line with DRC and donor requirements.

*Donor Liaison, Partnerships & Representation*

- Represent DRC with donors, consortia, coordination bodies, authorities and local partners; advance localization and coherent programme positioning; ensure effective governance of DRC-led consortia.
- Deputize for the Country Director when delegated.

*Advocacy & Communication*

- With the CD and the Advocacy & Communications function, develop evidence-based advocacy messages grounded in programme data, promoting the protection and rights of displaced and conflict-affected populations.
- Support the development and review of external communication materials (case studies, success stories, donor visibility).

*People management*

- Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
- Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
- Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team
- Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
- Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
- Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.

*Technical supervision – Field Offices*

- Providing technical direction, guidance, and where mandated, instructions to ensure compliance with DRC policies, standards, and strategies.
- Supporting managers and technical staff through regular communication, capacity building, and promotion of best practices.
- Support managers with assessing the technical skills and performance of most senior technical staff in the Country/Field offices.
- Escalating and, where authorized, addressing issues of non-compliance or poor performance in line with the technical supervision mandate.
- Participating in the recruitment of most senior technical staff in Country/Field offices.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to At least 7 years in humanitarian/development programming, including at least 4 years managing staff and senior country-level programme responsibilities. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Proven strategic planning, Theory of Change, multi-sector programme management, institutional fundraising, proposal and budget development experience.
- Master’s degree in international development, Humanitarian Affairs, Political Science, Economics, Social Sciences or related discipline.
- Strong management, delegation, prioritisation, decision-making, PCM, grants/MEAL oversight, donor compliance, partnership and communication skills; experience in complex contexts.
- Sound knowledge of displacement issues and related international standards; knowledge of the DR Congo / Great Lakes context is a strong asset.
- Proven experience of external representation with donors, authorities and clusters, and of managing programmes within consortia.
- Experience of leading change processes (scale-up/scale-down) and of working in insecure, rapidly changing environments.
- English – full professional proficiency.
- French – professional proficiency highly desirablefull professional proficiency required

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: *1 Year*

Band: *Management E*

Work location: *Bunia*

Designation of Duty Station: *Non-Accompanied*

Start date: *2nd January 2027*

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of , please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/) for more details.

jobs.title: Business and Financial Analysis Lead
jobs.description:
The **Business and Financial Analysis Lead** will provide technical leadership in assessing the viability, effectiveness, sustainability, and scalability of inclusive agricultural business models and financial interventions. The role will lead the analysis of agribusiness performance, smallholder sourcing systems, financial service delivery, investment leverage, and market development outcomes. The specialist will generate robust evidence on commercial performance, financial sustainability, and developmental impact to inform strategic decision-making, learning, and future investment programming. The position will also contribute to evaluating how market actors, financial institutions, and agricultural enterprises create value for smallholder farmers while strengthening resilient and inclusive market systems.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead the assessment of the commercial viability, efficiency, and sustainability of smallholder sourcing and aggregation models.
- Analyze business performance indicators, including procurement costs, margins, productivity, quality improvements, supply reliability, and operational efficiency.
- Assess the financial sustainability and profitability of investments made by agribusinesses and other market actors.
- Conduct financial and portfolio analysis of lending mechanisms, risk-sharing facilities, and agricultural finance products supporting farmers, cooperatives, and enterprises.
- Evaluate the accessibility, utilization, and additionality of financial services and their influence on business growth and farmer participation.
- Analyze market system changes, including domestic sourcing, import substitution, market linkages, private sector engagement, value addition, and financial inclusion.
- Lead quantitative and qualitative analyses of business and financial performance data collected throughout the evaluation.
- Contribute to the design of methodologies, analytical frameworks, data collection tools, and performance indicators related to business and financial outcomes.
- Develop analytical reports, technical briefs, presentations, and evidence products that communicate findings to diverse stakeholders.

**Required Qualifications**

- Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Agricultural Economics, Agribusiness, Business Administration, Development Economics, or a related field.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in financial analysis, investment assessment, agribusiness development, market systems, or private sector development.
- Demonstrated experience evaluating business models, value chains, agricultural enterprises, and market-based development interventions.
- Strong expertise in financial modeling, investment analysis, profitability assessment, and business case evaluation.
- Experience assessing agricultural finance programs, blended finance mechanisms, guarantee schemes, credit facilities, or impact investment initiatives.
- Proven experience analyzing financial institutions, lending portfolios, and investment performance.
- Experience working with private sector actors, financial institutions, investors, donor-funded programs, and development partners.
- Fluency in written and spoken English; additional local language skills are an asset.

jobs.title: Finance Manager Mali
jobs.description:
**Contexte**

Depuis 2012, le Mali fait face à une crise humanitaire complexe marquée par une dégradation progressive de l’environnement sécuritaire dans plusieurs régions du pays. Au cours des dernières années, les incidents sécuritaires et les tensions communautaires se sont étendus à de nouvelles zones, y compris dans certaines régions du sud, accentuant les vulnérabilités des populations et compliquant davantage l'accès aux services essentiels. Cette situation continue d'avoir des répercussions significatives sur les conditions de vie des communautés et sur les besoins humanitaires à travers le pays.

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés travaille au Mali depuis 2013. L'organisation dispose d'un bureau de coordination à Bamako, et de bureaux de terrain situés à Mopti , Ségou, Tombouctou, Gao et Ménaka.

Pour répondre aux besoins des populations affctées par les conflits, les déplacements et les aléas climatiques, le NRC met en œuvre des programmes danes les domaines suivants : éducation, abris/WASH, mécanismes de réponse rapide (MRR), Information, Conseil et Assistance juridique (ICLA), moyens de subsistance et sécurité alimentaire, médiation humanitaire et protection contre la violence.

**Ce que nous cherchons:**

NRC est à la recherche d'un Finance Manager expérimenté et dévoué. Le titulaire du poste contribuera activement à la gestion des financements multiples et diverses pour la mission NRC au Mali. Il/elle sera responsable de la mise en place des systèmes et outils de finance de NRC, ainsi que de la formation rigoureuse et compréhensive du personnel des finances et du programme.

Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) sera un(e) travailleur(euse) humanitaire passionné(e) et engagé(e) avec 3 ans d'expérience minimum dans un poste de gestionnaire des finances ou directeur financier, dans un contexte humanitaire ou de relèvement (post-crise). NRC est particulièrement à la recherche d’un(e) responsable des finances ayant la force et la vision nécessaires pour soutenir des équipes nouvelles, composées d’un personnel hautement professionnel dans tous les départements /unités du bureau pays. Un penseur stratégique, un connecteur, avec de solides compétences en gestion financière et une personne ayant une solide compréhension du contexte. Les candidats ayant une compréhension approfondie et une expérience de travail avec les systèmes et procédures financiers sont particulièrement encouragés à postuler. Une expérience de l'audit, de la gestion des risques et de la budgétisation est essentielle

**Ce que vous ferez:**

1. Superviser la mise en œuvre de toutes les politiques, procédures, stratégies et initiatives liées aux finances en coordination avec l'équipe des finances des bureaux de pays et de zone pour assurer le succès, la cohérence et la conformité.
2. Responsabilité de la direction hiérarchique pour le personnel hiérarchique direct et responsabilité de la supervision technique pour le personnel des finances dans les bureaux de zone, sur la base de la supervision technique de NRC. Lignes directrices. Cela comprend :
- Processus de gestion de la performance : fixer des objectifs clairs alignés sur les priorités stratégiques, suivre et soutenir la réalisation du personnel.
- Planification de la main-d'œuvre, recrutement, intégration et perfectionnement du personnel, et soutien au devoir de diligence.
3. Élaborer et tenir à jour les documents, procédures, directives et outils financiers des pays, y compris la stratégie, en veillant à la cohérence dans l'ensemble du programme national et conformément aux normes organisationnelles.
4. Maintenir le contrôle budgétaire global du pays et surveiller les flux de trésorerie.
5. S'assurer que la budgétisation, la comptabilité, les procédures de fin d'année et les autres processus financiers se déroulent conformément au Manuel financier, aux politiques du NRC et aux exigences des donateurs et des auditeurs.
6. Former et développer les capacités du personnel et des partenaires du NRC en matière de responsabilités financières et budgétaires.
7. Assurer une mise en œuvre correcte de la politique de lutte contre la corruption dans toutes les opérations et activités financières.

**Compétences professionnelles:**

- Minimum de 10 années d’expérience, dont trois années dans un poste de direction financière avec des responsabilités de gestion dans un contexte humanitaire.
- Master dans un domaine pertinent.

***Compétences, connaissances et expérience liées au contexte***

- Une expérience antérieure dans la région et/ou la zone d'opérations est préférable.
- Maîtrise professionnelle du français ET de l'anglais, tant à l'écrit qu'à l'oral.
- Expériences de rapportage et d’audit avec les bailleurs de fonds humanitaires.
- Expérience de la gestion des risques avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Gestion d'un environnement non sécurisé
- Planification et obtention de résultats
- Analyse des risques
- Communiquer avec impact et respect
- Faire face au changement

***Compétences du profil de leadership***

- Établir des relations significatives
- Responsabiliser l’équipe
- Obtenir des résultats
- Agir avec intégrité

Veuillez trouver la [JD \_Finance Manager Mali.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCn3foZkHf4QZGXoCcL6ESKAWsaCjX-ExOyF33ad5qYin8?e=uRaReB)

**Ce que nous offrons:**

- Contrat: CDD 12Mois Renouvelable
- NRC echelle nationale/international : Grade 9
- Lieu: Mali, Bamako
- Une opportunité d’associer votre carrière à une cause impérieuse
- Une chance de rencontrer et de travailler avec des personnes qui sont les meilleures dans leur domaine

[Apprenez sur les avantages de travailler avec NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

**Informations importantes sur le processus de candidature:**

- Pour postuler en tant que candidat interne, connectez-vous avec votre adresse électronique officielle ou cliquez sur Opportunity MarketPlace.
- Lors de la création de votre profil, indiquez votre nom complet tel qu'indiqué sur votre passeport.

jobs.title: Stagiaire Juriste : Droit international humanitaire, Droit pénal national et/ou international, Médico-légal F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission du/ de la stagiaire Support juridique est d'apporter un soutien aux opérations humanitaires à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre les activités de MSF, spécifiquement associées aux pôles thématiques DIH et Médico-Légal.

Le Département Juridique Intersectionnel de MSF est composé de conseillers et managers juridiques sous une Direction unique qui avise les différents centres opérationnels de MSF de manière harmonisée et mutualisée. Il est constitué de pôles thématiques (1. DIH, 2. Médico-Légal, 3. RH & Duty of care 4. Cadre légal et administratif 5. Gouvernance 6. Innovation, recherche médicale et protection des données).

Le service juridique recherche un·e : Stagiaire Juriste - Droit international humanitaire, Droit pénal national et/ou international, Médico-légal

Le Département Juridique de MSF apporte conseil et support juridique aux équipes de Médecins Sans Frontières aussi bien sur le terrain qu’aux sièges.

Au sein du département juridique vous serez rattaché.e aux pôles thématiques 1 et 2.

**Activités principales**

**En support des opérations humanitaires, et à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre les activités de MSF :**

- Recherches juridiques variées en droit international humanitaire ainsi que sous différentes législations nationales (médico-légales, santé sexuelle et reproductive, droit des patients et l'éthique médical, droit pénal, état d’urgence…) ;
- Rédaction de notes, d’outils et de guidelines ;
- Facilitation de l’organisation de réunions et de leur suivi (CR, suivi des points d’action…) au sein des Unités 1 et 2, ainsi qu’en interaction avec les autres unités du département ;
- Archivage des dossiers médico-légaux confidentiels.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation/Expérience :**

- Stage PPI EFB / Titulaire d’un Master 2 / Ecole de droit de Science Po / Autre profil équivalent.
- Droit international humanitaire, droit pénal national et/ou international, ou droit de la santé.
- Expérience en ONG, contentieux pénal, cabinet d’avocat ou un service juridique couvrant les thématiques des Unités 1 ou 2, serait un atout.

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Rigueur rédactionnelle,
- Capacité de problématisation et de synthèse,
- Intérêt pour les activités humanitaires et associatives de MSF,
- Ouverture d’esprit,
- Capacité d’adaptation et travail en équipe.

**Langues :**

- Très bon niveau d’anglais et de français, notamment à l’écrit (50% du travail en anglais).

**Statut et conditions :** Stage de 6 mois, avec **convention de stage obligatoire.**

Basé à Paris 19ème. Le montant de la gratification est compris entre 4,35€ et 7,70€ brut par heure en fonction du niveau d’études.1 ticket restaurant est attribué par jour travaillé, d’une valeur faciale de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). 2 jours de repos indemnisés par mois. Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

jobs.description:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL · UK NAMED COMMUNITY SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME

**Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom**

*London area-based (hybrid) · Full-time*

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom to join Pathways International’s powerful global team at a formative moment for the UK’s new named community sponsorship programme.

This is a broad, versatile role spanning programme and partnership delivery and policy. You will plan and deliver the projects and partnerships that build the named community sponsorship ecosystem, while also helping shape policy development and implementation and keeping the programme informed by wider migration developments. The balance between policy and delivery will flex with the needs of the programme and the shape of the UK team.

Reporting to Hannah Gregory, Global Director Knowledge and Sponsorship, and working closely with Pathways International’s UK and global teams, you will help shape and sustain the development of named community sponsorship in the UK.

**Responsibilities**

**Policy, research and the migration landscape**

- Contributing to the development of the UK named community sponsorship policy framework, supporting the design and development of the framework post-launch, including sponsored labour and education routes, in coordination with colleagues and partners.
- Building and maintaining an understanding of the national, devolved, regional and local landscape relevant to sponsorship, and drawing out its implications for the programme.
- Maintaining an overview of wider migration developments in the UK and globally, and advising on their relevance for named community sponsorship.
- Researching, analysing and drafting high-quality briefings, policy documents and other written materials for senior stakeholders.

**Programme delivery, relationships and representation**

- Planning, delivering and coordinating projects across the UK named community sponsorship portfolio, including organising events and meetings, developing resources, materials and tools and supporting monitoring, reporting and learning.
- Building and maintaining relationships across government, civil society, local partners and funders, and communities across the UK, and connecting delivery partners to training, mentoring and resources, including via Pathways International’s global networks and UK partners.
- Supporting the multi-stakeholder working group, engaging government and other policy stakeholders (including preparing for and following up on meetings and events), and representing the programme externally.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a versatile person who can move comfortably between programme and partnership delivery and policy thinking, and who thrives on a varied portfolio in a fast-paced environment. You combine professionalism and maturity with the warmth and versatility to build rapport quickly across very different audiences.

We particularly encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement or migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Skills and experience required**

- At least 8 years of relevant work experience spanning programme or project delivery and policy, research or analysis, including working in or closely with government.
- A proven understanding of one or more relevant fields, such as forced displacement, refugee protection, community sponsorship, global migration or migration policy.
- Strong policy and analytical skills, with excellent written and verbal communication in English and the ability to produce high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders, with keen attention to detail.
- A confident, approachable relationship-builder who can work with and convene a wide range of UK stakeholders — government, civil society, delivery partners and communities — collaborate effectively with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages, and bring the judgement to represent the programme in senior meetings.
- Excellent project-management and organisational skills, comfortable coordinating meetings, events and projects, prioritising across competing demands, and getting stuck into the practical details when needed.
- Able to thrive on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently showing professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility.
- A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g. public policy, public affairs, political science, international development). Education and work experience equivalencies will be considered.
- Comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using AI tools, Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.

**Location**

This is a London area-based hybrid-working role with the ability to travel within the UK on a regular basis as needed and access available to shared office space. Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in the UK. Maintaining such legal right to work is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

One-year term (renewable)

**How to apply**

Please submit a cover letter, a CV, and a short, unedited writing sample of no more than five pages (in English) through through Pathways International’s BambooHR portal at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61) by Friday, November 20th at 11:59 pm EST to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.
