jobs.title: Appel à candidature pour le poste de Directeur (trice) National(e)
jobs.description:
**Appel à candidature pour le poste de Directeur (trice) National(e) basé (e) à Abidjan**

**A propos de l’Organisation**

Présente en Côte d’Ivoire depuis 1971, l’Association Nationale SOS Villages d’Enfants en Côte d’Ivoire est une Organisation nationale de développement social qui œuvre pour la satisfaction des besoins et la protection des droits des enfants vulnérables. A ce jour, SOS Villages d'Enfants en Côte d'Ivoire dispose de trois villages (Abobo, Aboisso et Yamoussoukro) et intervient au NORD dans le Poro et Tchologo à travers un financement de SOS Villages d’enfants Norvège.

Pour la coordination des interventions, la gestion des équipes et la gestion des partenariats stratégiques et la représentation, l’Association Nationale SOS Villages d’Enfants en Côte d’Ivoire recrute un(e) Directeur(trice) National(e)

**Mission de la position:**

Sous l’autorité du Président du Conseil d’administration, le / la directeur (trice) national(e ) dirige, gère et développe l'Association Nationale (AN) en tant que chef de l'exécutif. Il/elle veille à la mise en œuvre efficace des programmes et des services de qualité aux enfants et aux jeunes, aux familles et aux communautés, dans le cadre de la vision, de la mission, des valeurs et de la stratégie de l'organisation internationale SOS Villages d'Enfants. En recherchant des subventions et des financements gouvernementaux, des subventions internationales/nationales ainsi qu'en collectant des fonds, il/elle maximise l'autosuffisance financière de l'association nationale (et la capacité à soutenir financièrement d'autres associations nationales) en fonction du potentiel du pays.

**Objectifs généraux du poste :**

- Mettre en œuvre la stratégie et les décisions des organes de gouvernances notamment le Conseil d’administration
- Diriger les processus de planification stratégique afin de garantir la durabilité et la pertinence du travail de l'AN.
- Assurer l'efficacité opérationnelle de tous les programmes et garantir la qualité de la prise en charge des enfants conformément aux normes définies par l'organisation.
- Assurer la mise en œuvre des principes de protection de l'enfance au sein de l'AN.
- Assurer une gestion efficace et durable des ressources financières et autres de l'AN
- Assurer la gestion des risques et la continuité des activités de l’AN
- Renforcer les capacités humaines de l'association nationale afin d'assurer sa croissance et sa stabilité à long terme.
- Assurer un enracinement local solide en promouvant l'intégration locale de l'association et en la faisant reconnaître à tous les niveaux dans le pays. Renforcer l'affiliation à la Fédération internationale en participant et en contribuant aux processus internationaux.
- Promouvoir et gérer une image appropriée de l'organisation, tant en interne qu'en externe, en utilisant les valeurs et les normes de SOS Villages d'Enfants comme base pour façonner la marque.
- Veiller à la mise en œuvre des normes internationales de SOS Villages d'Enfants.

**Principaux clients** :

- Conseil d'administration (ou administrateurs)
- Équipe de Management National
- Directeur de l’équipe IDS siège
- Points focaux des Associations ou Fondations partenaires
- Partenaires centraux et régionaux de l’Etat
- Parties prenantes externes de la société civile nationale et internationale

**Domaines de performance clés et principales responsabilités** :

**Planification stratégique**

- Facilite le processus de planification stratégique sous la direction du conseil d'administration (ou guidé par le conseil d'administration), en impliquant l'équipe de gestion nationale et d'autres membres clés du personnel dans l'identification des domaines prioritaires et la définition des objectifs.
- Communique et suis les plans pour garantir une mise en œuvre efficace des projets
- Présente les plans, les rapports et les propositions lors des réunions du conseil d'administration. Veille, en coopération avec le président, à la légalité de l'organisation nationale, dans le respect de la législation nationale applicable.
- Veille à ce que les décisions du conseil d'administration se traduisent par des actions claires.

**Développement de la marque**

- Applique le concept de développement de la marque convenu au niveau international dans la stratégie, la planification et la mise en œuvre au niveau national.

**Gestion des ressources humaines et développement de l'organisation**

- Veille à ce que les bonnes personnes soient employées aux bons postes afin que les collaborateurs et les partenaires extérieurs soient toujours traités avec le professionnalisme voulu et conformément aux principes de la culture organisationnelle.
- Veille à la mise en place d'un système efficace de gestion des performances et de développement des ressources humaines qui garantisse le développement des collaborateurs et l'identification des talents. Il/elle encourage la responsabilisation à tous les niveaux de l'association nationale.
- Dirige et gère l'équipe nationale,
- Assure le fonctionnement efficace du bureau national.

**Elaboration, gestion et suivi des programmes**

- Veille à ce que les ressources soient concentrées sur la mise en œuvre de programmes et de services adaptés et efficaces.
- Veille à l'examen et à l'évaluation des programmes afin de s'assurer que les plans et les politiques convenus sont mis en œuvre et fournit un renforcement des capacités et un soutien technique si nécessaire.
- Promeut l'interaction et l'échange d'expériences pertinentes entre les programmes.
- Vise l’atteinte de standards de haut niveau pour les projets et programmes.

**Finances et gestion des fonds**

- Assure la planification et la budgétisation
- Met en œuvre et surveille le système de contrôle interne, examine les chiffres clés et les rapports financiers
- Veille à la réalisation de l'état financier annuel et du rapport d'audit externe.
- S’assure de la conformité dans la gestion des ressources.
- S’assure de la gestion des risques et de la continuité des activités.

**Recherche de fonds et relations publiques**

- Promeut la stabilité à long terme et l'autosuffisance financière en recherchant le soutien de sources gouvernementales et privées dans le but de maximiser le potentiel de collecte de fonds.
- Soutient l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies durables de collecte de fonds et de demandes de subventions.
- Soutient les activités de relations publiques/marketing selon les besoins et veille à ce que l'image de l'organisation soit appropriée.
- S’assure de la bonne mise en œuvre de toutes les initiatives de collecte de fonds

**Création** **de partenariats, plaidoyer et coopération avec les parties prenantes externes**

- Établit des relations solides avec les autorités gouvernementales compétentes, assure une représentation appropriée des points de vue de l'organisation et recherche la reconnaissance et le soutien du gouvernement pour le travail de SOS Villages d'Enfants.
- Etablit des partenariats avec des organisations non gouvernementales qui défendent les droits des enfants
- Poursuit des objectifs de plaidoyer dans les forums de protection de l'enfance et en partenariat avec d'autres ONG qui s'unissent pour donner vie à notre mission en faveur des enfants et des jeunes en situation de vulnérabilité.

**Coopération et rapports**

- Entretient des relations professionnelles et une coopération étroite avec le bureau des services IDS qu'avec d'autres unités du bureau international ;
- Fournit des rapports spécifiques aux parties prenantes et donne suite aux accords.
- Représente l'organisation auprès des autorités gouvernementales et d'autres parties prenantes externes.

**Sauvegarde de l'enfant (CS)**

- Responsable de la mise en œuvre et de la gestion de la politique de sauvegarde au sein de l’Association Nationale
- Veille à ce que tous les collaborateurs, partenaires et associés signent toutes les politiques de l’organisation
- Rapporte aux autorités compétentes toute préoccupation de l'organisation concernant la sauvegarde des enfants dans le cadre de ses programmes ;
- Veille à ce que la sauvegarde des enfants ne soit pas compromise par des activités dans le domaine de la collecte de fonds ou des relations avec les donateurs.
- S’assure que tous les partenaires/donateurs sont informés de la politique de la sauvegarde de l’enfant de l’organisation et sont invités à la respecter.
- Est responsable de la commande d'enquêtes internes en cas de besoin
- Veille à ce que les incidents de la sauvegarde de l’enfant qui répondent aux critères des incidents graves soient signalés dans les délais au bureau international.

**Qualification et Compétences requises**

- Le ou la candidat (e) doit avoir le niveau de BAC +5, MBA, Maitrise en Sciences sociales, économiques ou toute autre filière pertinente.
- Avoir une expérience d’au moins 10 ans dans la gestion des projets et programmes et des partenariats.
- Avoir au moins 5 ans d’expérience à un poste similaire ou de senior leadership dans une organisation humanitaire ou une institution de développement.

**Ce que nous défendons :**

SOS Villages d’Enfants Côte d’Ivoire est engagé à créer et à maintenir un environnement chaleureux et protecteur. Elle promeut ses valeurs fondamentales, prévient et traite les abus et l’exploitation des enfants. Nous condamnons fermement toutes les formes de maltraitance et d'exploitation des enfants, que ce soit au sein ou à l'extérieur de notre organisation. Nous répondons toujours à tout cas de maltraitance avérée, allégation ou tentation d’abus dans notre sphère d'influence selon sa nature. Nous veillons à ce que des mécanismes soient en place pour sensibiliser, aider à la prévention, encourager les signalements et faciliter les réponses. Ces mécanismes vont des actions de développement des ressources humaines telles que la formation et le conseil aux mesures telles que la suspension, le licenciement et l'action en justice.

jobs.title: Chief of Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch, D1
jobs.company: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.description:
This position is located in the Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch (SPPB), Humanitarian Sector Division, Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), in Geneva. OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Chief of Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch in Geneva. With delegated authority of the Humanitarian Sector Division Director, the Chief of Branch will be responsible for leading the reform of the humanitarian programme cycle and strengthening and streamlining humanitarian coordination in line with the Humanitarian Reset; the training of OCHA and IASC personnel; the documentation and sharing of best practice; shepherding interagency negotiations; spearheading cash coordination; enhancing humanitarian-development collaboration; and the provision of technical support to Humanitarian Coordinators, Humanitarian Country Teams and OCHA Country/Regional Offices. The Branch is responsible for the production of the Global Humanitarian Overview. The Chief of Branch will also oversee support from her/his teams to effectively contribute to the implementation of OCHA's Strategic Plan. The incumbent of this post reports to Director, Humanitarian Sector Division.

## **Responsibilities**

With delegated authority, the Chief of Branch will be responsible for the following duties: MANAGEMENT/REPRESENTATION: - Streamlines the functions of the Branch to ensure cohesion and 'fit-for-purpose' structures designed to effectively implement its responsibilities under the OCHA Strategic Plan and the Humanitarian Reset. - Drives change management to implement the reform of the humanitarian programme cycle and transform humanitarian coordination in line with the Humanitarian Reset’s four ‘D’s – Define, Devolve, Deliver, Defend. - Promotes localization of humanitarian action and coordination, accountability to affected people (AAP), gender, age and disability-sensitivity, and cross-cultural responsiveness. - Fosters and strengthens collaboration and consultation with all functions of OCHA HQ and Country and Regional Offices. - Provides strategic vision and leadership on each area of the humanitarian programme cycle: coordinated needs assessment, analysis and prioritization; joint strategic response planning; resource mobilization and joint response monitoring. - Guides and coordinates the establishment of a work plan for the Branch, the determination of priorities, and the allocation of resources to ensure timely delivery of agreed outputs. - Ensures regular and effective supervision of staff, particularly by leading, managing, developing and training staff. - Fosters teamwork and communication among staff, and strengthens the linkages between staff in country operations, regional offices and headquarters offices. - Undertakes or oversees the programmatic and administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Branch, including preparation of budgets, reporting on budget and programme performance, evaluation of staff performance, interviews of candidates for job openings, and evaluation of candidates. - Promotes OCHA's mandate, objectives and tools in terms of the humanitarian progamme cycle and humanitarian coordination through contacts with governments, diplomatic missions, UN entities, non-governmental organizations and the media. - Represents OCHA in the IASC in all matters related to the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration); and coordinates the development of relevant IASC policies and tools. - Leads efforts to raise awareness of the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and efforts to strengthen and reform these among Member States, Regional Organisations and other stakeholders. - Ensures close and regular engagement with the Development Coordination Office in support of humanitarian-development collaboration and guidance as well as leading OCHA's secretariat support to the Joint Steering Committee and OCHA’s work on transition. GUIDANCE AND COUNTRY SUPPORT: - Leads the development and maintenance of normative guidance, procedures and tools that enable Resident/Humanitarian Coordinators and Humanitarian Country teams, with the support of OCHA Country/Regional Offices, to effectively manage all aspects of the humanitarian programme cycle and the coordination architecture in-country, including relationships with development partners, to drive forward the Humanitarian Reset. - Facilitates the documentation and dissemination of best practice and drives innovation and reform around the humanitarian programme cycle and the coordination architecture, ensuring processes and tools evolve and are adaptable to different contexts, in line with the Humanitarian Reset, including with respect to localization and AAP. - Oversees and ensures coherence of efforts to strengthen the role of humanitarian coordination mechanisms in guiding humanitarian action. CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING: - Works with the Crisis Response Division and OCHA Heads of Country/Regional Offices to identify and fill technical support requirements through coordinated missions. - Oversees the development and implementation of a plan for providing comprehensive training to OCHA headquarters and country/regional presences on the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and using online tools and platforms to support planning and response monitoring. - Supports and complements on-going efforts by OCHA Country/Regional Offices, Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator Offices and IASC subsidiary bodies' to reach out to, partner with and build capacities within Governments, national entities, regional organisations and other stakeholders on humanitarian programme cycle components and humanitarian coordination in crisis-prone areas. CONTRIBUTION TO CORPORATE LEADERSHIP: - Contributes, as a member of OCHA's General Management Team (GMT), OCHA Management Committee and other bodies, to policy development at corporate level that enhances OCHA's overall effectiveness. - In support of the Director, Humanitarian Sector Division, OCHA Geneva, advises the ERC and other Senior Leadership Group members all issues of policy and practice related to the humanitarian programme cycle, humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and accountability to affected people. - Provides leadership and oversight to ensure Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch adherence to relevant areas of OCHA's Strategic Plan and its results framework.

jobs.title: Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead - MENAU
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Jordan and Lebanon.**

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than forty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs—improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead for MENAU is a key member of IRC’s Regional Management Team, ensuring a strategic approach to policy and advocacy engagement across the region. The role aims to influence the policies and practices of key national, regional and global decision-makers while translating the experience and expertise of IRC programmes and partners into influence at national, regional and global levels.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead provides strategic leadership and support to country programmes, while leading on policy and, advocacy and managing in partnership IRC’s communications efforts across the region. S/he leads the development of regional policy positions and ensures that MENAU advocacy products are strategically aligned, evidence-based and meet the quality and standards expected by the organisation.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead represents IRC on regional policy and advocacy platforms, helping to shape debate and ensuring the perspectives and priorities of country programmes and partner organizations are at the forefront of humanitarian and development decision-making. Working closely with global colleagues, s/he also ensures that regional realities shape the IRC's wider policy and advocacy positions.

Reporting to the MENAU Regional Vice President, with a management in partnership to Global Policy and Advocacy team, namely the Global Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, Director – Policy and Advocacy and works closely with global Policy and Advocacy, while supervising and supporting regional and country level policy, advocacy and communication staff. The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead is based in Amman or Beirut with frequent travel in the region, and as needed to New York, Washington D.C., London, Brussels, Geneva and other capitals.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Overall Strategy and Team Management:**

- In close coordination with the Regional Vice President, leads the development, alignment and implementation of policy and advocacy strategy for the region.
- In close coordination with the global Policy and Advocacy team, contributes to and supports the implementation of organizational strategies.
- Builds and maintains relationships with diverse MENAU organizations and individuals to develop networks and increase collective impact.
- Maintains overall accountability for regional and country-based policy, advocacy and communications team cohesion, product delivery and ensures all products meet the quality and standard set by the organization.

**2. Advocacy and Policy:**

- Works in close collaboration with country-level and global policy and advocacy colleagues, to develop and drive policy and advocacy products for in-country, regional and international policymakers, ensuring that field priorities and perspectives are integrated.
- Coordinates and supports the work of country-level policy and advocacy staff and ensures that country-focused information and materials are widely disseminated internally and externally.
- Supports the development of policy and advocacy material for national, regional and global use including talking points, briefing notes, position papers and advocacy reports.
- Supports IRC’s efforts to scale the most impactful programmatic interventions by crafting strategies to overcome political and policy barriers to their deployment nationally, regionally, while informing global debates.
- Provides policy review for organizational positions and materials related to key issues in MENAU.
- Represents IRC in regional advocacy, policy and coordination forums, as well as at key lobbying meetings in global capitals, the UN and where necessary.
- Provides analysis and produces content for executive and regional leadership and ensures the Regional Vice President is briefed on all relevant policy developments.

**3. Communications and Media:**

- Provide day-to-day management of the Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications, MENAU to ensure regional alignment of the regional public affairs and communications strategy.
- Support the expansion of IRC’s reach and visibility in the region, acting as an IRC spokesperson with regional and international media.
- Ensures consistent advocacy messages, calls to actions and policy asks in external communications products, including press releases, talking points, and spokesperson briefings.
- Collaborates with Deputy Director on polished and accessible external communications materials to inform key audiences and influence policy decisions.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:** Management in Partnership of the MENAU Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications and their team. Management in Partnership of the ECD Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead, as well as Management in Partnership of country-level policy and advocacy staff.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

**Internal:** Regional Vice President; MENAU Regional Management Team; MENAU Country Directors; global policy and advocacy staff and Vice President for Global Policy and Advocacy with Management in Partnership with the Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, global communication staff with close coordinate with the Director of Global Public Affairs and Communication; country and regional based staff as appropriate.

**External:** Regional and national advocacy fora, international and national NGOs, UN agencies, public and private donor agencies, national governments/authorities, regional and international media representatives.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- University Degree in Communications, International Affairs, Policy & Advocacy, Political Science, or any other relevant field. Master’s degree is preferable.
- At least ten years of increasingly responsible professional experience responding to complex humanitarian crises and/or post-conflict situations, with a track record of delivering change through highly impactful policy, advocacy and communications strategies
- A keen understanding of political complexities in the MENAU region is required; previous experience working in the Middle East is required
- Solid communications and media relations experience required
- Fluency in English and Arabic (written and spoken) is required, with demonstrated outstanding writing skills.
- Proven ability to persuade and influence diverse audiences
- Excellent analytical, presentation, communication and reporting skills
- Ability to navigate interpersonal and inter-departmental organizational dynamics to keep focus on goals and products
- Must be willing and able to travel regularly within the region and occasionally internationally
- Culturally sensitive, able and interested in working with a multi-ethnic team
- Arabic Speaking candidates from the Middle East region are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Accounting Assistant
jobs.description:
**Purpose and Objectives:**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization for cooperation in and implementation of disaster risk reduction and building climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. It was established in 1986 as a regional disaster preparedness center (DMC). ADPC has grown and expended its role to be for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) in and effective manner.

The Finance and Accounting Unit is one of the ADPC’s Program Support Service Units with interlinked responsibilities with the Human Resource and Administration Unit and Procurement Unit and solely or jointly responsible for:

- Ensure compliance with statutory, legislative, and donor requirements.
- Safeguard ADPC’s cash, resources, and financial assets through effective internal control procedures.
- Monitor the effectiveness of the key control framework to minimize the risk of fraud and irregularities across ADPC.
- Ensure the availability of accurate and timely financial information for management decision-making.
- Develop and utilize appropriate financial tools to capture, store, and analyze financial data effectively and efficiently.
- Ensure the accuracy of budgetary information by promoting accountability and ownership among budget owners and facilitating budget monitoring.
- Allocate resources based on the priorities outlined and approved in the annual work plan.
- Administer institutional and donor audits in accordance with established guidelines.

**Purpose for the Assignment:**

ADPC is seeking a Finance and Accounting Assistant under a consultant contract to support its financial operations as the organization adopts International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) from 1 January 2027. The assignment will focus on reviewing supporting documents, assisting with payment processing, preparing accounting entries, and maintaining financial records. The Assistant will help ensure timely and accurate transaction processing, contributing to the Finance Unit’s capacity to meet new accounting and reporting requirement.

**Expected Outputs:**

The Accounting Assistant will provide support throughout the assignment in reviewing financial documents, assisting with payment processing, and preparing accounting entries and supporting records. Tasks will be assigned by the supervisor according to the Finance Unit’s operational needs and accounting and reporting requirements.

This position will be based in Headquarters in Bangkok, Thailand.

Note:

*It is not the intent of this Terms of Reference to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

Under the supervision of the designated Finance supervisor, the Accounting Assistant will perform the following tasks :

**Document examination**

- Review payment and advance requests to ensure they are properly authorized, fully supported with required documentation, and in compliance with ADPC policies and procedures.
- Review liquidation of cash advance to ensure that reported expenditures are adequately supported and comply with established policies and procedures.
- Follow up with relevant staff on missing documents, discrepancies, and outstanding liquidations, and notify them by email of the completion of liquidations and the corresponding settlement amounts
- Ensure that project codes, activity codes, and account codes are accurate and consistent with the nature and purpose of each transaction
- Calculate withholding tax on payment to vendor, supplier, consultant as applicable, as per Thai Revenue Code.

**Payment Processing Support**

- Ensure that all payment requests are processed within the required deadlines.

**Accounting**

- Prepare accounting entries for review, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency with ADPC’s accounting policies
- Maintain supporting records in an orderly manner and compile transaction information for financial reporting and audit purposes

**Others**

- Perform any other related duties and responsibilities as may be assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the purpose and scope of this assignment

**Corporate Responsibilities**

- Ensure that all duties and responsibilities are carried out with a commitment to gender equality, diversity, social inclusion.
- Create a working environment at ADPC and ensure the protection and safety of all beneficiaries in accordance with ADPC’s PSEA and child protection policies.
- Contribute to environmentally sustainable practices, minimize waste, and ensure do no harm to people or the environment is observed.
- Ensure fraud is prevented, detected and dealt with promptly in their area of work. Be responsible for safeguarding resources entrusted to ADPC and for upholding and protecting its reputation.

**Working Principles:** The consultant will work in close collaboration with the Finance and Accounting Unit. The role requires adherence to accounting policies and key operational guidelines to ensure smooth workflow and compliance with ADPC policies.

**Qualifications:** The candidate should hold:

**Required Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree, preferable in accounting, finance, business or related field.
- Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply. Working/Internship experience in finance and accounting, particularly within an international non-profit or non-governmental organization, would be an advantage.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, MS Office applications, and Google Sheet. Experience in accounting software (preferable SUN systems) and database would be advantage. Knowledge on basic accounting principles and practices, familiar with international Accounting Standards would be an advantage.
- Knowledge on relevant tax laws and regulations would be an advantage.
- Attention to detail with excellent organizational skills.
- Good command of English, both written and spoken.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Ability to work in a team and across teams, in a multi-cultural environment
- Strong motivation, desire to learn; undertake new challenges
- Self-confidence, commitment and willingness to work hard
- Ensure confidentiality in all sensitive information

**Duty Station:** ADPC Bangkok office, Thailand

**Duration:** Twelve months consultancy contract January – December 2027

**Itinerary:** N/A

**Condition of payment:**

The payment will be based on a monthly basis, supplemented with a monthly timesheet submitted and approved by designated supervisor.

jobs.title: Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** will provide strategic and technical expertise in the design, development, governance, and deployment of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data systems, including databases, digital platforms, and AI-enabled solutions. Support evidence-based management and strengthen capacity across Pacific Island countries through innovative, standardised, and sustainable data systems.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Develop and maintain high-quality regional and national coastal fisheries and aquaculture databases and information systems and provide training in their use**

- Develops, maintains and updates the regional coastal fisheries (science, management and development) and aquaculture databases including training in the use of databases, data extraction and analysis
- Develops new web and mobile applications for the regional and national databases in line with country needs and the needs of the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff
- Develops and assists in maintaining national databases based on the regional databases and additional modules.
- Develops specific queries for data extraction and analysis as required by countries or the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff.
- Promotes and encourages the use of standard databases and information systems across the region for coastal fisheries and aquaculture data, and countries to providing the data they collect for back-up and storage at SPC.
- Identifies and develops linkages between the coastal fisheries and oceanic fisheries databases in collaboration with oceanic fisheries statistics and data collection section.
- Identifies ways to better use GIS and remote sensing products in relation to the analysis of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data.

**Practical assistance to members in the designing and targeting of appropriate awareness raising and educational information**

- Develops training materials on data entry, cleaning and extraction.
- Assists with developing and maintaining the website for the CFAP with the Information Unit to assist with the dissemination of information in general.
- Provides input to awareness raising and educational materials focused on coastal fisheries science and/or management or livelihoods and aquaculture

**Develop Artificial Intelligence based tools and models for data collection**

- Improves coastal fisheries and aquaculture data collection using photos and videos automatically processed by computer vision and artificial intelligence
- Develops and trains models to calibrate and reproject pictures for measurement from picture
- Develops and trains models to automate measurements of fishes and invertebrates for the various types of measurements
- Develops and trains models for species identification

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration in coastal fisheries and aquaculture**

- Develops links with other CROP agencies and NGOs in regard to database needs and design for coastal fisheries and aquaculture
- Advocates at global forums on behalf of the Pacific region sectoral interests
- Develops and promotes collaborations within the CFAP on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.
- Works closely with other sections of CFAP to ensure smooth implementation of projects.

**Administration and communication**

- Assists the CFAP Deputy Director and Section heads, to include information and database needs in the annual work plans and work plan reports for each Section, consistent with the strategic plan.
- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, and Divisional reports for CRGA.
- Produces reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity including technical reports and trip reports, and input to funding proposals, donor reports.
- Manage, develop and train direct report.
- Fills in for senior staff when they are on leave or duty travel, when required

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master’s in computer science, database development or a related field/discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ of demonstrated experience in database management, project management and software development associated with the successful implementation of medium- to large-scale web and desktop application systems.
- At least 8 years’ of demonstrated experience in the use of Microsoft products, both as a user and developer, in particular, (i) experience in software engineering, (ii) programming in client-server environments in C# with MS Visual Studio, (iii) ASP.NET Core and single page web applications with MS Visual Studio (C#, JavaScript and angularjs), (iv) database technologies (preferably SQL Server) and other database formats, (v) development of mobile application in C# (.NET MAUI).
- Demonstrated experience with (i) producing system and user manual documentation, (ii) user training and (iii) ongoing technical support for deployed applications.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills, detail orientation, and ability to multi-task.

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and negotiate with people from different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 5,012-6,169 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 723,251-890,185 (USD 6,717-8,267; EUR 6,061-7,460). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Human Rights and Social Development Division** has a vision for just, equitable and resilient Pacific societies and it aims to achieve this by advancing human rights, equality and social inclusion for all Pacific people, grounded in cultural values and principles. The work of this Division includes work previously undertaken by the Regional Rights Resource Team (RRRT) in the area of human rights and the Social Development Programme (SDP) in the areas of gender equality and social inclusion, culture and youth development.

In line with its vision, the work of the Division will encompass the following focal areas:

- **Objective 1:** Pacific institutions are strong, transparent, and responsive for upholding and promoting human rights and implementing inclusive, gender sensitive and culturally respectful development.
- **Objective 2:** Pacific Civil Society understand and can advocate for their rights and uphold cultural values.
- **Objective 3:** Pacific culture is protected, preserved, and promoted and culturally relevant and appropriate knowledge and systems are integrated across all work.
- **Objective 4:** All SPC programs and operations are grounded in people centered approaches and consider the rights and cultural values of diverse groups including women, children, youth and persons with disabilities.
- **Objective 5:** HRSD Division teams work collectively, coherently, and efficiently and to a high standard to achieve shared success for Pacific societies.

The role – **Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development** will provide technical advice, assistance and capacity building under the HRSD work programme. As the role requires working across the objectives of the HRSD work programme, the Adviser will have a matrix reporting relationship with other Team Leaders in this regard.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Provide technical assistance and support on human rights and GESI**

- Support governments and civil society organisations in Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs) to implement and deliver on human rights and GESI commitments, including through human rights mechanisms.
- Support governments and civil society organisations in PICTs to implement and deliver on climate change and human rights priorities, with a particular focus on implementing and progressing the *International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (ICJAO) on Climate Change and Human Rights.*
- Support Pacific Island Countries in the establishment and strengthening of their National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs).
- Conduct research, legal and policy analysis on key and emerging regional human rights, gender and social inclusion issues in line with PICTs’ priorities.

**Human rights and GESI capacities and skills development**

- Identify needs for development of capacities and skills for PICTs and other stakeholders.
- Develop and deliver capacity building on human rights and GESI through multiple modalities.
- Develop and deliver capacity building material on Climate Change, Environment and Human Rights.
- Support capacity strengthening needs of PICTs to engage with human rights mechanisms.

**Stakeholder engagement, networking and coordination**

- Support stakeholder engagement, networking and coordination to advance divisional objectives at national, regional and institutional levels.
- Engage in working groups, task forces and other technical committees.
- Represent SPC at national, regional and international forums as delegated by the Director.

**Project management and people management**

- Manage and report on the delivery of projects, programmes and activities.
- Collaborate with in country staff to develop implement, monitor and report against project, programmes and activities work plans and budgets.
- Manage the leave approvals, management plans and performance appraisals of Country Focal Officers (CFOs) as required.
- Collaborate with CFOs and in country focal points to develop, implement, monitor and report against CFOs’ work plans and budgets.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in development, human rights, law, gender, international relations or other relevant social science from a recognised university or equivalent work experience or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7 years of development experience in human rights, gender equality and social inclusion, and/or youth development, including at least 5 years of experience working in the Pacific.
- Proven track record in quality programming, including developing, delivering and reporting against work plans.
- Experience in developing capacity building resources and delivering sessions to diverse government and non-government audiences.
- Practical experience and understanding of the nexus between climate change, the environment and human rights, including relevant Pacific and international convenings.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/211**
- **Position Title**: Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit
- **Duty Station:** Beirut.
- **Duration:** 6 months (without exceeding 12 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 01 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 08 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a90xr5GZdIL87Ql2u97GNfjeoHI4DLsh/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a90xr5GZdIL87Ql2u97GNfjeoHI4DLsh/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

In line with the strategic objective of enhancing the transparency, efficiency, and public accessibility of judicial institutions in Lebanon, efforts are underway to establish a permanent, professionally staffed Communication and Media capacity specifically serving the Higher Judicial Council (HJC).

The Lebanese judiciary operates in a highly complex, fast-paced, and politically sensitive environment where the absence of structured institutional communication has frequently eroded public trust, compromised the authority of judicial decisions, and allowed misinformation to destabilize the perception of justice. Establishing a professional, proactive media presence is not merely an administrative addition, but a core requirement for safeguarding judicial independence, upholding procedural confidentiality, and positioning the HJC as a transparent and trusted institution.

UNDP is seeking a Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit to support the President and members of the Higher Judicial Council in managing external media relations, developing proactive communication strategies, mitigating media crises, and rolling out strategic public trust initiatives.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Rule of Law and Governance Chief Technical Advisor and in close coordination with the Higher Judicial Council and designated Spokesperson Judges, the Consultant will manage day-to-day media operations and strategic communications. All duties must be performed while strictly respecting judicial independence, procedural confidentiality, and the sensitivity of court cases.

The role is structured around four primary operational and strategic pillars:

**2.1. Strategic Support to the establishment of the Judicial Communication Unit**

- Establish and operationalize the HJC Judicial Communication Unit (structure, workflows, and coordination protocols with spokesperson judges and external media).

**2.2. Strategic Communication & Proactive Media Planning**

- Develop a general media communication approach for the HJC in line with Council priorities and key judicial milestones.
- Identify key media messages and adapt complex legal/judicial rulings into accessible, concise language for dissemination to journalists and civil society.
- Draft educational and informative media content, articles, and awareness materials that explain the functions of the judiciary and promote public legal literacy.

**2.3. Media Relations and Press Operations:**

- Serve as the primary operational focal point for media inquiries, receiving, filtering, and responding to journalists and media outlets in accordance with an established Judicial Communication Charter.
- Draft, edit, and distribute press releases, media advisories, and official explanatory statements under the direct guidance and clearance of the designated Spokesperson Judge(s) or the HJC President.
- Provide logistical, strategic, and content support for official press conferences, public briefings, and media appearances by judicial representatives.
- Review all media content prior to publication across official judicial channels and social platforms.

**2.4. Misinformation Monitoring and Internal Coordination:**

- Manage misinformation through day-to-day media scanning across national news outlets and social platforms to identify emerging false narratives regarding the judiciary.
- Draft corrective statements for approval by the relevant judicial bodies when misinformation is detected.
- Ensure seamless, daily coordination between the Communication Unit, the designated Spokesperson Judges, and the various judicial councils to ensure a unified institutional voice.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities noting that the total duration should not exceed 6 months (without exceeding 12 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The expert will work under the overall guidance of the UNDP Rule of Law Chief Technical Advisor (CTA).
- The work is expected to start upon contract signature.
- The UNDP project team will organize briefing meetings with the expert and will be responsible for providing them with necessary materials related to the assignment in a timely manner.
- The expert will rely on his/her own means of communication and transportation. Transportation and communication fees for the expert should be included in their financial offer.
- The title rights, copyrights and all other rights whatsoever nature in any material produced under the provisions of this TOR will be vested exclusively in UNDP. UNDP has full ownership of the activity and of its final product. Thus, any public mention (including through social media) about the activity should state clearly that ownership. In addition, any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated and approved by UNDP.
- In the event of any delay, the expert will inform UNDP promptly so that decisions and remedial action may be taken accordingly. Delays that would affect the flow of the collaborative work and the delivery of outputs on schedule will lead to termination of contract; and
- Should UNDP deem it necessary, it reserves the right to commission additional inputs, reviews, or revisions, as needed to ensure the quality and relevance of the work.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 6 months.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within six months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit will be based in the Justice Palace Building of Beirut.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** A Master’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Media Studies, or other related fields is required.
- **Experience:** A minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in journalism, media relations, TV/radio production, or institutional communications.
- **Language:** Fluency in Arabic.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Chief of Unit, Movement Control, P4
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting This position is located in the Strategic Multimodal Movement Operations Centre (SMMOC) within the Integrated Movement Service (IMS), Logistics Division (LD), Office of Supply Chain Management (OSCM), Department of Operational Support (DOS). The position is based in Brindisi, Italy. The Department of Operational Support (DOS) was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, Offices Away from Headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. The Office of Supply Chain Management includes the Office of the Assistant Secretary-General for Supply Chain Management, Logistics Division, Procurement Division, Uniformed Capabilities Support Division, Global Service Centre and the Enabling and Outreach Service. The Logistics Division (LD) performs a central role in the implementation of end-to-end supply chain management across the United Nations (UN) operations. The LD provides direction and advice on logistical matters, monitors and assesses the delivery of strategic transportation and support services and directs the delivery of transportation and specialist support services in the functional areas of air transport including unmanned/remotely piloted aviation, ground transport, engineering, medical and supply, inclusive of fuel, rations and general supplies and security equipment. The Integrated Movement Service (IMS) provides unified strategic oversight of multimodal movement operations. It comprises the Strategic Multimodal Movement Operations Centre (SMMOC) in Brindisi, Movement Control and Delivery Planning capacity in New York, and Forward Support Deployment Hub in Entebbe, to provide seamless service to all UN secretariat entities. As a single coordination entity, IMS delivers an integrated end-to-end approach that aligns multimodal transportation activities and enhances operational efficiency. The incumbent of the post will report to the Chief SMMOC or designated official. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Chief of Unit, Movement Control is responsible for the following duties: • Provides effective and timely execution oversight, and management and coordination of delivery activities; ensures effective and timely coordination of diverse delivery and movement requirements to and from peacekeeping missions in the field while taking into account the quantities required, delivery timelines, cost estimates, delivery locations, existing freight contracts and prioritization based on urgent requirements. Proposes, prepares, monitors and advises on the implementation of the delivery plans to ensure timely arrival of personnel and commodities to their destination; • Optimises the supply chain network and delivery modalities through the analysis of modes of transport, regional hubs, warehousing, staging areas, port management, host country agreements, customs clearance procedures and third-party suppliers; • Liaises with Police Contributing Countries (PCCs) and Troop Contributing Countries (TCCs) to coordinate movements of military and civilian personnel and Contingent Owned Equipment (COE); • Analyses inbound delivery process; identifies supply chain bottle necks and provides solutions; • Provides leadership and work direction to assigned work team, and mentors and supervises the work of new/junior officers; serves as a first-level supervisor of a small organizational entity; • Provides advice to the Strategic Support Service regarding the appropriate use of delivery terms in systems contracts; • Plans freight requirements for UN Owned Equipment (UNOE) purchased when volumes exceed Global Freight Forwarding (GFF) contract benchmarks; • Participates in consultations with representatives of the principal components on satisfying the urgent needs of field missions; • Supports the development of delivery planning policies, guidelines and procedures and reviews them periodically; • Assists in assessing human resource needs and recruits staff for the Unit, taking due account of geographical and gender balance and other institutional values; • Participates in the preparation of the programmatic/administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Unit including, assigning and monitoring performance parameters, reporting on budget/programme performance, preparation of inputs for results-based budgeting, evaluation of staff performance, interviews and evaluation of candidates for job openings. • Performs other duties as assigned. Competencies PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of diverse logistics operations and practices and supply chain management, in particular planning. Ability to develop and apply supply chain and logistics plans, policies, procedures and new programmes. Ability to provide technical and procedural advice in a broad range of supply chain and logistics areas. Knowledge of policies and guidelines pertaining to logistics operations, supply chain management and related matters. Ability to complete in-depth analyses and to formulate conclusions and recommendations. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. ACCOUNTABILITY: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. CLIENT ORIENTATION: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent degree) in business administration, public administration, supply chain, transportation or related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Certification in Dangerous Goods Transportation in accordance with the rules and regulations of the International Air Transport Association (IATA) and/or the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and/or International Maritime Organization (IMO) is required. Work Experience A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in multimodal freight transportation operations, is required. A minimum of two years of experience managing a multicultural team is required. A minimum of two years of experience in at least two modes of transport (air, sea, road, and rail), including the planning, coordination and executing of large-scale personnel and cargo movement operations at the international level is required. Experience in assessing contract proposals and managing transportation services in at least two (2) modes of transportation is required. Experience in using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems such as SAP, including supply chain modules such as the Transportation Management (TM) module or equivalent is required. Experience in handling dangerous goods cargo, including packaging and documentation is desirable Experience in military transportation and movement operations is desirable Experience working in or in support of a United Nations common system field presence (inclusive of peacekeeping operations, special political missions, agencies, funds and programmes), or other similar international organization is desirable. Experience in sourcing, cleaning and preparing data, selecting and developing visualization/metrics in transportation, procurement, and/or supply chain management is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. French is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). Required Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking English UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II Desirable Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking French UN Level I UN Level I UN Level I UN Level I Assessment Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by an informal interview. Special Notice • This position is funded by the Support Account. • This position is temporarily available for six months, with a possibility of extension. If the selected candidate is a staff member from the United Nations Secretariat, the selection will be administered as a temporary assignment. The appointment or assignment and renewal thereof are subject to the availability of the post or funds, budgetary approval or extension of the mandate. • While this temporary assignment may provide the successful applicant with an opportunity to gain new work experience, the selection for this position is for a limited period and has no bearing on the future incumbency of the post. •Subject to the funding source of the position, the eligibility for this temporary job opening may be limited to candidates based at the duty station. • This temporary job opening may be limited to "internal candidates," who have been recruited through a competitive examination administered according to staff rule 4.16 or staff selection process including the review of a central review body established according to staff rule 4.15. • The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. • Staff members of the United Nations common system organizations who will reach the mandatory age of separation or retirement within the duration of the current temporary need period are not eligible to apply. Submitting an application or selection for the current temporary job opening does not delay or increase the mandatory age of separation. • Retirees above the mandatory age of separation who wish to be considered for the current temporary job opening must indicate the reason for their last separation as "retirement." Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service. • At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application. United Nations Considerations According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. Applicants are urged to carefully follow all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira, and to refer to the Applicant Guide by clicking on “Manuals” in the “Help” tile of the inspira account-holder homepage. The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines. Applicants must provide complete and accurate information pertaining to their personal profile and qualifications according to the instructions provided in inspira to be considered for the current job opening. No amendment, addition, deletion, revision or modification shall be made to applications that have been submitted. Candidates under serious consideration for selection will be subject to reference checks to verify the information provided in the application. All external candidates recruited in accordance with section ‎2.2 (a) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment without limitation and all external candidates recruited in accordance with section 2.2. (c) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment limited to the entity are subject to an initial probationary period of one year under a fixed-term appointment. Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING).
