Background

The Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) serving as the implementing partner and UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project supports national and local governments in accelerating the transition toward sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, and people-centered urban development. The project promotes integrated urban planning, climate-smart infrastructure, sustainable mobility systems, resource-efficient urban services, enhanced urban biodiversity, and accessible green public spaces. It also strengthens institutional capacities and inclusive governance mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of citizens, communities, civil society organizations, the private sector, and vulnerable groups in urban development and decision-making processes. Through these interventions, the project contributes to creating greener, more resilient, and more inclusive cities that improve quality of life while advancing Mongolia's climate and sustainable development objectives.

The Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry (MOFALI) serving as the implementing partner and the UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by GEF, the project supports national efforts to reduce the use and release of hazardous chemicals across key economic sectors and supply chains.

The project seeks to strengthen the policy and regulatory framework for chemicals management, enhance institutional and technical capacities, improve industry practices, promote the adoption of safer and more sustainable alternatives, and increase transparency and accountability among public and private sector stakeholders. It also supports knowledge generation, awareness raising, and multi-stakeholder engagement to facilitate informed decision-making and responsible chemicals management throughout product life cycles. Through these interventions, the project contributes to reducing environmental pollution and health risks, advancing circular economy principles, and accelerating Mongolia's transition toward greener production systems and sustainable consumption patterns.

The Admin and Finance Associate will provide administrative, financial, and logistical support for the effective implementation of the GEF Funded projects of UNDP Mongolia. Under the direct supervision of the respective Project Managers and in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office operations team, the incumbent will support project budgeting, financial planning and reporting, travel and event logistics, asset and inventory management, records management, and compliance with UNDP, GEF, and national implementation modality (NIM) requirements. The Associate will ensure timely processing of financial transactions, maintain accurate project documentation, monitor expenditures against approved budgets, support project audits and reviews, and facilitate administrative coordination among implementing partners, government institutions, service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure efficient and accountable project delivery and achievement of project results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administrative and Finance Associate provides integrated operational, financial, and administrative support to the Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project and the Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project, ensuring efficient implementation, compliance, and coordination across both GEF-funded initiatives. Working closely with Project Managers, implementing partners, and the UNDP Country Office, the Associate supports financial management, administrative processes, logistics, and reporting to facilitate the timely and accountable delivery of project results.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Project Managers, the Admin and Finance Associate is responsible for project implementation support services, ensuring effective operational management of the project and transparent utilization of financial resources. The Admin and Finance Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. The Admin and Finance Associate works in close collaboration with the Project Implementing Unit (PIU) and the Country Office.

Summary of key functions:

- Financial Management and Budget Administration

- Assets Management

- Administrative Travel support

- Actively contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans to support effective project implementation

- Maintain project financial records and supporting documentation in accordance with UNDP, GEF, and Government requirements

- Process budgets, fund allocations, payments, advances, and financial transactions through Quantum and other applicable systems

- Verify the accuracy and completeness of financial documents and ensure timely resolution of financial processing issues

- Maintain effective internal controls and ensure compliance with UNDP financial rules, regulations, and procedures

- Monitor budget utilization, expenditures, cash flow, and delivery rates, and advise the NPC on variances, risks, and corrective actions

- Prepare financial forecasts, analyses, and periodic financial reports to support project planning, decision-making, and reporting requirements.

Financial Management and Budget Administration

- Monitor project financial performance and expenditures against approved GEF budgets, work plans, and results frameworks;

- Track, verify, and report co-financing contributions in accordance with GEF requirements and reporting standards;

- Coordinate with UNDP, government counterparts, implementing partners to ensure timely submission Government of Mongolia, UNDP, and GEF financial reports and supporting documentation;

- Ensure compliance with UNDP POPP, GEF, NIM, and relevant Government regulations;

- Contribute to gender-responsive budgeting and tracking of expenditures related to gender equality and social inclusion.

Assets Management:

- Ensure effective inventory and asset management in compliance with applicable Government of Mongolia, UNDP policies and procedures;

- Participate in periodic physical verification of project assets and inventories, prepare and submit inventory verification reports, and process all required asset receiving and disposal documentation;

- Manage the transfer, reassignment, and disposal of project assets in accordance with Government of Mongolia and UNDP asset management rules, regulations, and established procedures.

Administrative and Travel Support:

- Support the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans;

- Provide administrative, logistical, and travel support for project activities, including meetings, missions, training, workshops, conferences, and seminars;

- Maintain office supplies, inventory records, contract files, project documentation, and archives in accordance with established procedures;

- Prepare and monitor procurement and contractual documentation and maintain an up-to-date contract management system;

- Support the preparation of project reports and ensure proper filing, record management, and archiving of project documents;

- Facilitate coordination among projects, partners, and related initiatives to promote collaboration and synergies;

- Document, compile, and disseminate project knowledge, lessons learned, and good practices, and contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Monitor and share relevant national, regional, and international best practices to support project implementation and learning;

- Perform other administrative, operational, and financial tasks as assigned by the Project Manager to support effective project delivery.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL), Analyst [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Approche Tiers

Veuillez noter le niveau approprié indiqué dans le titre de l'avis de vacance de poste et vous assurer que vous détenez le type de contrat correspondant, tel que défini ci-dessous :

- Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/UNCDF/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026

- Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/UNCDF/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA)

- Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes

- Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes

Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé de l'offre d'emploi, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions d'éligibilité pour postuler.

II. Background and Organizational Context

Depuis 2012, le Mali est confronté à une crise multidimensionnelle marquée par la persistance de l’insécurité,

la fragilité institutionnelle et les vulnérabilités socio-économiques. Malgré les réformes engagées par les

autorités de la Transition, notamment dans le cadre de la refondation de l’État et du renforcement de la

gouvernance, les groupes armés terroristes continuent de menacer la stabilité de plusieurs régions du pays.

Les causes profondes de la crise sont liées aux déficits de gouvernance et de dialogue politique, aux inégalités

socio-économiques, aux tensions autour de l’accès aux ressources naturelles et aux effets de la criminalité

transfrontalière. Ces facteurs sont aggravés par l’extrémisme violent, le terrorisme et les conflits

communautaires dans un contexte marqué par une présence limitée de l’État dans certaines localités.

Dans ces conditions, la consolidation de la paix exige des interventions intégrées favorisant la gouvernance

inclusive, le dialogue, la cohésion sociale, le développement local et le renforcement de la résilience des

communautés afin de traiter durablement les causes structurelles des conflits.

Pour accompagner les efforts nationaux, le Mali bénéficie de l’appui du Fonds pour la consolidation de la

paix (PBF) du Secrétaire général des Nations Unies. Le PBF est le principal instrument de l’ONU pour

maintenir la paix dans les pays confrontés à des conflits violents ou en phase de relèvement. Il investit

auprès d’entités des Nations unies, de gouvernements, d’organisations régionales, de banques multilatérales,

de fonds fiduciaires nationaux à donateurs multiples ou d’organisations de la société civile.

Le PBF est présent au Mali depuis 2014 et y a investi plus de 100 millions de dollars. Actuellement, le

portefeuille compte huit (08) projets en cours pour un montant de plus de 21 millions de dollar. Deux (2)

autres initiatives sont en cours d’élaboration, pour un budget total d’environ 5 millions de dollar.

Le Secrétariat du PBF au Mali, sert de lien entre la Branche de financement pour la Paix du Bureau d’Appui

à la consolidation de la paix et au maintien de la paix à Naw York (PBPSO), la Coordonnatrice Résidente de

l’ONU, le Gouvernement, la société civile et les agences des Nations Unies sur le terrain. Son rôle est

d’identifier des opportunités pour des projets financés par le PBF, de soutenir le développement de nouvelles

initiatives et de s’assurer que le portefeuille s’aligne sur les priorités stratégiques nationales et internationales.

Le Secrétariat aide également à orienter les investissements du PBF, en coordonnant, surveillant et évaluant

les projets pour garantir leur conformité aux normes de qualité et pour éclairer les investissements futurs.

Dans ce contexte, afin d’assurer un suivi, une évaluation, une redevabilité et un apprentissage efficaces, le

PBF, en collaboration avec le PNUD, cherche à recruter un(e) spécialiste MEAL.

III. Objectif du poste

Sous la direction stratégique du Coordonnateur Résident de l’ONU et la supervision directe du Coordonnateur

du Programme PBF, l'Analyste MEAL promeut la gestion axée sur les résultats et une approche axée sur

l'efficacité du programme en dirigeant la mise en œuvre de cadres, de systèmes et d'outils de suivi et

d'évaluation innovants et efficaces. L'Analyste MEAL fournit un soutien technique sur les pratiques de MEAL

et de reporting aux équipes de programme et de projet. Le cas échéant, l'Analyste MEAL soutiendra également

l'assurance qualité du programme et le développement de systèmes pertinents. L’analyste MEAL promeut une

approche collaborative, efficace, axée sur le client, fondée sur des données probantes et la gestion de

portefeuille.

Il / elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chargés de suivi-évaluation d'autres agences de l'équipe de

pays des Nations Unies au Mali et des organisations récipiendaires de financement du PBF, les responsables

gouvernementaux et les donateurs sur le suivi de la mise en œuvre des programmes/projets et les pratiques

d'évaluation.

IV. Principales tâches et responsabilités

1.) Développer, soutenir et renforcer les systèmes de planification MEAL sensibles au genre et aux

conflits

• Promotion des normes du suivi et d’évaluation du PBF, en s’assurant de la qualité et du

contrôle, ainsi que le développement des capacités pour les agences des Nations Unies

récipiendaires ;

• Renforcement des capacités de S&E des agences récipiendaires des fonds PBF, pour

l’élaboration des projets et le suivi des résultats, y compris l’appui à l’élaboration de leurs

cadres de résultats et l’organisation des ateliers de renforcement des capacités en S&E;

2.) Assurer la coordination de la collecte et de la restitution des données de suivi, et appuyer les

activités d’évaluation

• Accompagner les équipes de projet dans la collecte et l’analyse des données de suivi.

• Planifier et organiser des missions de suivi PBF, ainsi que des missions conjointes avec le

Comité Technique et le Comité National de Pilotage.

• Appuyer la mise en œuvre du plan de suivi et d’évaluation de l’exercice d’alignement

stratégique (SRF) avec les IFIs.

• Appuyer les évaluations des projets PBF notamment la revue des TDRs et l’appui technique

pour s’assurer que ces évaluations soient conformes aux exigences du PBF.

• Appui aux exercices évaluatifs indépendants organisés par le Siège ;

3.) Assurer l’exploitation des enseignements tirés du suivi et de l’évaluation et promouvoir le partage

des bonnes pratiques

• Procéder à l’archivage des différentes ressources PBF en vue de faciliter la documentation

des bonnes pratiques

• Superviser la formulation et la diffusion des enseignements pour permettre une réorientation

des projets et encourager l’apprentissage continu.

• Concevoir et animer des activités d’apprentissage au sein de la Communauté de Pratiques et

contribuer à la communauté de pratique du PBPSO.

• Fournir des conseils stratégiques aux équipes de projet pour documenter les bonnes pratiques

des projets

4.) Garantir un reporting, une recherche et une communication efficaces

• Orientation des agences récipiendaires des fonds PBF et les partenaires de mise en œuvre sur

les exigences du PBF en suivi et évaluation des projets et assurance de qualité des rapports

semestriels et annuels des agences ;

• Fournir un appui stratégique et technique au Comité National de Pilotage et aux partenaires

d’exécution des projets pour établir des systèmes de suivi et de reporting robustes.

• Accompagner les chercheurs dans la réalisation d’études de référence, d’enquêtes de

perception, de CBM&E de cartographies des partenaires et d’autres analyses contextuelles

Le titulaire exécute d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel et jugées nécessaires au bon

fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Responsabilités de supervision et de gestion : N/A

V. Exigence

Education

• Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) dans un domaine lié tel que le suivi et

l'évaluation, les études sur la paix, la transformation des conflits, la consolidation de la paix, les relations

ou affaires internationales, les affaires humanitaires ou d'autres domaines pertinents pour la consolidation

de la paix des Nations Unies est requis ou

• Un diplôme universitaire de premier niveau (Licence) dans les domaines mentionnés ci-dessus, associé à

deux années supplémentaires d'expérience qualifiante, sera dûment pris en considération en lieu et place

du diplôme universitaire supérieur.

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

• Au moins deux (2) ans (avec un master) ou quatre (4)ans (avec une licence) d'expérience pertinente

progressive en MEAL est requise.

• Expérience avérée en gestion de programmes/projets, évaluation et suivi est requise.

• Expérience en analyse des conflits et en programmation sensible aux conflits est requise.

• Familiarité avec les procédures du PBF, y compris le suivi et l’évaluation est souhaitée.

• Expérience en gestion du cycle de projet et en développement organisationnel est souhaitée.

• Expérience en traitement des données de projets/programmes, y compris le nettoyage des données est

souhaitée.

• Une expérience avérée de la conception de systèmes de suivi et d'évaluation et de la conception de projets

de développement ou de portefeuilles intégrés est souhaitable.

• Une capacité avérée à travailler avec des données quantitatives et qualitatives et à utiliser de manière

appropriée des outils de collecte de données et d'informations qualitatives de manière innovante est requise.

• Une expérience de la conception, de la mise en œuvre et/ou de la gestion d'évaluations et/ou

d'exercices/processus de collecte de données est souhaitée.

• Une expérience de la conduite de projets de recherche appliquée et de la production de rapports sur les

résultats est souhaitable

• Expérience dans le travail avec les Nations Unies est souhaitable

• Expérience de l'utilisation d'ordinateurs, de progiciels de bureau (MS Word, Excel, etc.) et de systèmes de

gestion Web, et connaissance avancée et à jour des outils de gestion de données et des progiciels de bases

de données est requise..

Exigences linguistiques

• Maîtrise du français parlé et écrit ainsi que de la langue nationale (Bambara) est requise

Connaissance professionnelle de l'anglais souhaitée

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Compétences de base

Obtenir des résultats NIVEAU 1 : Planifie et assure le suivi de son travail, veille à la

qualité des livrables et respecte les délais.

Penser de manière innovante NIVEAU 1: Ouvert aux idées créatives et aux risques connus, c'est

un solutionneur de problèmes pragmatique qui apporte des

améliorations

Apprendre en permanence NIVEAU 1 : Reste ouvert aux idées nouvelles, partage ses

connaissances et tire les enseignements de l'expérience.

S'adapter avec agilité NIVEAU 1 : Accueille positivement le changement et ajuste son

approche face à l'incertitude.

Agir avec détermination NIVEAU 1 : Fait preuve de constance et de calme face à la

pression et poursuit les objectifs fixés.

Engagement et partenariat NIVEAU 1: Fait preuve de compassion et de compréhension envers

les autres, tisse des relations positives

Favoriser la diversité et l'inclusion NIVEAU 1 : Traite chacun avec respect et valorise les différences

dans le travail d'équipe.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Domaine thématique Nom Définition Direction et stratégie de l'entreprise

Pensée systémique: Capacité d'utiliser l'analyse objective des problèmes et le jugement pour comprendre comment des éléments interdépendants

coexistent au sein d'un processus ou d'un système global, et d'examiner comment la modification d'un élément peut avoir un impact sur d'autres parties du système.

Gestion d'entreprise: Gestion de portefeuille _Aptitude à sélectionner, hiérarchiser et contrôler les programmes et projets de l'organisation, conformément à ses objectifs

stratégiques et à ses capacités ; capacité à équilibrer la mise en œuvre d'initiatives de changement et le maintien du statu quo, tout en optimisant le rendement du capital investi

Gestion d'entreprise Suivi: Évaluation _Capacité à suivre systématiquement les résultats des stratégies, programmes et activités afin de s'assurer qu'ils sont mis en œuvre

de manière efficace ; capacité à fournir aux responsables et aux principales parties prenantes des retours d'information et des rapports réguliers sur la cohérence ou les écarts entre les activités prévues, la gestion des programmes et les résultats.

Capacité à porter un jugement indépendant sur la gestion et les résultats des stratégies, programmes et activités en se fondant sur des critères et des repères définis, tout en tenant compte des besoins et des préoccupations des clients, actuels et futurs.

Connaissance et compréhension des cadres, concepts, méthodologies, systèmes, processus et outils de suivi et d’évaluation. Capacité à porter un jugement indépendant sur la base de critères et de références définis.

Capacité à anticiper les besoins et préoccupations futurs des clients. Développement des affaires Génération de connaissances

Capacité de rechercher et de transformer l'information en connaissances utiles, pertinentes pour le contexte ou répondant à un besoin déclaré

Gestion des partenariats Gestion des relations _Capacité à s'engager avec un large éventail de partenaires publics et privés, à établir, à maintenir et/ou à renforcer les relations de travail, la confiance et la compréhension mutuelle

Programme 2030 : Engagement et efficacité

jobs.title: Communications Associate (Office Based) [Open to Internal and External applicants]
jobs.description:
Tier Decription

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026

Tier 1: Other UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed term (FTA) appointments (defined as “internal” candidates)

Tier 2: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates”

Background:

Suriname's mangrove ecosystems are among the country's most valuable natural assets. Covering nearly 86,000 hectares and accounting for approximately 0.6% of the world's mangrove area (SBB, 2023; FAO, 2023), they provide critical habitat for biodiversity, support fisheries, strengthen climate resilience, and sustain coastal livelihoods and community well-being in areas where nearly 90% of the country's population resides (ABS, 2024). They also provide a foundation for sustainable economic opportunities through tourism, research, education, and other nature-based sectors.

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994 and continues to support Suriname through its three broad programmatic areas: Democratic Governance, Social Development, Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resource Management. The three programmatic areas are interlinked, integrating nature-based solutions, justice and social services with the engagement of stakeholders that are relevant to all three programmatic areas.

UNDP in partnership with the European Union has been supporting Suriname in preservation and conservation of mangrove forests, especially through the two phases of the Global Climate Change Alliance (GCCA+) programmes; phase one: from March 2016 to August 2019 and phase 2: 2020- 2023. In 2024, UNDP and EU launched a new initiative Protection, Restoration, and Sustainable Use of Mangrove Forest (PRSUMF) project (2024 to 2027).

The PRSUMF project builds on the results achieved in strengthening mangrove protection and conservation by the GCCA+ programme. The PRSUMF project aims to support Suriname in building the resilience of target coastal communities through inclusive, gender-responsive coastal zone management, mangroves conservation, and sustainable use.

SBB. 2023. Mangrove Monitoring System: Total Mangrove Forest Area per District in Suriname (2023).

FAO. 2023. The World's Mangroves 2000-2020.

ABS. 2024. Population and Housing Census (Census 9), population distribution by district.

The project aims to achieve this objective:

a) By strengthening coordination, legal and strategic frameworks, for integrated coastal zone management, water management, coastal defense, and governance.

b) By enhancing the meaningful participation of local communities in the co-management of mangroves and Multiple Use Management Areas (MUMAs) and

c) By increasing sustainable income generation with a focus on women and youth, from mangrove-based value chains such as honey, fisheries, and mangrove ecosystem based-tourism.

Through the above approach, the project aims to support mitigation of rising sea levels impact, frequent flooding, and support the country’s population to adapt to climate change by playing a central role in mangrove protection, restoration and sustainable use through nature positive economic activities.

The project is implemented through a Project Management Unit (PMU) headed by the Project Manager. The Communications Associate will be part of the project management unit.

Scope of Work:

The incumbent will contribute to stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, visibility, and public awareness efforts that support achievement of project outputs and donor communication requirements. S/He will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, and the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Suriname. The Communications Associate will also work in close collaboration with the Technical Officer of the PRSUMF project.

The Communication Associate will design and implement specific targeted public relations (PR) and media activities highlighting project activities, results and accomplishments, including related products and articles for social media distribution.

Key functions and responsibilities of the Communication Associate include:

a. Implement and revise the Media/Communication and Visibility Plan as needed:

- Monitor implementation of and periodically update the Project Communication and Visibility Plan based on emerging communication needs, project progress, and donor requirements.

- Based on the Communication and Visibility and Communications Plan, develop a Media/Communication Action Plan and relevant budget in close collaboration with the Project Manager and supporting PMU members.

- Develop graphic designs for third party production (audiovisual and or print) in support of project branding communication and visibility, in line with UNDP and EU communication guidelines and requirements.

- Maintain and expand the network of project stakeholders and media and maintain regular contact with and provide information to media on project activities and project progress.

- Ensure and monitor visibility through the proper and correct use of logo’s during events, in photo-, audio-, and video productions and on all publication materials, equipment, materials and goods financed by the project as agreed with donors.

- Ensure that the project related information and communication materials are regularly updated on UNDP Suriname website, Facebook page, X and other social media platforms.

- Support the PRSUMF PMU in the organization and implementation of all project events and facilitate media coverage thereof.

- Advise and assist Project Manager and other project staff on aspects related to awareness and stakeholder engagement; dialogues and other stakeholder awareness activities.

b. Lead knowledge management and dissemination:

- Plan and prepare publication of articles, human interest stories, quarterly newsletters, and project results, this includes the gathering of supporting visual, audiovisual material and basic editing for publication.

- Liaise with specific sector specialists and technical resource persons for the development of folders, brochures and presentations and other communication material on climate change, mangrove conservation, sustainable use of mangroves for economic development.

- Develop and maintain a repository of communication, visibility, and knowledge products, ensuring accessibility and institutional memory for the project.

c. Support awareness and training activities of the project:

- In collaboration with project team, Support the design of behaviour-change and awareness campaigns tailored to local communities, women, youth, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholder groups.

- Assist with developing training material in general and specifically for policy makers; coastal communities, entrepreneurs and media professionals.

- Enable the production of video records of project activities and results achieved, as well as provide support for script writing; editing and formatting allowing for multiple media applications of the raw footage that will be captured.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Communications Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager of the PRSUMF project and under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office and collaborate closely with the PRSUMF project team and all other CO units.

Competencies:

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 1: Appreciates/respects differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT

Communication

• Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT

Digital Awareness and Literacy

• Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skillfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

• Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real stakeholder/ partner’s needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond stakeholder/ partner’s immediate requests. Ability to anticipate stakeholder/ partner’s upcoming needs and concerns.

DIGITAL

Social media

• Knowledge of social media and ability to advise the use of socialmedia for development outcomes.

COMMUNICATIONS

Campaign management

Public relations

COMMUNICATIONS

Writing and editing

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Minimum Education requirements & Professional Certificates

- A university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in communications, journalism, advertising, or related field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

- Supplemented by formal training, professional certification, or other verifiable credentials relevant to the assignment.

Minimum years of relevant work experience

Minimum of 7 years (with high school diploma) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant communications experience preferably at the national level for Government, NGO’s or International Organizations is required.

Required skills

Experience in office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, knowledge of graphic design, content creation, website content management, and digital communication tools is required.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Verifiable experience in branding, producing and publishing information articles, short social media targeted audio and video productions for education and awareness purposes is desired.

- Verifiable experience in social media strategy, content creation, storytelling, audience engagement, and analytics is desired.

- Verifiable experience with graphic design photography and/or videography is an asset.

jobs.title: Intern - Communications and Outreach
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities and build resilience in order to sustain development results.

UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The key 2030 Agenda principle of leaving no one behind and stamping out inequality is at the core of everything we do.

UNDP focuses on helping countries build and share solutions in three main areas:

- Sustainable development

- Democratic governance and peacebuilding

- Climate and disaster resilience

In all our activities, we encourage the protection of human rights and the empowerment of women, minorities and the poorest and most vulnerable.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Duties and Responsibilities

Working in UNDP Country Office in Thailand and under the direct supervision of the UNDP Communications and Outreach Officer (Head of Communications), the UNDP Communications Intern will work to raise the profile of UNDP Thailand in the media and among Government Agencies, (I)NGOs and other partners, manage the office’s website and general communications requirements, and provide Thai-language editing services to the office team.

The intern will assist in the following duties and responsibilities:

Communications and Outreach (50%):

- Assist in the preparation of promotional/advocacy materials for UNDP outreach, assisting in preparation of presentations, reporting, etc.

- Strengthen social media outreach; support producing new content for social media accounts, drafting messaging in both Thai and English.

- Assist with producing graphic visuals using Microsoft Powerpoint, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator or any other data visualization tools.

- Assist with media production (e.g., video) using Adobe Premiere Pro, Capcut or any other data visualization tools

Administrative (40%):

- Support communications team on technical and administrative requirements as needed (e.g., planning meetings/workshops, procurement, media)

- Provide back-up translation services when required

- Maintain an up-to-date list of contact media addresses, publication distribution lists.

- Co-manage the UNDP Thailand website to increase digital presence

- Support drafting press releases, op-eds and other text-based outreach materials; copy-writing and proofread; Thai-English translation.

- Assist UNDP staff in media outreach and information dissemination-related activities.

Other (10%):

- Support other/ad hoc activities as seen relevant and needed

Competencies

- Interest and motivation in working in an international organization;

- Good analytical skills in gathering and consolidating data and research for practical implementation;

- Outgoing and initiative-taking person with a goal oriented mind-set;

- Communicates effectively when working in teams and independently;

- Good in organizing and structuring various tasks and responsibilities;

- Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability;

- Responds positively to feedback and differing points of view;

- Consistently approaches work with energy and a positive, constructive attitude.

- Strong communication and persuasion skills

- Excellent research and analytical skills

- Results driven, able to meet targets/deadlines

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Candidates must meet one of the following educational requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree (newly graduated or in the final year of study) or pursuing a Master’s degree in related field in Communications, Journalism, Social Sciences or related field; or

- Currently in the final year of a Bachelor’s degree; or

- Currently enrolled in a Master’s degree; or

- Have graduated no longer than 1 year ago from a bachelor’s or master’s degree or equivalent studies.

Language skills:

- Fluent in English- both written and spoken in addition to native proficiency in Thai required;

- Knowledge of other UN languages is an advantage.

INTERNSHIP CONDITIONS

- UNDP will not pay interns for internship but will provide a stipend in the amount of THB 8,302.50 monthly in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP internship policy; all other expenses connected with it will be borne by me or my sponsoring Government or institution;

- UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship;

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship;

- Interns must provide proof of enrolment in health insurance plan;

- Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

- Interns are expected to work full time but flexibility is allowed for education programmes;

- Interns need to obtain financing for subsistence and make own arrangements for internship

Disclaimer

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Human Resources Assistant (1 vaga) (Home based) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

In the context of the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by member States of the United Nations (UN), UNDP has supported Member States and other stakeholders in implementing commitments – which set concrete aspirations to end hunger and disease for all people in the world; fight inequality and discrimination; promoting sustainable production and consumption systems and combating climate change.

Supporting the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs in Brazil is an essential part of UNDP’s mandate, and UNDP has been working, in partnership with the Brazilian government and other partners, on social mobilization and territorialization of the SDGs to reach areas and communities where progress has been slower and assure that “no one is left behind”. The focus is on strengthening institutional capacities and social participation mechanisms to ensure the design and implementation of inclusive public policies in a friendly and profitable business environment respecting and preserving the environment.

In aligning the organizational resources behind its strategy, the Brazil Country Office (CO) functional structure comprises three main areas, the management support functions, Programme team and Operations Team. The Operations Team is composed of Human Resources (HR), Finance, Support to Projects, and the Common Back Office (CBO), which encompasses common services for the UN House, including Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Administration and Logistics, Procurement and Travel, and HR services tailored for UN entities and Protocol. All of which are responsible for quality assurance for the implementation of UNDP policies and procedures in these operational functions.

The Operations Team plays a pivotal role in enhancing the efficacy of UN operational services and UNDP Brazil. It does so by crafting a comprehensive service delivery platform aimed at providing operational solutions to all UN entities and UNDP programs and projects. Moreover, it coordinates operational services and explores their potential expansion to the UN Common Back Office.

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Operations Manager and UN Common Back Office Manager for Brazil and direct supervision of the Human Resources Associate and the overall supervision of the Human Resources Analyst, the Human Resources Assistant (HR) generalist provides support to the HR Unit with the contract administration of personnel hired under NPSA modality, including payroll management, strategic reports, recruitment and selection process, mainly for UNDP projects and UN Agencies, and ensuring high quality, accuracy and consistency of work.

The HR Assistant generalist will support our HR department in ensuring smooth and efficient business operations. This position will have both transational and strategic responsibilities, helping to plan and administer important functions, such as recruitment & selection and administration of contracts.

The HR Assistant generalist provides support to all employees and works in line with the HR Strategy, in close collaboration with the Operations, Programme and projects’ staff in the Country Office.

The incumbent will ensure consistent service delivery with full compliance with UN/UNDP rules related to HR processes, records, regulations, policies and strategies on the National Personnel Service Agreement modality.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide support to the implementation of HR strategies related to project positions:

- Ensure full compliance of HR processes and records with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and strategies;

- Provide HR administrative support for the effective implementation of HR strategies and initiatives;

- Support in the elaboration of new SOPs and KPIs of HR Services;

- Suggests ideas for streamlining procedures to deliver optimal client service.

Provide support on Recruitment & Selection processes of project positions:

- Assist with the review of TORs and R&S documentation for completeness, consistency and compliance with applicable policies and procedures;

- Support the organization and follow-up of R&S processes, including recruitment timelines and process tracking;

- Support the publication and follow-up of vacancy announcements, ensuring accurate and timely dissemination through appropriate recruitment channels;

- Conduct initial screening of applicants against established minimum requirements and selection criteria;

- Assist with the preparation and administration of technical assessments and other recruitment tools, as applicable;

- Facilitate interview panels, including scheduling the preparation of documentation and interview materials, coordination with panel members, and preparation of minutes/reports;

- Facilitate information sharing and follow-up with Hiring Managers and relevant stakeholders throughout the R&S process;

- Maintain accurate and complete R&S records, ensuring proper filing and documentation of recruitment processes;

- Ensure accurate data management in official databases;

- Support the maintenance and update of recruitment metrics and tracking systems;

- Assist with the maintenance and management of CO rosters and talent pools, as applicable;

Implement HR services and act as Country Office (CO) Liaison with GSSC:

- Act as the primary focal point and liaison with the Global Shared Services Center (GSSC) for the end-to-end administration of project staff life-cycle transactions.

- Coordinate with GSSC to ensure timely processing of hires, contract extensions, lateral transfers, salary distribution setups, benefits, and separations.

- Track HR transactions related to positions, recruitment, benefits, earnings/deductions, retroactivity, recoveries, adjustments, and separations through ERP, in close coordination with GSSC as applicable.

- Monitor and support the collection of mandatory onboarding/offboarding documents from personnel, serving as the local administrative bridge to submit complete packages to GSSC.

- Maintain proper filing system for HR records and documents.

- Extract, input, copy and file data from various sources.

- Prepare routine correspondence, memoranda, and reports in accordance with CO needs and SOPs.

- Provide HR administrative support for the effective implementation of HR services to the UNDP project positions and partner agencies.

Supports effective communication and administration assistance for varied and inter-related services, including project operations support, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Maintenance of the filing system ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials. Use of automated filing system;

- Support the information flow in the office and dissemination of corporate and interoffice communication to personnel as required;

- Support the facilitation information sharing with Management Support and Programme and Operations Teams;

- Support the follow up of deadlines, established commitments, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to the HR Analyst;

- Draft routine correspondence, interoffice circulars, general briefing notes, documents, reports, minutes of meetings and translations when required;

- Support the administration of meetings, appointments and briefings within the HR Unit

- Assist and carry administrative tasks related to HR Unit.

Supports knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support the organization and delivery of training sessions for Operations and project staff on HR-related matters and other relevant topics;

- Contribute to knowledge sharing through HR-related guidance, knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Human Resources Associate, the Human Resources Assistant contributes to the HR Services, ensuring high quality of work, ensuring high quality on the delivery of the services needs.

Competencies

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management | Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

Abilit to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Business Development | Integration within the UN: Ability to identity, and integrate capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work; knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations.

Business Development | Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management | Customer Satisfaction/Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

HR - Compensation/remuneration | Payroll management: Knowledge of and ability to apply mechanisms and tools to collect payroll data, process payroll, and manage payroll reports.

HR - People strategy and planning | People analytics: Ability to generate and align people data with business intelligence data to inform strategic decision-making; knowledge of databases, their architecture, integration and landscape; ability to create and use data models; knowledge of visualization techniques.

Gathering and using data and information to provide insights into people issues and guide decision-making.

HR - Recruitment | Assessment and selection: Knowledge and ability to apply various candidate

assessment and selection methodologies, tools and platforms; ability to effectively align them with specific recruitment needs

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Secondary education is required.

- A University degree (bachelor´s degree) in Business Administration, Psychology, Human Resources or related areas of humanities, Communications, Social Sciences or an equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 4 years (with secondary education) or 1 year (with Bachelor´s degree) of relevant experience in Human Resources, preferably covering areas such as recruitment and selection, personnel administration, contract administration, payroll, benefits and entitlement management, among others.

Required skills

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.).

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience in Recruitment & Selection processes;

- Experience with personnel contract management and HR transactions;

- Experience in preparing reports, developing indicators, and monitoring administrative processes.

- Experience in maintaining and organizing personnel records and HR documentation.

- Experience in using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, particularly HR-related modules.

- Experience working with multiple stakeholders, including Hiring Managers, project teams, operations teams and/or shared service centres.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in Portuguese is required.

- Working knowledge in English is desirable.

Professional Certificates

- N/A

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.
